IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p19/r4.claim: The introduction notes that Ibn Jinnī’s discussion of “اهدنا صراطا مستقيما” treats tajrīd.

BURHAN:v1p305/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p305/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p305/r6.claim: Avoid remote ellipsis and complex metaphor; read اغفر لنا and اهدنا as supplication or request, not command, out of deference since command can imply superiority.
BURHAN:v1p305/r6.anchor: فعلى دعاء أو سؤال ولا نقول فعلى أمر تأدبا من جهة أن الأمر يستلزم العلو

BURHAN:v1p100/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p100/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p100/r3.claim: Citing the divine hadith dividing prayer between God and the servant, he says المستقيم is settled and the verse boundary is arranged after اهدنا, with عليهم as the first ending matching the prior rhyme.
BURHAN:v1p100/r3.anchor: لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بينى وبين عبدى نصفين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.claim: Al-Harali maps al-Fatiha's verses to the seven letters: praise, lawful and forbidden, command and prohibition, clear and ambiguous, then the corresponding petitions; its opening gathers all seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.claim: The transition from al-Fatiha's plea for the straight path to al-Baqara identifies that guidance with this Book, then describes the guided and rejected groups to teach the path to follow and the path to avoid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو

BURSEVI:v1p11/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11/r1.claim: Guide us to the straight path spells out the requested help, and supplication after completing worship is a religious practice.
BURSEVI:v1p11/r1.anchor: بيان المعونة المطلوبة كأنه قيل : كيف أعينك؟

BURSEVI:v1p11/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r2.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p11/r2.claim: The Taysir commentary reads worship as affirming divine unity, seeking help as asking aid for it, and guidance as asking steadfastness in religion.

BURSEVI:v1p11/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11/r3.claim: Steadfast guidance is among the greatest needs, sought by prophets, Pharaoh's magicians, and the Companions; outward devotion cannot guarantee one's final state.
BURSEVI:v1p11/r3.anchor: وذلك لأن الثبات على الهداية أهم الحاجات إذ هو الذي سأله الأنبياء والأولياء كما قال يوسف عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v1p11/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r4.speaker: القاضي
BURSEVI:v1p11/r4.claim: The seeker who has reached God still asks for guidance through Him, because the journey in God has no endpoint while knowledge and divine possibilities remain without limit.
BURSEVI:v1p11/r4.anchor: وفي "تفسير القاضي" إذا قاله العارف الواصل إلى الله عنى به

BURSEVI:v1p11/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r5.speaker: الفناري
BURSEVI:v1p11/r5.claim: Al-Fanari explains the continuing journey by saying that knowledge and what God can do have no limit, so the servant's longing never ends.
BURSEVI:v1p11/r5.anchor: قال المولى الفناري : ومبناه أن السير في الله غير متناه كما قال قطب المحققين

BURSEVI:v1p11/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11/r6.claim: Straight path is a metaphor for Islam and true religion, likened to a physical route because a seeker must cross distances and endure obstacles to arrive.

BURSEVI:v1p11/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11/r7.claim: Even the guided ask for the balanced middle in desire, anger, and spending, and for insight into how every thing points to God's essence, attributes, and acts.
BURSEVI:v1p11/r7.anchor: أن لا بد بعد معرفة الله تعالى والاهتداء بها من معرفة الخط المتوسط بين الإفراط والتفريط

QASHANI:1:6-7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r1.claim: The prayer asks to be kept firmly on the path of unity: the special mercy of essential knowledge, love, and guidance, traversed by prophets, martyrs, the truthful, and saints who witness God in every aspect and vanish from the transient shadow-self.
QASHANI:1:6-7/r1.anchor: ثبتنا على الهداية ومكنا بالاستقامة في طريق الوحدة التي هي طريق المنعم عليهم بالنعمة الخاصة الرحيمية

QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.claim: Muhammadan unifiers answer the calls to seek pardon and paradise, fear God and believe His messenger, and worship God without partners, thereby combining love of the essence’s beauty with the attributes’ goodness.

QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.claim: The unified path joins hope and fear, prayer for complete light, steadfastness, gardens, reward and light, seeing God’s face wherever one turns, and the best reward with increase.

QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.claim: Those who do good receive the best and an increase, completing the cited evidence that the unified servants are rewarded with both mercy and divine vision.

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r1.claim: The prayer asks God to turn hearts toward Him and direct intentions before Him, guiding from Himself to Himself without severance from what is for Him.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r1.anchor: مل بقلوبنا إليك وأقم بهممنا بين يديك وكن دليلنا منك إليك

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r2.claim: Seekers ask for guidance to paths of gnosis so they can serve steadily.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : اهدنا الصراط المستقيم أي : أرشدنا إلى طرق المعرفة

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r3.claim: Believers ask to see the path of guidance and stand firm in God's oneness.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r3.anchor: أرنا طريق هدايتك كي نستقيم معك على توحيدك فهذا دعاء المؤمنين

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r4.claim: Knowers ask for the path of intimacy so they may rejoice in nearness.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r4.anchor: أرنا طريق أنسك فنفرح ونطرب بقربك فهذا دعاء العارفين

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r5.claim: Guidance from God to God bypasses the intermediary stations and struggles.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : اهدنا بك إليك ، لنستعين ببدايتك عن وسائط المقامات والمجاهدات

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r6.claim: One seeks annihilation of one's attributes as the way to God's eternal attributes.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r6.anchor: اهدنا بفناء أوصافنا فبنا الطريق إلى أوصافك التي لم تزل

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r7.claim: The prayer asks God to remove heedlessness from the route to His pleasure.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r7.anchor: اهدنا بكشف الغفلة عنا طريق الوصول إلى رضاك

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r8.claim: It asks for direct witnessing after proof, so one may stand in love for God's will within oneself.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : اهدنا هدى العيان بعد البيان ؛ لنستقيم لك على حب إرادتك فينا

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r9.claim: It asks for guidance to true knowledge under God's own care, ending in the annihilation of self-attributes in Him.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r9.anchor: اهدنا هدى من أنت المتولي لهدايته طريق حقيقة معرفتك

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r10.claim: The requested path begins from God and ends at Him.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r10.anchor: وقيل اهدنا هدى من يكون منك مبداه ؛ حتى يكون إليك منتهاه

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r11.claim: It asks God to dispel the darkness of one's states so hidden realities may be seen steadily.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : اهدنا أي : اكشف عنا ظلمات أحوالنا لننظر في خفي غيبك

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r12.claim: One interpretation asks for self-effacement from the path, lest the traveler be trodden by it.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r12.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم بالغيبوبة عن الصراط ليلا يكون من يوطأ بالصراط

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r13.claim: The servant asks that concern with the path and steadfastness not distract from God Himself.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r13.anchor: اهدنا بك ولا تشغلنا بموارد الصراط والاستقامة عنك

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r14.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r14.claim: Guidance means being directed to use the Prophetic practices when fulfilling obligations.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r14.anchor: حكي عن أبي عثمان في قوله : اهدنا الصراط المستقيم أي : أرشدنا لاستعمال السنن

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r15.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r15.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r15.claim: He identifies the straight path with pilgrimage and the recipients of favor with prophets and saints; Jews and Christians are excluded, citing the prohibition on approaching the Sacred Mosque (9:28).
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r15.anchor: حكي عن فضيل بن عياض في قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم قال : طريق الحج

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r16.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r16.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r16.claim: The prayer seeks God's guidance against Satan, who vowed to sit on His straight path (7:16).
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r16.anchor: وقيل : اهدنا الصراط المستقيم لنستعين بهدايتك على الشيطان ،

SULAMI:v1p38#2/r17.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r17.speaker: أبو حفص النيسابوري
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r17.claim: The straight path is neediness before God; the poor person has nothing to present to the Rich but poverty.
SULAMI:v1p38#2/r17.anchor: قال : وما للفقير أن يقدم به على الغنى سوى فقره

SULAMI:v1p41/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41/r1.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SULAMI:v1p41/r1.claim: Guidance is God's help in finding the way to Him.
SULAMI:v1p41/r1.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله : أرشدنا بمعونتك الطريق إليك

SULAMI:v1p41/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p41/r2.claim: Repeatedly asking for guidance seeks an increase even for someone already guided, as God says He increases guidance for those already guided (47:17).
SULAMI:v1p41/r2.anchor: إنما سأل الله زيادة هدى ، كما قال الله تعالى : ﴿ والذين اهتدوا زادهم هدى ﴾

SULAMI:v1p41/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p41/r3.claim: The seekers ask to escape bewilderment before eternal attributes and to be guided to the qualities of servanthood, lest they be absorbed in witnessing God's eternal attributes.
SULAMI:v1p41/r3.anchor: وقال الجنيد : إن القوم إنما سألوا الهداية من الحيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel glossed 'guide us' as 'inspire us.'
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال جبريل : قل يا محمد : اهدنا يقول : الهمنا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r2.claim: Ali reports from the Prophet that the straight path is God's Book.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r2.anchor: عن الحارث قال : دخلت على علي بن أبي طالب فقال : سمعت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r3.claim: The Prophet's parable identifies the straight path as Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r3.anchor: عن نواس بن سمعان الانصاري ، عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - انه قال : ضرب الله مثلا صراطا مستقيما ، والصراط الاسلام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the straight path with the Prophet and his two successors after him; Asim says Hasan affirmed that Abu al-Aliya spoke truly and advised well.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية اهدنا الصراط المستقيم قال هو النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r5.claim: Hasan affirms Abu al-Aliya's interpretation as true counsel.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r5.anchor: فذكرنا ذلك للحسن فقال : صدق أبو العالية ونصح

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r6.claim: Mujahid says the straight path is the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله الصراط المستقيم قال : الحق

IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'guide us' means inspire us to the true religion: worshipping God alone without partner.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p30/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : اهدنا الصراط المستقيم يقول : الهمنا دينك الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.claim: He reads the sura's annexation to Fatihat al-Kitab as descriptive: it means a sura characterized as the Book's opening, with no separate title needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: إضافة السورة إلى فاتحة الكتاب من إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.claim: By contrast, Fatihat al-Kitab is a true annexation: al-Kitab here means the remainder of the Book apart from the sura called the Opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: إضافة فاتحة إلى الكتاب فإضافة حقيقية باعتبار أن المراد من الكتاب بقيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.claim: The names Umm al-Qur'an and Umm al-Kitab are established in the Sunna; “mother” denotes a thing's origin and source.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: وأما تسميتها أم القرآن وأم الكتاب فقد ثبتت في السنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says Abu Sa'id al-Khudri recited Umm al-Qur'an over a person suffering from a sting as a healing prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.anchor: أن أبا سعيد الخدري رقى ملدوغا فجعل يقرأ عليه بأم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.claim: A sound hadith calls a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an deficient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.anchor: كل صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.claim: One explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it begins and opens the Qur'an, making it like its origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.anchor: أنها مبدؤه ومفتتحه فكأنها أصله ومنشؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.claim: A second explanation is that the sura gathers the Qur'an's three main aims: praise, commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.anchor: تشتمل محتوياتها على أنواع مقاصد القرآن وهي ثلاثة أنواع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.claim: The sura's three aims together represent the Qur'an's original purposes, while its remaining material elaborates them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.anchor: فهذه هي أنواع مقاصد القرآن كله ، وغيرها تكملات لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.claim: He also supports the sura's comprehensiveness by citing the sound report that al-Ikhlas counts as a third of the Qur'an because all its wording praises God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.anchor: وقد يؤيد هذا الوجه بما ورد في الصحيح في : { قل هو الله أحد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: A third explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it contains the Qur'an's theoretical wisdom and practical rulings, including theology, prophecy, admonition, worship, transactions, morals, and law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.anchor: تشتمل معانيها على جملة معاني القرآن من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r9.claim: The request for the straight path encompasses human circumstances and their rules of worship, transactions, and manners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r9.anchor: يشمل الأحوال الإنسانية وأحكامها من عبادات ومعاملات وآداب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.claim: Taken explicitly and by implication, the sura gives a general outline of the Qur'an's aims and prompts readers to seek their fuller detail as able.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.anchor: يحصل من معاني الفاتحة تصريحا وتضمنا علم إجمالي بما حواه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.claim: Requiring al-Fatiha in every rak'ah preserves recollection of the Qur'an's purposes contained within it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.anchor: فرضت قراءة الفاتحة في كل ركعة من الصلاة حرصا على التذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.claim: A hadith in both Sahihs from Abu Hurayra has God divide prayer between Himself and the servant, answering each portion of al-Fatiha and granting the servant's request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.anchor: قسمت الصلاة نصفين بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.claim: The verse division differs by region: Medinans exclude the basmala and count “those You favored” as a verse; Meccans and Kufans include the basmala and combine that phrase with its verse; Hasan counts both separately.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.anchor: فعند أهل المدينة لا تعد البسملة آية وتعد : { أنعمت عليهم } آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: Important guidance requires preparing listeners, stirring their attention, and removing stubbornness, false assumptions, and satanic impulses that block learning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: ما بقي يخالجها العناد والبهتان ، وتخامر رشدها نزغات الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: Placed first by the Prophet's instruction, al-Fatiha trains readers in inner purification through its supplication from “You alone we worship” onward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: نبه الله تعالى قراء كتابه وفاتحي مصحفه إلى أصول هذه التزكية النفسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Asking for guidance expresses the desire to acquire sound direction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: الثالث الرغبة في التحلي بالرشد والاهتداء بما تضمنه { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.claim: As a Qur'anic preface, al-Fatiha models an Arabic literary opening that improves understanding and attentive reception.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.anchor: وهذا الأسلوب له شأن عظيم في صناعة الأدب العربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: Because the Qur'an guides people and reforms both worldly and future life, listeners must prepare by removing stubbornness, error, and low impulses before receiving its wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: فلا مناص لها قبل استقبال تلك الحكمة والنظر من الاتسام بميسم الفضيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r8.claim: Requesting guidance acknowledges a need for knowledge and distinguishes true knowledge from ideas mixed with doubt and error, preparing one to follow the better way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r8.anchor: فإن طلب الهداية اعتراف بالاحتياج إلى العلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: These aims help explain why al-Fatiha is called Umm al-Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: ولأجل هذا سميت هاته السورة أم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r1.claim: Worship and reliance bridge praise and petition; after praising God, the supplicants ask for what benefits them now and later, fitting the Fātiḥa as a preface to a book of guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r1.anchor: فكان ذلك واسطة بين الثناء وبين الطلب ، حتى إذا ظنوا بربهم الإقبال عليهم ورجوا من

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r2.claim: The sentence is the petitionary aim of the preface and is separated from the earlier declaratives; this is preferable to treating it as an answer to an implied question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r2.anchor: وهذا أولى في التوجيه من جعلها جوابا لسؤال مقدر على ما ذهب إليه صاحب ( الكشاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r3.claim: The alternative analysis makes the request for guidance an answer to an unspoken question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r3.anchor: جوابا لسؤال مقدر على ما ذهب إليه صاحب ( الكشاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r4.claim: Guidance is gentle direction, especially toward what benefits the person guided; the verb takes one direct object and may take its destination with إلى or لام.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r4.anchor: والهداية الدلالة بتلطف ولذلك خصت بالدلالة لما فيه خير المدلول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r5.claim: Examples show a prepositional destination with إلى and لام, while the verse uses a direct second object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r5.anchor: ويتعدى إلى المفعول الثاني وهو المهدى إليه بإلى وباللام والاستعمالان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r6.claim: Some grammarians say direct second-object use is Hijazi, while other Arabs require a preposition and explain the direct object as deletion and connection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r6.anchor: وقد يعدى إلى المفعول الثاني بنفسه كما هنا على تضمينه معنى عرف قيل هي لغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r7.claim: He rejects a fixed semantic split between direct and prepositional forms; the construction usually reflects whether the verb means showing or general guidance, not a different basic sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p187/r7.anchor: والحق أن هذا إن تم فهو أغلبي على أنه تخصيص من الاستعمال فلا يقتضي كون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r1.claim: Guidance literally means showing a route to a destination; religious uses are metaphors, and when attributed to God it means directing toward deeds that please Him, opposite to misleading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r1.anchor: حقيقة الهداية الدلالة على الطريق للوصول إلى المكان المقصود فالهادي هو العارف بالطرق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r2.claim: The migration report describes Abū Bakr hiring a skilled guide from Banū al-Dayl, illustrating the literal route-finding sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r2.anchor: وفي حديث الهجرة : ( إن أبا بكر استأجر رجلا من بني الديل هاديا خريتا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r3.claim: Most theologians, including the Ashʿarites, define guidance as showing the way whether or not the person reaches the good destination; Ibn ʿĀshūr endorses this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r3.anchor: فالجمهور على عدم اعتباره وأنها الدلالة على طريق الوصول سواء حصل الوصول أم لم يحصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r4.claim: The opposing view, also held by a group of theologians, requires guidance to include arrival; otherwise it would not differ from misguidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r4.anchor: وذهب جماعة منهم الزمخشري إلى أن الهداية هي الدلالة مع الإيصال وإلا لما امتازت عن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r5.claim: The disagreement rests on whether divine guidance concerns command or actual creation: Ashʿarites focus on commanded direction, while Muʿtazilites focus on God's creative act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r5.anchor: الأشعري اعتبروا الهداية التي هي من متعلق الأمر ، والمعتزلة نظروا إلى الهداية التي هي من

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r6.speaker: عبد الحكيم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm chooses a shared meaning broad enough for both Quranic uses: the Prophet cannot guide a loved one, yet Thamūd were guided and chose blindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r6.anchor: اختار عبد الحكيم أنها موضوعة في الشرع لقدر المشترك لورودها في القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r7.claim: Guidance comprises four ranked kinds; the first is the natural endowment of perceptive and motivating faculties that sustain human life, from infant instinct to rational thought.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p188/r7.anchor: الأول إعطاء القوى المحركة والمدركة التي بها يكون الاهتداء إلى انتظام وجود ذات الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r1.claim: The second kind of guidance is setting out evidence that distinguishes truth from falsehood and correct judgment from error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r1.anchor: الثاني نصب الأدلة الفارقة بين الحق والباطل والصواب والخطأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r2.claim: The third kind comes through messengers, scriptures, and just measures when evidence is insufficient or too difficult to apply; the Quran says messengers guide by God's command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r2.anchor: الثالث الهداية إلى ما قد تقصر عنه الأدلة أو يفضي إعمالها في مثله إلى مشقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r3.claim: The highest kind unveils transcendent truths and mysteries through revelation, true inspiration, or spiritual manifestations, as in the Quran's description of prophets.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r3.anchor: أقصى أجناس الهداية وهي كشف الحقائق العليا وإظهار أسرار المعاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r4.claim: The request may concern the guidance suited to one supplicant, or all kinds apportioned according to capacity when the believers pray collectively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r4.anchor: هو أنواع الهداية على الجملة باعتبار توزيعها على من تأهل لها بحسب أهليته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r5.claim: Some guidance is requested for those who lack it, while already attained guidance is requested to continue, especially the natural endowments of the first kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r5.anchor: فبعض أنواع الهداية مطلوب حصوله لمن لم يبلغ إليه ، وبعضها مطلوب دوامه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r6.claim: An imperative used only to request persistence is figurative, as in the command for believers to believe; asking for additional degrees is literal acquisition and implies preserving what is gained.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r6.anchor: وصيغة الطلب موضوعة لطلب حصول الماهية المطلوبة من فعل أو كف فإذا استعملت في طلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r7.claim: For the Prophet, who attained every degree, the prayer is figurative and borrowed from the verse rather than its primary intent: asking for complete guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p189/r7.anchor: فإن دعاءه حينئذ يكون من استعمال اللفظ في مجاز معناه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r1.claim: Ṣirāṭ is read with ṣād or sīn; the Hijazi shift from sīn to ṣād lightens articulation before emphatic ṭāʾ, while other dialects preserve sīn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r1.anchor: وهو بالصاد وبالسين وقد قرىء بهما في المشهورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r2.speaker: الجعبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī says speakers also alter sīn before several consonants; here ṣād matches ṭāʾ in emphatic articulation and avoids a difficult low-to-high transition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r2.anchor: عن الجعبري إنهم يفعلون ذلك في كل سين بعدها غين أو خاء أو قاف أو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r3.claim: Ḥamza, in Khalaf's transmission, reads an intermediate sīn-ṣād sound; some Arab tribes used a pure zāy, but that reading is weak and unattested among the canonical readers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r3.anchor: وقيس قلبوا السين بين الصاد والزاي وهو إشمام وقرأ به حمزة في رواية خلف عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r4.claim: Most readers choose ṣād as the preferable reading because it matches the written muṣḥaf and the eloquent dialect; Ibn Kathīr through Qunbul reads sīn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r4.anchor: جمهور القراء وقرأ بالسين ابن كثير في رواية قنبل ، والقراءة بالصاد هي الراجحة لموافقتها رسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r5.claim: The Companions wrote ṣād to indicate the more eloquent Quraysh form; readers of sīn understood the spelling as permitting a known dialectal pronunciation, not a different word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r5.anchor: إن الصحابة كتبوها بالصاد تنبيها على الأفصح فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r6.claim: Ṣirāṭ is an Arabic word; the claims that it means path in Roman are unsupported by the lexicographers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r6.anchor: والصراط اسم عربي ولم يقل أحد من أهل اللغة إنه معرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r7.speaker: النقاش
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r7.claim: Al-Naqqāsh and Ibn al-Jawzī, citing Abū Ḥātim, say the word means path in the Roman language; al-Suyūṭī adopted the claim in his foreign-word poem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190/r7.anchor: ذكر في ( الإتقان ) عن النقاش وابن الجوزي أنه الطريق بلغة الروم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r3.claim: The imperative “Guide us” is a dependent creature's request to its Lord; the same form is a command when spoken by a superior.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r3.anchor:
وقوله تعالى:
اهدنا رغبة لأنها من المربوب إلى الرب، وهكذا صيغة الأمر كلها، فإذا كانت من الأعلى فهي أمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r4.claim: Guidance literally means direction, and its varied exegetical senses all reduce to direction when examined.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r4.anchor: والهداية في اللغة الإرشاد، لكنها تتصرف على وجوه يعبر عنها المفسرون بغير لفظ الإرشاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r5.claim: Huda can mean creating faith in the heart, as in 2:5, 10:25, 28:56, and 6:125.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r5.anchor: فالهدى يجيء بمعنى خلق الإيمان في القلب، ومنه قوله تعالى: أولئك على هدى من ربهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r6.speaker: أبو المعالي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r6.claim: Abu al-Maʿali says 6:125 can only be understood as creating faith in the heart, which is pure guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r6.anchor: فهذه آية لا يتجه حملها إلا على خلق الإيمان في القلب، وهو محض الإرشاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r7.claim: Guidance can also mean calling or inviting, as in 13:7 and 42:52, but this too is initial direction whether or not the invited person responds.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r8.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r8.claim: Exegetes gloss God's guidance of every creature in 20:50 as inspiring animals to their benefits, which also expresses direction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون: معناه «ألهم الحيوانات كلها إلى منافعها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r9.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r9.claim: Exegetes gloss 41:17 as “We made clear to them,” while Abu al-Maʿali takes it as “We called them”; both are forms of guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r9.anchor: قال المفسرون: «معناه بينا لهم» . قال أبو المعالي: معناه دعوناهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r10.claim: God's statement that guidance is incumbent upon him in 92:12 means that he must make it clear, still retaining the sense of direction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73/r10.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله تعالى: إن علينا للهدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: أبو المعالي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.claim: Guidance may mean directing believers along the routes to Paradise, as in 47:5, or leading people to Hell, as in 37:23.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: وقد ترد الهداية والمراد بها إرشاد المؤمنين إلى مسالك الجنان والطرق المفضية إليها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.claim: This wayfinding is the sense of “Guide us to the straight path”: it is guidance along a route, the opposite of going astray, not creating faith or merely calling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r2.anchor: وهذه الهداية بعينها هي التي تقال في طرق الدنيا، وهي ضد الضلال وهي الواقعة في قوله تعالى: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.speaker: اللحياني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.claim: Al-Lihyani treats huda as feminine, while Ibn Sidah says it is masculine and also names daylight; Ibn Muqbil's poem illustrates the latter use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r3.anchor: والهدى لفظ مؤنث، وقال اللحياني: «هو مذكر» قال ابن سيده: «والهدى اسم من أسماء النهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.claim: Sirat means a clear path, illustrated by Jarir and another poet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r4.anchor: والصراط في اللغة الطريق الواضح فمن ذلك قول جرير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.claim: Al-Naqqash says sirat means “path” in the language of Rome; the author judges the claim extremely weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r5.anchor:
وحكى النقاش: «الصراط الطريق بلغة الروم» .
قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف جدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir and a group read the word with sīn, which the source says is its original form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r6.anchor: واختلف القراء في الصراط فقرأ ابن كثير وجماعة من العلماء: «السراط» بالسين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r7.claim: Al-Farisi also transmits the ṣād pronunciation from Ibn Kathir.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r7.anchor: قال الفارسي: «ورويت عن ابن كثير بالصاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r8.speaker: باقي السبعة غير حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r8.claim: The remaining canonical readers except Hamza use plain ṣād, assimilating original sīn to the emphatic ṭāʾ for a more harmonious sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة غير حمزة بصاد خالصة وهذا بدل السين بالصاد لتناسبها مع الطاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r9.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r9.claim: Sibawayh records the sīn-to-ṣād substitution as a dialect.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r10.claim: Abu ʿAmr is reported with both sīn and ṣād and with an intermediate pronunciation approaching zāy; al-Asmaʿi also reports a plain zāy reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r10.anchor: روي عن أبي عمرو السين والصاد، والمضارعة بين الصاد والزاي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r11.speaker: بعض اللغويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r11.claim: Some philologists say al-Asmaʿi mistook Abu ʿAmr's intermediate sound for plain zāy and was not qualified as a grammarian to vouch for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p73#2/r11.anchor: إنما سمع أبا عمرو يقرأ بالمضارعة فتوهمها زايا، ولم يكن الأصمعي نحويا فيؤمن على هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r1.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak read “Guide us to a straight path,” without the definite article.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والضحاك: «اهدنا صراطا مستقيما» دون تعريف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads “Guide us to the path,” making path genitive in an annexation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r2.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد الصادق: «اهدنا صراط المستقيم» بالإضافة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r3.speaker: ثابت البناني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r3.claim: Thabit al-Bunani reads “Show us the path.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r4.claim: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib says the straight path here is the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r4.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: الصراط المستقيم هنا القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r5.speaker: جابر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r5.claim: Jabir says the path is Islam, meaning the hanif religion, and describes its breadth as extending between heaven and earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r5.anchor: وقال جابر: «هو الإسلام» يعني الحنيفية. وقال: سعته ما بين السماء والأرض.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya defines it as God's religion, the only one accepted from servants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r6.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية: «هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r7.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says the straight path is the Prophet and his two companions Abu Bakr and ʿUmar; al-Hasan affirms his correctness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: «هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه أبو بكر وعمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r8.claim: These interpretations converge: believers ask to follow the blessed in belief and law, embodying the Qur'an, Islam, and the way of the Prophet and his two companions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r8.anchor: ويجتمع من هذه الأقوال كلها أن الدعوة إنما هي في أن يكون الداعي على سنن المنعم عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r9.claim: Believers who already possess some guidance ask for constancy, while they ask for direction toward what they lack through ignorance or negligence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r9.anchor: فمعنى قولهم اهدنا فيما هو حاصل عندهم طلب التثبيت والدوام، وفيما ليس بحاصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r10.claim: Each petitioner asks for the complete path in speech, conduct, and belief; “Guide us” cannot mean create our faith or call us, since the request is for guidance to a specified path.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r10.anchor: فإنما يريد الصراط بكماله في أقواله وأفعاله ومعتقداته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r11.claim: Sirat is the second object of the verb; mustaqim means without bend or deviation, set upon truth toward success and Paradise, and sirat alladhina is an appositive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r11.anchor: والصراط نصب على المفعول الثاني، والمستقيم الذي لا عوج فيه ولا انحراف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r12.claim: Mustaqim derives from mustaqwim by moving the vowel to qaf and changing wāw to yāʾ after kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r12.anchor: وإعلال مستقيم أن أصله مستقوم نقلت الحركة إلى القاف وانقلبت الواو ياء لانكسار ما قبلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r13.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r13.claim: Ibn Mujahid says Hamza's intermediate ṣād-zāy requires an awkward sound between letters, though it exists in eloquent Arab speech; he considers plain ṣād clearer and more widespread.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p74/r13.anchor: قال ابن مجاهد: «وهذه القراءة تكلف حرف بين حرفين، وذلك أصعب على اللسان

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.claim: The same waṣl rule applies to initial alifs in verbs or verbal nouns whose imperfect form begins with a fatḥa vowel on its yāʾ, as in the cited imperatives.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r5.anchor: وكذلك كل الف كانت في اول فعل او مصدر

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r6.claim: When these verb alifs begin speech they are normally pronounced with kasra; if the third letter is ḍamma, the initial vowel is ḍamma to ease the transition without changing meaning.

AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r7.claim: An initial ḍamma is used when the verb's third letter is ḍamma because moving from kasra through a sukūn to ḍamma is difficult.
AKHFASH:v1p3#2/r7.anchor: الا ما كان منه ثالث حروفه مضموما فانك تضم أوله اذا استأنفت

AKHFASH:v1p16/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r2.claim: Ihdinā means ʿarrifnā, make us know; the people of the Hijaz say hadaytuhu al-ṭarīq or the house, while other Arabs add ilā.

AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.claim: Ṣirāṭ has both sīn and ṣād forms; al-Akhfash prefers ṣād because that is how it is written throughout the Qurʾān.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.anchor: الا انا نختار الصاد لان كتابها على ذلك في جميع القرآن

AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.speaker: أهل الحجاز
AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.claim: The Hijaz dialect feminizes ṣirāṭ like al-ṭarīq, al-zuqāq, al-sabīl, al-sūq, and al-kalāʾ; Tamīm uses masculine forms, while Asad feminizes al-hudā.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r1.speaker: علي وأبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r1.claim: One meaning of ihdinā is “keep us firm,” reported from ʿAlī and Ubayy.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r2.claim: A second meaning of ihdinā is “guide us.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r3.claim: A third meaning is “grant us success”; the last three explanations are transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r3.anchor: والثالث وفقنا والرابع ألهمنا رويت هذه الثلاثة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r4.claim: A fourth meaning is “inspire us,” likewise among the explanations transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r4.anchor: والرابع ألهمنا رويت هذه الثلاثة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r5.claim: Ṣirāṭ means a road or path.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r5.anchor: الطريق ويقال إن أصله بالسين لأنه من الاستراط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Yaʿqūb read with sīn, preserving the word's proposed original form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r6.anchor: فمن قرأ السين كمجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب فعلى أصل الكلمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr and most readers use ṣād because it is lighter on the tongue.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r7.anchor: ومن قرأ بالصاد كأبي عمرو والجمهور فلأنها اخف على اللسان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r8.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r8.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī transmits from Abū ʿAmr a zāy reading, supported by the paired forms Saqar/Zaqar.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ بالزاي كرواية الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو واحتج بقول العرب سقر وزقر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r9.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r9.claim: Two reports from Ḥamza describe blending sīn toward zāy, or pronouncing ṣirāṭ between ṣād and zāy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن حمزة إشمام السين زايا وروي عنه أنه تلفظ بالصراط بين الصاد والزاي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls ṣād the good dialect, that of Quraysh and most Arabs; most Arabs use sīn, while some Qays blend it, and Ḥamza's zāy is a dialect of ʿUdhrā, Kalb, and Banū al-Qayn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r10.anchor: قال الفراء اللغة الجيدة بالصاد وهي لغة قريش الأولى وعامة العرب يجعلونها سينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r11.speaker: علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r11.claim: A report from ʿAlī, going back to the Prophet, identifies the path as God's Book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r11.anchor: أحدها أنه كتاب الله رواه علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r12.claim: Another interpretation identifies the path as Islam; it is held by Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Abū al-ʿĀliya among others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r12.anchor: والثاني أنه دين الاسلام قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن و أبوالعالية في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r13.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r13.claim: A third view calls it the path that guides toward God's religion, transmitted by Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās and held by Mujāhid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r13.anchor: والثالث أنه الطريق الهادي إلى دين الله رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r14.claim: A fourth view, also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the path is the road to Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r14.anchor: والرابع أنه طريق الجنة نقل عن ابن عباس أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r15.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r15.claim: Asked why the already guided ask for guidance, Ibn al-Anbārī says the request means to be kept on the path, with “remaining” omitted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r15.anchor: أحدها أن المعنى إهدنا لزوم الصراط فحذف اللزوم قاله ابن الأنباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r16.claim: A second answer is “keep us in guidance,” like telling someone who is standing to remain where he is until one returns.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r16.anchor: والثاني أن المعنى ثبتنا على الهدى تقول العرب للقائم قم حتى آتيك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p14#2/r17.claim: A third answer is that the request asks God to increase their guidance.

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.claim: In a divine report, God divides the prayer between Himself and His servant, responds to each recited section, calls 1:5 shared between them, and grants the servant's request.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.anchor: قال : هذا بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r1.claim: The majority read al-ṣirāṭ with ṣād; other readings use sīn or zāy, the latter being a dialect of several tribes according to al-Farra.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r2.claim: After praising the One being asked, the sura turns to the request, an exemplary supplication that praises the addressee before asking for needs, including believers' needs.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r3.claim: Supplication can also state the supplicant's need, as Moses does, combine need with praise as Jonah does, or consist of praise that itself suffices to prompt a request.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r3.anchor: وقد يكون السؤال بالإخبار عن حال السائل واحتياجه

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r4.claim: Hidāyah here means guidance and enabling success; direct transitivity can mean inspire, guide, provide, or grant, while construction with ilā means show or direct, and with li means make worthy.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says interpreters unanimously understand the straight path as a clear road without crookedness, a usage confirmed by Arabic speech and poetry.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r5.anchor: أبو جعفر بن جرير : أجمعت الأمة من أهل التأويل

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r6.speaker: جرير بن عطية
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r6.claim: Jarir ibn Atiyyah's verse uses the straight path for a ruler who remains upright when destinations become crooked.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r7.claim: Interpretations of the straight path ultimately converge on following God and His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r7.anchor: ثم اختلفت عبارات المفسرين من السلف والخلف

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r8.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet through Ali identifies the straight path as the Book of God; Ibn Kathir says the report is more plausibly a statement of Ali himself.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir regards the report identifying the straight path with God's Book as more likely transmitted from Ali himself rather than from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r9.anchor: وقد روي هذا موقوفا عن علي ، وهو أشبه

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r10.claim: A related report calls the Qur'an God's strong rope, wise remembrance, and straight path.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r10.anchor: وهو حبل الله المتين ، وهو الذكر الحكيم

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r11.claim: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud says the straight path is the Book of God.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r11.anchor: عن منصور ، عن أبي وائل ، عن عبد الله

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, says the straight path is the guiding way, God's religion without deviation.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas through Maymun ibn Mihran interprets the straight path as Islam.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r13.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران ، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأصحاب النبي
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r14.claim: A collective report from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and Companions of the Prophet identifies the straight path as Islam.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r14.anchor: عن مرة الهمداني ، عن ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r15.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r15.claim: Jabir says the straight path is Islam and describes it as wider than the distance between heaven and earth.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r15.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن محمد بن عقيل ، عن جابر

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r16.speaker: ابن الحنفية
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r16.claim: Ibn al-Hanafiyyah says the straight path is God's religion, the only religion He accepts from servants.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r16.anchor: وقال ابن الحنفية في قوله تعالى

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r17.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r17.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam also interprets the straight path as Islam.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r17.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r18.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet likens the straight path to Islam, bordered by God's limits and forbidden doors, with the Qur'an calling from its head and God's inward admonition calling from above.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r18.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r19.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r19.claim: Mujahid says the straight path is the truth, a broader interpretation that does not conflict with the other explanations.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r19.anchor: وقال مجاهد : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } ، قال : الحق

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r20.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r20.claim: Abu al-Aliyah interprets the straight path as the Prophet and his two successors after him; al-Hasan says he spoke truly and advised well.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r20.anchor: للحسن ، فقال : صدق أبو العالية ونصح

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r21.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r21.claim: Ibn Kathir says all these interpretations agree: following the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar is following truth, Islam, and the Qur'an, God's strong rope and straight path.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r21.anchor: وكل هذه الأقوال صحيحة ، وهي متلازمة

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r22.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r22.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r22.claim: A report from Abdullah says the straight path is the way the Messenger of God left the community upon.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r22.anchor: عن عبد الله ، قال : الصراط المستقيم الذي تركنا عليه رسول الله

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r23.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r23.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r23.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers understanding the request as asking God to keep the worshipper steadfast in the beliefs and acts He approved and granted to those He favored, comprising Islam, revelation, obedience, and the prophetic and rightly guided way.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r23.anchor: بن جرير ، رحمه الله : والذي هو أولى بتأويل هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r24.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r24.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r24.claim: A believer's repeated request for guidance is not redundant: servants always need God's help to stay firm, deepen insight, grow, and continue on guidance because they control neither benefit nor harm for themselves.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r25.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r25.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r25.claim: The command for believers to believe in God and revelation does not seek an already completed state; it asks for steadfastness, continuity, and perseverance in the acts that preserve faith.

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r26.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r26.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r26.claim: Abu Bakr would recite the prayer that God not let hearts deviate after guidance silently in the third unit of the Maghrib prayer, after the Fatiha.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r26.anchor: وقد كان الصديق رضي الله عنه يقرأ بهذه الآية

IBNKATHIR:1:6/r27.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r27.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r27.claim: The request to be guided on the straight path means asking God to keep the worshippers on it and not turn them toward another way.
IBNKATHIR:1:6/r27.anchor: فمعنى قوله تعالى : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم }

JISHUMI:v1p213/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r3.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v1p213/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads ṣirāṭ with an articulation between ṣād and zāy throughout the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة الصراط بإشمام الصاد الزاي كل القرآن

JISHUMI:v1p213/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r4.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p213/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is reported to articulate ṣirāṭ with an articulation between sīn and ṣād throughout the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r4.anchor: وعن الكسائي بإشمام السين كل القرآن

JISHUMI:v1p213/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r5.speaker: يعقوب برواية رويس
JISHUMI:v1p213/r5.claim: Yaʿqūb in Ruways’s narration reads ṣirāṭ with sīn throughout the Qur’an; attribution of that reading to Ibn Kathīr is said to be mistaken.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r5.anchor: قرأ يعقوب برواية رويس بالسين كل القرآن، وقرأ الآخرون بالصاد

JISHUMI:v1p213/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r6.claim: The author prefers ṣād: it better harmonizes with emphatic ṭāʾ, is Qurashī, matches the written codex, and is the reading of most leading reciters; the other forms retain or suggest the root or harmonize voicing.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r6.anchor: والاختيار الصاد لوجوه: منها: أن اجتماع الحرفين المتشاكلين أحسن في المسموع

JISHUMI:v1p213/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r7.claim: Guidance linguistically is indication or direction along a way, opposite error, and in essence indicates the truth; ṣirāṭ means path, from the image of swallowing food, and istiqāmah resembles evenness, opposite crookedness.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r7.anchor: أصل الهداية في اللغة الدلالة، يقال: هديته إلى الطريق، أي دللته

JISHUMI:v1p213/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r8.claim: In ihdinā the object pronoun is the first object, ṣirāṭ the second, and al-mustaqīm modifies ṣirāṭ.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r8.anchor: والصراط: المفعول الثاني، والمستقيم: نعت للصراط

JISHUMI:v1p213/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r9.speaker: أبي علي وأبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v1p213/r9.claim: One gloss asks God to keep the worshippers firm on the straight way of guidance, like telling someone already eating to continue eating.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r9.anchor: قيل: ثبتنا على الطريق المستقيم والهداية، عن أبي علي وأبي بن كعب

JISHUMI:v1p213/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r10.claim: Other proposed meanings ask for direction to Paradise in the Hereafter, future divine لطف to dispel doubts and satanic whispering even for believers, or direction to the route to success and deliverance.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r10.anchor: وقيل: أرشدنا إلى طريق الجنة في الآخرة، وقيل: الطف بنا في المستقبل والمستأنف

JISHUMI:v1p213/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p213/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p213/r11.claim: The request to be kept on the path is best because it matches the preceding request for assistance.
JISHUMI:v1p213/r11.anchor: والأحسن هو الأول؛ ليشاكل ما قبله من طلب المعونة

JISHUMI:v1p215/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r1.claim: The verse requires asking God for guidance and teaches worshippers how to pray; it also calls for repeated supplication so desires do not lead them astray.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r1.anchor: الآية تدل على وجوب طلب الهداية، وتعليم من الله كيف ندعوه

JISHUMI:v1p215/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r2.claim: The author argues human acts are not created by God: otherwise requesting help and guidance would be pointless, like asking help for one’s colors or bodily form.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن أفعال العباد ليست بخلق لله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: The request for guidance explains the help being sought: when asked how He should assist, the servants answer, guide us to the straight path.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor: بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة كأنه قيل كيف أعينكم فقالوا اهدنا الصراط المستقيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.claim: Hada normally takes li or ila, but here it is used transitively like ikhtara; this pattern is illustrated by the choice of Moses's people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r1.anchor: هدى أصله ان يتعدى باللام أو بإلى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.claim: Asking for guidance despite already being guided means asking God for further guidance through special favor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى طلب الهداية وهم مهتدون طلب زيادة الهدى بمنح الإلطاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.speaker: علي وأبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.claim: Ali and Ubayy explain ihdina as keep us steadfast; the imperative and prayer share a request form and differ only in rank.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r3.anchor: وعن علي وأبي رضي الله عنهما اهدنا ثبتنا وصيغة الأمر والدعاء واحدة لأن كل واحد منهما طلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r4.claim: Abdullah reads the phrase as guide us rightly.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.claim: Sirat is the road, from a root meaning to swallow because it swallows up travelers; luqma has a similar sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r5.anchor: السراط الجادة من سرط الشيء اذا ابتلعه لأنه يسترط السابلة اذا سلكوه كما سمي لقما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.claim: Sirat alternates sīn and ṣād because of the following ṭā; several readings exist, but pure ṣād is most eloquent, Qurashi, and the codex reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r6.anchor: والصراط من قلب السين صادا لأجل الطاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.claim: Sirat has a plural and can be masculine or feminine; here it means the path of truth, the religion of Islam.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p57#2/r7.anchor: ويجمع سرطا نحو كتاب وكتب ويذكر ويؤنث كالطريق والسبيل والمراد طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.claim: After referring to the absent, the discourse returns to direct address in ‘You alone we worship, You alone we ask for help, guide us.’
MAJAZ:v1p22/r4.anchor: ثم رجع فخاطب شاهدا فقال: «إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين اهدنا» (5) ، قال عنترة بن شداد العبسى:

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r1.claim: Ihdina can mean guide and show us the way.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r2.claim: He interprets ihdina as grant us success in following the way.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r2.anchor: معناه وفقنا , وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r3.claim: Sirat can mean the straight path, as illustrated by Jarir's verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r3.anchor: ومنه قول جرير : أمير المؤمنين على صراط

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r4.claim: Sirat can also mean the clear road; the Quran and another poem use it this way, and its root is the passage of food through the throat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ { ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r5.claim: The prayer for guidance can seek its continuation even for people already guided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r5.anchor: أنهم دعوا باستدامة الهداية , وإن كانوا قد هدوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r6.claim: The prayer can ask God to increase their guidance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r7.claim: The prayer can express sincere desire and hope for the reward of supplication.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r7.anchor: أنهم دعوا بها إخلاصا للرغبة , ورجاء لثواب الدعاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r8.speaker: علي وعبد الله
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r8.claim: They identify the straight path as God's Book; a similar interpretation is also transmitted from the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r8.anchor: وهو قول علي وعبد الله , ويروى نحوه عن النبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله ومحمد بن الحنفية
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r9.claim: They identify the straight path as Islam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r9.anchor: وهو قول جابر بن عبد الله , ومحمد بن الحنفية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r10.claim: He identifies it as the route that leads to God's religion and has no crookedness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r10.anchor: الذي لا عوج فيه , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r11.speaker: الحسن البصري وأبو العالية الرياحي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r11.claim: They identify the straight path as the Messenger and the best of his family and Companions.

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r3.claim: The straight path is Islam, since no religion besides Islam is straight.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r3.anchor: يعنى دين الإسلام؛ لأن غير دين الإسلام ليس بمستقيم

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading replaces the request to guide with the wording meaning direct or guide us.

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet related that God divided this sūra between Himself and the servant: praise is thanks, the two mercy names are praise, the King verse is glorification, and the rest belongs to the servant; seeking help is God's special acknowledgment of the servant's plea.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.anchor: عن أبى هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r1.claim: “Guide us” can mean keep us firm on the clear way, like telling someone already standing to remain there, or guide us henceforth as You have guided us already.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r1.anchor: أي ثبتنا على المنهاج الواضح كقولك للقائم قم حتى أعود إليك اى اثبت على ما أنت عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r2.claim: Hada can govern one object directly or govern another with the particles li and ila, as the cited verses show.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r2.anchor: وهدى يتعدى بنفسه إلى مفعول واحد فأما تعديه إلى مفعول آخر فقد جاء متعديا إليه بنفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r3.claim: Sirat is the road, from the root for swallowing, as if it swallows travelers who walk it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r3.anchor: والسراط الجادة من سرط الشئ إذا ابتلعه كأنه يسرط السابلة إذا سلكوه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r4.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r4.claim: Hamza reads the initial consonant as a sound between ṣād and zāy, assimilated toward the emphatic ṭāʾ.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r4.anchor: وهى قراءة حمزة والسين قراءة ابن كثير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir reads sirat with sīn throughout the Qur'an; the source calls this the word's original form.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r5.anchor: والسين قراءة ابن كثير فى كل القرآن وهى الأصل فى الكلمة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r6.claim: The remaining readers use pure ṣād, the Quraysh dialect and the form fixed in the codex; sirat can be masculine or feminine and here means Islam's path of truth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8/r6.anchor: والباقون بالصاد الخالصة وهى لغة قريش وهى الثابتة فى المصحف الإمام

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r11.claim: Ihdina is a prayer from servant to Lord: guide and show us the straight path leading to intimacy and nearness.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r11.anchor: اهدنا دعاء ورغبة من المربوب إلى الرب والمعنى: دلنا على الصراط المستقيم

QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r12.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r12.claim: Some say the sura’s first half gathers praise and its second half petitions; this prayer is especially excellent because the servant uses words spoken by the Lord of the worlds.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:5-6/r12.anchor: فجعل الله جل وعز عظم الدعاء وجملته موضوعا في هذه السورة، نصفها فيه مجمع الثناء، ونصفها فيه مجمع الحاجات

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r1.claim: A hadith says nothing is more honored by God than supplication.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r1.anchor: " ليس شيء أكرم على الله من الدعاء "

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r2.claim: Another explanation asks for guidance through observing the sunnas in fulfilling obligations; the root may mean to incline, so the prayer asks God to turn hearts toward truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى: أرشدنا باستعمال السنن في أداء فرائضك وقيل: الأصل فيه الإمالة ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r3.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r3.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad identifies the straight path as the pilgrimage route, but the author prefers the general meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r3.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: «الصراط المستقيم» طريق الحج، وهذا خاص والعموم أولى.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r4.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r4.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says the straight path is God’s religion, the only religion He accepts from servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r4.anchor: هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r5.speaker: عاصم الأحول عن أبي العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya identifies the path as Muhammad and his two successors, Abu Bakr and ʿUmar; al-Hasan affirms that this is truthful counsel.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r5.anchor: قال عاصم فقلت للحسن: إن أبا العالية يقول: «الصراط المستقيم» رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه، قال: صدق ونصح.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r6.claim: Ṣirāṭ is the Arabic word for road; a claim that it is Roman is very weak according to Ibn ʿAtiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:6/r6.anchor: وحكى النقاش: الصراط الطريق بلغة الروم قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف جدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r1.claim: The word has readings with sīn, between zāy and ṣād, or pure zāy; sīn is original, while the zāy dialect is associated with ʿUdhra, Kalb, and Banu al-Qayn.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r1.anchor: صراط بدل من الأول بدل الشيء من الشيء كقولك: جاءني زيد أبوك

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r2.claim: Ṣirāṭ is the second object of guidance, which may take a preposition or not; mustaqīm means without bending, from mustaqwim with a sound change.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو صراط آخر، ومعناه العلم بالله جل وعز والفهم عنه قاله جعفر بن محمد.

NAHHAS:v1p174/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p174/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats ihdinā as a supplication and request in the jussive.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r1.anchor: دعاء وطلب في موضع جزم عند الفراء

NAHHAS:v1p174/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r2.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p174/r2.claim: The Basrans call the verb stopped or indeclinable, which explains the loss of its yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r2.anchor: ووقف عند البصريين ولذلك حذفت الياء

NAHHAS:v1p174/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r3.claim: The initial alif is a connecting hamza, and its kasra reflects the verb yahdī; nā is the first object and al-ṣirāṭ the second.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r3.anchor: والألف ألف وصل لأن أول المستقبل مفتوح وكسرتها لأنه من يهدي والنون والألف مفعول أول

NAHHAS:v1p174/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r4.claim: The small plural of ṣirāṭ is aṣriṭa and its larger plural is ṣuruṭ.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r4.anchor: وجمعه في القليل أصرطة وفي الكثير صرط

NAHHAS:v1p174/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r5.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p174/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash says the people of the Hijaz make ṣirāṭ feminine.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r5.anchor: قال الأخفش أهل الحجاز يؤنثون الصراط

NAHHAS:v1p174/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p174/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads al-ṣirāṭ with sīn.

NAHHAS:v1p174/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r7.speaker: قطرب
NAHHAS:v1p174/r7.claim: Qutrub says some Qays speakers pronounce sīn between sīn and ṣād; sīn may become ṣād before ṭāʾ, qāf, khāʾ, or ghayn in the same word.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r7.anchor: قال قطرب إذا كان بعد السين في نفس الكلمة طاء أو قاف أو خاء أو غين فلك أن تقلبها صادا

NAHHAS:v1p174/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r8.claim: Al-mustaqīm is an adjective modifying al-ṣirāṭ.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.claim: Al-Fatiha is Meccan and has seven verses; Muslims recite it at least seventeen times daily, more with voluntary prayers, and may repeat it without limit.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.claim: The Prophet says prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening of the Book; the report is in both Sahih collections.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.claim: The short surah gathers core Islamic creed, worldview, feelings, and guidance, explaining its repetition in every rakʿa and why prayer without it is invalid.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.anchor: ما يشير إلى طرف من حكمة اختيارها للتكرار

QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r1.claim: The prayer asks God both to show the connected, straight road and to keep the worshippers upright on it; knowing and following it are gifts of His guidance and care.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r1.anchor: وفقنا إلى معرفة الطريق المستقيم الواصل

QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r2.claim: Guidance to the straight path is the believer's greatest and first request because it certainly secures happiness in both worlds and aligns human nature with God's law and creation.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:6/r2.anchor: وهذا الأمر هو أعظم وأول ما يطلب المؤمن من ربه العون فيه

QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.speaker: رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Sahih Muslim that God calls al-Fatiha a prayer divided between Himself and His servant: praise, mercy, and glorification are the Lord's; worship and aid are shared; guidance and the servant's request belong to the servant, who receives what he asks.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله [ ص ] :  "  يقول الله تعالى : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: The straight path in belief avoids both excessive transcendence, which negates attributes, and excessive affirmation, which anthropomorphizes; it affirms without either error.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: والصراط المستقيم الإقرار الخالي عن التشبيه والتعطيل

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: Regarding human acts, the middle position affirms human agency while holding that all occurs by God's decree, avoiding both Qadari determinism of human independence and denial of agency.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: والصراط المستقيم إثبات الفعل للعبد مع الإقرار بان الكل بقضاء الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: In conduct, the straight path is moderation: chastity between indulgence and rigid abstinence, and courage between recklessness and cowardice.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r3.anchor: والصراط المستقيم هو الوسط وهو العفة وأيضا من بالغ في الأعمال الغضبية

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Some say specifying the path of the favored shows that a seeker needs a guiding shaykh, since most people lack sound judgment and need a perfected guide's intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: إنه لما قال ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ لم يقتصر عليه بل قال

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: Razi says the surah sets out the covenants of lordship and servitude together, as in God's promise to fulfill each side of His covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: هذه السورة وافية ببيان ما يجب معرفته من عهد الربوبية وعهد العبودية

RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: The law, path, and reality complete human ascent: worship, reliance on God, and guidance culminate in fellowship with the pure and distance from the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: أعني الشريعة المدلول عليها بقوله إياك نعبد والطريقة المدلول عليها بقوله وإياك نستعين

RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.claim: As the servant ceases serving rulers and relying on them for wealth or rank, he turns instead to worshipping God and seeking guidance and knowledge from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r6.anchor: فعند زوال ذلك التعلق يعلم أنه لما كان مشتغلا بخدمة الأمير والوزير فلأن يشتغل بخدمة المعبود كان أولى

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha while counting the basmala as its first verse, followed by the rest of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: روى الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن مسلم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن أم سلمة أنها قالت

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: In the divided-prayer report, God calls the basmala glorification, al-Hamd praise, the two mercy names extolling, the Master of Judgment entrustment, and the remaining response a sharing and a request granted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: فإذا قال العبد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله سبحانه مجدني عبدي وإذا قال الحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
