RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p203/r1.claim: The spiritual stations are knowledge of lordship and servitude; together they fulfill the covenant of 2:40. The opening praise establishes lordship, worship begins servitude, reliance completes it, and guidance is its fruit.

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.claim: The apparent paradox is that a believer already has guidance; Rāzī answers that asking for the straight path can mean seeking the earlier believers' strength in bearing hardship for God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r1.anchor: المراد منه صراط الأولين في تحمل المشاق العظيمة لأجل مرضاة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.claim: Noah was beaten repeatedly and each time prayed for his people to be guided; Muhammad's repeated daily recitation of al-Fātiḥah means he uttered the request more often, so Noah's single prayer does not make him superior.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r2.anchor: وكان يقول في كل مرة : اللهم اهد قومي فإنهم لا يعلمون

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.claim: Guidance also means the just middle between excess and neglect in every character and action, including desire, anger, and spending; even a believer needs this balance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r3.anchor: وهما مذمومان والحق هو الوسط ويتأكد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.claim: A believer may know God through one proof yet overlook the many signs in created things; guidance asks God to reveal how each thing evidences His essence, attributes, power, and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r4.anchor: عرف الله بدليل واحد فلا موجود من أقسام الممكنات إلا وفيه دلائل على وجود الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.claim: The straight path is wholehearted turning to God, as 42:52–53 and 6:153 say; it means following the prophets' endurance in sacrifice, obedience, exile, and even death, while the verse also offers the easier hope of repentance and accepted mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r5.anchor: وذلك الصراط المستقيم هو أن يكون الإنسان معرضا عما سوى الله مقبلا بكلية قلبه

RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.claim: The seeker faces pressure from friends, enemies, Satan, passions, sectarian extremes, weak reason, short life, risky experience, and difficult destiny; he asks for a smooth path out to Paradise.
RAZI-FULL:v1p205#2/r6.anchor: كثرة الأحباب يجرونني إلى طريق والأعداء إلى طريق ثان والشيطان إلى طريق ثالث

RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r1.claim: Some identify the straight path as Islam, while others say it is the Qur'an.
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r1.anchor: الصراط المستقيم : الإسلام وقال بعضهم : القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r2.claim: Rāzī rejects those identifications because the following apposition points to the path of earlier nations, who did not have the Qur'an and Islam; the intended path is that of the truthful and Paradise-worthy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r2.anchor: بدل من الصراط المستقيم وإذا كان كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r3.claim: “Path” rather than the synonyms way or road evokes the path to Hell, increasing fear and caution.
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r3.anchor: لفظ الصراط مذكرا لصراط جهنم ؛ فيكون الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r4.claim: A second interpretation of “guide us” is “keep us firm in the guidance You have given,” as in 3:8; even learned people can be misled by a subtle doubt.
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r4.anchor: ثبتنا على الهداية التي وهبتها منا

RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r5.claim: The plural prayer is more likely to be answered: if any Muslim merits a response, God's generosity will not answer some worshipers and reject the rest.
RAZI-FULL:v1p206/r5.anchor: إذا أجاب الله الدعاء في البعض فهو أكرم من أن يرده في الباقي

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r1.claim: The Prophet says to call on God with tongues not used in sin; when the Companions ask who has such tongues, he tells them to pray for one another because none sinned with another's tongue.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r1.anchor: ادعوا الله بألسنة ما عصيتموه بها قالوا : يا رسول الله ومن لنا بتلك الألسنة

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r2.claim: The earlier wording “praise belongs to God,” rather than “I praise God,” includes all worshipers; the servant similarly says “guide us” to include them in his request.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r2.anchor: ألست قلت في أول السورة الحمد لله وما قلت أحمد الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r3.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r3.claim: The Prophet teaches that congregation is mercy and separation punishment; the servant therefore speaks collectively in praise, worship, reliance, guidance, following the righteous, and avoiding the condemned and astray, hoping to remain with the righteous in the next life.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r3.anchor: الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب فلما أردت تحميدك ذكرت حمد الجميع

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r4.claim: Geometry defines a straight line as the shortest distance between two points; a weak servant asks for this shorter route.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r4.anchor: الخط المستقيم هو أقصر خط يصل بين نقطتين

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r5.claim: A straight road is uniquely recognizable, while crooked paths resemble and confuse one another, making the straight way safer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r5.anchor: المستقيم فلا يشابهه غيره فكان أبعد عن الخوف والآفات

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r6.claim: The straight route reaches the goal, whereas a crooked route does not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r6.anchor: الطريق المستقيم يوصل إلى المقصود والمعوج لا يوصل إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p207/r7.claim: The straight route remains stable, whereas crooked paths change; this is the fourth reason to ask for it.

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.claim: The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآيات السبع دافعة لتلك الأخلاق القبيحة السبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.claim: The effects of worship are guidance, unveiling, and disclosure, expressed in the request to be guided to the straight path.

RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.claim: Human knowledge grows through one's own reasoning or through receiving predecessors' discoveries: “guide us” asks for the first, and the path of the favored for the second.
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.anchor: وقوله : ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ إشارة إلى القسم الأول

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: In a divine report transmitted by the Prophet, God responds to each Fatiha phrase: the opening remembers Him, praise praises Him, the mercy names magnify Him, Judgment Day glorifies Him or is entrusted to Him, worship belongs to Him, aid relies on Him, and guidance is the servant's request.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: فإذا قال العبد : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يقول الله تعالى ذكرني عبدي

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: Calling the Fatiha “prayer” shows that religious law serves human interests: people most need knowledge of God's lordship and servitude, which the surah's two halves provide to fulfill the covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: مدار الشرائع على رعاية مصالح الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: Since God names the Fatiha “prayer,” prayer without its recitation does not occur; Razi takes this to establish that reciting it is a pillar, as his school holds.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor: أن عند عدم قراءة الفاتحة وجب أن لا تحصل الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.claim: Razi supports obligatory Fatiha recitation because the Prophet consistently recited it and commands require following him.

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.claim: The rightly guided caliphs also consistently recited it, and the Prophet commanded Muslims to follow their sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.anchor: أن الخلفاء الراشدين واظبوا على قراءتها

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.claim: Muslims everywhere recite it in prayer, and the Qur'an commands following the path of believers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.anchor: أن جميع المسلمين شرقا وغربا لا يصلون إلا بقراءة الفاتحة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.claim: The prophetic statement “no prayer without the Opening of the Book” directly supports the requirement.

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.claim: The command to recite what is easy from the Qur'an is obligatory; because reciting other passages is not, the obligatory recitation must be the Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: وظاهره الوجوب فكانت قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن واجبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.claim: Reciting the Fatiha is the safer course, following the prophetic instruction to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.anchor: أن قراءة الفاتحة أحوط فوجب المصير إليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.claim: The Prophet's constant practice makes abandoning his command forbidden, and Muslims agree that the Fatiha is better and more complete than another recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.anchor: وسابعها : أن الرسول عليه السلام واظب على قراءتها فوجب أن يكون العدول عنه محرما

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.claim: If the superior prayer with the Fatiha discharges the obligation, it does not follow that the inferior prayer with another passage does; the obligation remains due.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.anchor: ولا يلزم من الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الكامل الخروج عن العهدة بالعمل الناقص

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.claim: Prayer seeks remembrance of the heart, and this concise surah gathers lordship and servitude and is equated with the mighty Qur'an; nothing else can replace it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r9.anchor: المقصود من الصلاة حصول ذكر القلب

RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.claim: The transmitted report itself says that prayer is not established without the Fatiha.
RAZI-FULL:v1p217#2/r10.anchor: أن هذا الخبر الذي رويناه يدل على أن عند فقدان الفاتحة لا تحصل الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: Scholars disagree about theology, prophecy, and resurrection despite comparable intellect and sustained inquiry; few reach the truth, so divine guidance must make truth attractive and falsehood repellent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: الشبهات غالبة والظلمات مستولية ولم يصل إلى كنه الحق إلا القليل القليل

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: People do not intend to believe falsehood; if choice alone controlled belief, no one would err, yet most go astray, showing that reaching truth depends on God's guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: ولما رأينا الأكثرين غرقوا في بحر الضلالات علمنا أن الوصول إلى الحق ليس إلا بهداية الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: Angels and prophets likewise attribute knowledge and guidance to God: Razi cites the angels, Adam, Abraham, Joseph, Moses, and Muhammad as examples.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: أما الملائكة فقالوا : ﴿ سبحانك لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: The seven Fatiha verses correspond to the seven bodily prayer acts—standing, bowing, rising, first prostration, rising between prostrations, second prostration, and sitting—as soul to body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: أن آيات الفاتحة سبع والأعمال المحسوسة أيضا في الصلاة سبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r6.claim: The request for guidance to the straight path corresponds to the second prostration, because the greatest request fits the greatest humility.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r6.anchor: فهو سؤال لأهم الأشياء فيليق به السجدة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.claim: The seven Fatiha verses are the soul of the seven prayer acts, themselves the soul of seven stages of human formation; God is the soul of souls and light of lights.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.anchor: روح الأرواح ونور الأنوار هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: Muhammad's ascent has a bodily journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and then the high kingdom, and a spiritual journey from the visible to the unseen and from the unseen to the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: أما ما يتعلق بعالم الأرواح فله معراجان

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: The spiritual ascent rises through human spirits, the spirits of the heavens, angels, throne-bearers, and pure spirits detached from bodies, whose worship and love of God exceed human comprehension.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: ثم تترقى فتنتهي إلى الأرواح المقدسة عن التعلقات بالأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: The ascent continues through ever-higher spiritual ranks until God, the source of all good and mercy; thus the spirit-world is the unseen and God's presence the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: فثبت أن عالم الأرواح هو عالم الغيب وحضرة جلال الربوبية هي غيب الغيب

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.claim: A prophetic report says God has seventy veils of light; if unveiled, the splendor of His face would burn everything perceived by sight, and only prophetic light reveals the number.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: إن لله سبعين حجابا من النور لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه كل ما أدرك البصر

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.claim: Prayer was given to Muhammad as a gift for his community because it joins bodily ascent through actions with spiritual ascent through remembrances.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: إن تحفة أمتك الصلاة وذلك لأنها جامعة بين المعراج الجسماني وبين المعراج الروحاني

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.claim: Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.anchor: فإنه إذا استحكمت المرافقة تعذرت المفارقة

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Raising the hands signals leaving both worlds and directing all inner faculties toward God; “God is greatest” means He exceeds all beings, knowledge, comparison, and even the claim that He is simply greater.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: فاقطع نظرك عنهما بالكلية ووجه قلبك وروحك وسرك وعقلك وفهمك

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.claim: The opening glorification reveals the lights of divine majesty and moves from declaring God's transcendence to praising Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: ثم قل : سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وفي هذا المقام تجلى لك نور سبحات الجلال

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.claim: “Blessed is Your name” unveils pre-eternity and eternity, since blessing here indicates abiding beyond extinction and nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.anchor: لأن قوله تبارك إشارة إلى الدوام المنزه عن الإفناء والإعدام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.claim: “Exalted is Your majesty” signifies that God's knowledge and greatness exceed every stated measure.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: أعلم وأعظم من أن تكون صفات جلاله ونعوت كماله محصورة في القدر المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.claim: “There is no god but You” means every attribute of majesty and perfection belongs only to God; ultimately reason, speech, understanding, and imagination fail before Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: كل صفات الجلال وسمات الكمال له لا لغيره

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r1.claim: Ihdinā is an imperative form used here as a supplication; a command from superior to inferior is an order, the reverse a prayer, and one between equals a request.

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r2.claim: The subject is obligatorily implicit anta; nā is the first object and a single attached pronoun form for first-person plural or royal first person across nominative, accusative, and genitive positions.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r2.anchor: وفاعله مستتر وجوبا لما مر، أي: اهد أنت، ونا مفعول أول

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r3.claim: The claim that yāʾ has the same one form across cases fails because nominative yāʾ addresses a woman, unlike the first-person yāʾ in accusative and genitive use.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r3.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء، لأن الياء في حالة الرفع ليست تلك الياء التي في حالة النصب والجر

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r4.claim: Hum can look alike across cases, but nominative hum is detached while accusative and genitive hum are attached, unlike nā.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r4.anchor: إلا أنه في حالة الرفع ضمير منفصل، وفي حالة النصب والجر ضمير متصل

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r5.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ is the second object, and al-mustaqīm is its adjective, agreeing in the four relevant features.

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r6.claim: Hadā normally governs its first object directly and its second with ilā or lām; the preposition is omitted here, yielding direct government of both objects.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r6.anchor: ثم يتسع فيه، فيحذف الحرف الحرف فيتعدى بنفسه

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r7.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r7.claim: Basrans hold that the imperative is indeclinable, whereas Kufans treat it as inflected.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r7.anchor: والأمر عند البصريين مبني وعند الكوفيين معرب

SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r8.claim: The Kufan derivation of iḍrib from an imperative jussive with deleted lām and imperfect prefix is unnecessary; the author reserves a fuller refutation for a better place.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6/r8.anchor: وهذا ما لا حاجة إليه، وللرد عليهم موضع أليق به

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r1.claim: Ihd has pattern ifʿ, with its final weak yāʾ deleted by analogy to the jussive, where a weak final letter drops.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r1.anchor: ووزن اهد: افع، حذفت لامه وهي الياء حملا للأمر على المجزوم

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r2.claim: Hidāya can mean guidance, direction, or going ahead, as in the forelocks of horses; Imruʾ al-Qays uses the latter sense.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r2.anchor: والهداية: الإرشاد أو الدلالة أو التقدم، ومنه هوادي الخيل لتقدمها

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r3.claim: The cited line uses al-hādiyāt for those preceding the rest of the horses.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r3.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: 67 فألحقه بالهاديات ودونه

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r4.claim: Hidāya also means making clear, as in the statement that Thamūd were shown the way, and inspiration toward what benefits each creature.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r4.anchor: أو التبيين نحو: وأما ثمود فهديناهم [فصلت: 17]. أي بينا لهم، أو الإلهام

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r5.claim: Another reported sense is supplication or calling, while deriving it here from inclination is mistaken because that belongs to a different root.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r5.anchor: أو الدعاء كقوله تعالى: ولكل قوم هاد [الرعد: 7] أي داع. وقيل هو الميل

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib defines guidance as gentle indication; hadaytu is for directing, while ahdaytu is for giving a gift.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r6.anchor: وقال الراغب: " الهداية دلالة بلطف ومنه الهدية وهوادي/ الوحش

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r7.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ is a readily traversed road, though some omit the qualification of ease; cited lines simply attest the road sense.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r7.anchor: والصراط: الطريق المستسهل، وبعضهم لا يقيده بالمستسهل، قال:

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r8.claim: Ṣirāṭ derives from swallowing: either the traveler swallows the road or the road swallows the traveler; this also explains calling it a mouthful or something that swallows.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r8.anchor: وهو مشتق من السرط، وهو الابتلاع: إما لأن سالكه يسترطه

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r9.claim: The original consonant is sīn; Qunbul reads it, while the common ṣād is an assimilation near the emphatic sound, as in cited lexical parallels.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r9.anchor: وأصله السين، وقد قرأ به قنبل حيث ورد، وإنما أبدلت صادا

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r10.claim: Some color ṣād toward zāy: Khalaf does so wherever the word occurs, Khallād only in its first occurrence, and pure zāy is also reported; the muṣḥaf writes ṣād.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r10.anchor: وقد تشم الصاد في الصراط ونحوه زايا، وقرأ به خلف حيث ورد

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r11.claim: Ṣirāṭ is masculine in Tamīm and feminine in the Hijaz; its plural patterns vary with gender.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r11.anchor: والصراط يذكر ويؤنث، فالتذكير لغة تميم، وبالتأنيث لغة الحجاز

SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r12.claim: Mustaqīm is an active participle of istaqāma with the simple verb's sense, meaning straight; its underlying form is mustaqwim, altered like nastaʿīn.
SAMIN-DURR:1:6#2/r12.anchor: والمستقيم: اسم فاعل من استقام بمعنى المجرد، ومعناه السوي من غير اعوجاج

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.claim: Most scholars place al-Fātiḥah among the earliest sūrahs revealed in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.anchor: to have been revealed in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.claim: Mujāhid says al-Fātiḥah was revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.anchor: According to Mujāhid (d. 104/722–23), one of the leading scholars among the second generation of Muslims, this sūrah was revealed in Madinah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.claim: Most scholars reject a Medinan origin because Muslims needed the sūrah to perform obligatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.anchor: Most scholars claim that this is impossible, however, as the Muslims would not have been able to perform their required prayers without it

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥah means The Opening: it opens the Book, each prayer cycle, many everyday acts, and may open the breast to faith.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.anchor: The primary meaning of al-Fātiḥah is “The Opening,” which indicates the sūrah’s function as “the opening of the Book”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.claim: The sūrah is seen as a synthesis and the Quran’s most important chapter, hence Umm al-kitāb; the title also refers to 3:7 and the celestial archetype of scripture.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.anchor: has been given the title Umm al-kitāb, “Mother of the Book,” a

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.claim: It is called the Mother of the Quran because it contains the meaning of the entire Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.anchor: It is also known as “The Mother of the Quran” (IK, Ṭ), a reference to its containing the meaning of the entire Quran

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.claim: Another title, The Seven Oft-Repeated, is linked to 15:87.

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.claim: The title The Cure reflects its reputed healing power for body and soul.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.anchor: is said to have healing powers for both body and soul

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.claim: The title The Foundation reflects the Fātiḥah’s role as a foundation for the whole Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.anchor: because it serves as a foundation

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.claim: As Sūrat al-Ḥamd and Sūrat al-Ṣalāh, the Fātiḥah begins each prayer cycle for Sunnis and many Shiites.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.anchor: the Fātiḥah is recited at the beginning of each

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.claim: Shiite law permits reciting the Fātiḥah in the third and fourth cycles or an alternative formula praising God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.anchor: In Shiite law one is allowed to recite the Fātiḥah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.claim: Muslims recite the Fātiḥah at diverse life events; funeral services are called fātiḥah in some lands as an opening from one life to another.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.anchor: It is also recited by Muslims on occasions as diverse as a funeral, a wedding, the birth of a child, the inauguration of an official event

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.claim: The Prophet identifies the Fātiḥah as the greatest sūrah, calling it Praise be to God and the seven oft-repeated, and linking it to 15:87.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.anchor: the Prophet told a man that he would teach him the greatest sūrah; when asked what it was, the Prophet responded

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.speaker: God
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.claim: In a hadith qudsī, God responds to the servant’s praise, magnification, and glorification during the prayer, which is divided between them.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.anchor: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.claim: The Fātiḥah is a prayer encapsulating metaphysical and eschatological realities and teaches the proper human disposition toward God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.anchor: the Fātiḥah is more than the confessional prayer of Muslims. It is a prayer that encapsulates all the metaphysical and eschatological realities

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.claim: Its structure moves from God’s nature in the first three verses, through the God-human relationship, to human states in the final three.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.anchor: The Fātiḥah thus has a threefold structure: the first three verses deal with the nature of God, the middle verse deals with the relationship between God and human beings

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.claim: A report says nothing like the Fātiḥah was revealed in the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, or Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.anchor: In one the Prophet says, “By Him in Whose Hand lies my soul, in neither the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel, nor the Quran was the like of it revealed”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.claim: One attribution says Satan was frightened when the Fātiḥah was revealed, among four events; others attribute the saying to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.anchor: attributed by some to Mujāhid (Q) and by

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.claim: The Fātiḥah’s exalted status generated many independent commentaries, often showing how the Quran as a whole is contained in it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.anchor: The exalted status of the Fātiḥah has resulted in numerous independent commentaries upon it, some numbering hundreds of pages

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī compresses the Quran into the Fātiḥah, the basmalah, its opening bāʾ, and the diacritical point beneath it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.anchor: a famous saying attributed to ʿAlī ibn AbīṬālib

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.claim: The point beneath bāʾ can symbolize the Divine Pen’s first drop of ink, which inscribed all archetypes on the Preserved Tablet before creation; thus basmalah marks both Quranic and cosmic beginnings.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.anchor:
This point can be understood to represent the first
drop of ink

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r1.claim: After asking for help in obedience, the worshipper asks for perseverance and firmness in truth, as God guides believers through faith (10:9).
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r1.anchor: guide us can be understood as a prayer for perseverance in following the straight path and thus for continued aid

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r2.claim: Guidance can mean desire for intimacy, nearness, knowledge, and love of God; mystics paraphrase it as directing hearts and aspirations toward Him and from Him.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r2.anchor: The request for guidance also implies seeking to be led to God Himself and thus a desire for intimacy with Him

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r3.claim: Intellectually, the straight path means using God-given intelligence correctly to reach truth instead of reasoning toward error.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r3.anchor: following the straight path can be understood to mean using one’s God-given intelligence correctly in order to reach the truth

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r4.claim: The straight path is a clear, uncurved road; religiously it is a middle way joining outward Law and inward spirituality, with outer servitude and inner freedom.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r4.anchor: From a religious perspective, it is a middle way that avoids worldliness, on the one hand, and extreme asceticism, on the other

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r5.claim: The Prophet guides his community on this path; the Muslim community is a middle community in all dimensions of life.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r5.anchor: middle community (2:143) that follows a middle way in action

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r6.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r6.claim: A prophetic parable identifies the path as Islam, its walls as God’s limits, doors as prohibitions, the gate-caller as the Book, and the caller above as divine admonition in the heart.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r6.anchor: The straight path is Islam, the two walls are the limits set by God, while the doors refer to what God has prohibited

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r7.claim: Commentators identify the path with the Quran, Islam, or the Prophet; Shiite readings identify ʿAlī or the Prophet and Imams, while Sunni accounts name the Prophet and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r7.anchor: Some see the straight path as a reference to the Quran itself (Ṭ, Ṭū, Ṭs), while others say that it refers to Islam

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r8.claim: The path can mean walking with God toward God: God guides believers to Himself (4:175), while God Himself is on a straight path (11:56).
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r8.anchor: To be on the straight path, or a straight path as it is usually presented in the Quran, can also be understood as walking with God to God

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r9.claim: The straight path is also interpreted as the post-Judgment traverse across which beings pass at varying speeds, with some falling into Hellfire.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r9.anchor: The straight path is also understood as a reference to the traverse that human beings and jinn must cross as the final stage of Judgment

STUDYQURAN:1:6/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r10.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r10.claim: The Prophet describes the traverse as finer than a hair and sharper than a sword, crossed at varying speeds or ending in a fall to Hell.
STUDYQURAN:1:6/r10.anchor: According to the Prophet, this traverse is “finer than a hair and sharper than a sword”

TAB-FULL:v1p167/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r1.claim: Here ask God to grant steadfastness on the straight path: future success in obedience, right judgment, and avoiding what He forbids, like the request for help in the remaining lifetime.
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r1.anchor: في هذا الموضع عندنا: وفقنا للثبات عليه

TAB-FULL:v1p167/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r2.claim: In Gabriel's explanation to Muhammad, the request means that God inspire them with the guiding way; al-Ṭabarī equates this inspiration with granting success.
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r2.anchor: قل يا محمد {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} [الفاتحة: 6] ، يقول: ألهمنا الطريق الهادي

TAB-FULL:v1p167/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r3.claim: The complete prayer asks to worship God alone, receive help to worship, and be granted the way and method given to God's favored prophets and obedient servants; Arabic poetic usage also makes guidance mean success in a request.
TAB-FULL:v1p167/r3.anchor: اللهم إياك نعبد وحدك لا شريك لك، مخلصين لك العبادة دون ما سواك

TAB-FULL:v1p168/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r1.claim: When God says He does not guide wrongdoers, He means He does not grant them success or open their hearts to truth and faith, not that He withholds clarification of duties, which He gave all accountable people.
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r1.anchor: أنه لا يوفقهم، ولا يشرح للحق والإيمان صدورهم

TAB-FULL:v1p168/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r2.claim: The interpretation increase our guidance cannot mean more explanation: God never imposes a duty before explaining it and establishing proof, so this would make the prayer ask for already-provided explanation or for new duties.
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r2.anchor: لأن الله جل ثناؤه لا يكلف عبدا فرضا من فرائضه إلا بعد تبيينه له وإقامة الحجة عليه به

TAB-FULL:v1p168/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r3.claim: If increase our guidance means more aid and success, it concerns future deeds, since no help is needed for a completed act; that is precisely his interpretation, and it refutes the Qadari claim that the commanded already have all needed aid.
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r3.anchor: أن معنى مسألة تلك الزيادة إنما هو مسألته الزيادة لما يحدث من عمله

TAB-FULL:v1p168/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r4.claim: Some interpret the request as lead us along the path to Paradise in the afterlife, meaning take us there and make us arrive; they compare it with being guided to the path of Hell and with leading a woman to her husband or a gift to its recipient.
TAB-FULL:v1p168/r4.anchor: أسلكنا طريق الجنة في المعاد، أي قدمنا له وامض بنا إليه

TAB-FULL:v1p170/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r1.claim: Arabic uses hadā with a direct object, with li-, or with ilā- for directing someone to a path; Qur'anic and poetic usage confirms these equivalent constructions, including omission of a preposition in analogous verbs.
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r1.anchor: والعرب تقول: هديت فلانا الطريق، وهديته للطريق، وهديته إلى الطريق

TAB-FULL:v1p170/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r2.claim: He rejects interpreting the straight path as a way to Paradise in the afterlife: the Prophet's request for aid in worship and the consensus of Companions and Successors show this is a request to remain guided during life.
TAB-FULL:v1p170/r2.anchor: وذلك أن جميع المفسرين من الصحابة والتابعين مجمعون على أن معنى الصراط في هذا الموضع غير المعنى الذي تأوله

TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r1.claim: Exegetes unanimously define the straight path as a clear, unbending way, as Arabic poetry by Jarīr, Abū Dhuʾayb, and a rajaz poet illustrates; Arabs extend the term to any speech or deed described as straight or crooked.
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r1.anchor: أجمعت الأمة من أهل التأويل جميعا على أن الصراط المستقيم هو الطريق الواضح الذي لا اعوجاج فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r2.claim: The request means grant steadfastness in the words and deeds God approved and granted to the favored; this is Islam, belief in messengers, holding to Scripture, obeying commands, avoiding prohibitions, following Muhammad and the rightly guided caliphs, and every righteous servant's way.
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r2.anchor: وفقنا للثبات على ما ارتضيته ووفقت له من أنعمت عليه من عبادك، من قول وعمل

TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r3.speaker: علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r3.claim: Ali reports from the Prophet that the Qur'an is the straight path.
TAB-FULL:v1p170#2/r3.anchor: قال وذكر القرآن فقال: «هو الصراط المستقيم»

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r1.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r1.claim: Ali says the straight path is God's Book.

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also identifies the straight path as God's Book.
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله: «الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله»

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r3.claim: Jābir identifies the straight path with Islam and says it is broader than the distance between heaven and earth.
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r3.anchor: قال: الإسلام، قال: هو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Gabriel's gloss, calls it God's religion, the guiding way without crookedness.
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r4.anchor: يقول ألهمنا الطريق الهادي وهو دين الله الذي لا عوج له

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the concise gloss Islam.

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r6.speaker: ابن الحنفية
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r6.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya calls it God's religion, the only religion accepted from His servants.
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r6.anchor: قال: هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره

TAB-FULL:v1p174/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r7.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح عن ابن عباس ومرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وأناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p174/r7.claim: The report assembled by al-Suddī from these authorities identifies the straight path as Islam.

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the straight path simply as the road.

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the path as God's Messenger and his two successors, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r2.anchor: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده: أبو بكر وعمر

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan affirms Abū al-ʿĀliya spoke truly and advised sincerely.
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r3.anchor: فذكرت ذلك للحسن، فقال: «صدق أبو العالية ونصح»

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identifies the straight path as Islam.

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نواس بن سمعان
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r5.claim: The Prophet gives the parable of a straight path and identifies the path as Islam.
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r5.anchor: ضرب الله مثلا صراطا مستقيما، والصراط: الإسلام

TAB-FULL:v1p176/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r6.claim: God calls it straight because it is correct and contains no error; he rejects the claim that it is named for leading its people straight to Paradise, contrary to all exegetes.
TAB-FULL:v1p176/r6.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله بالاستقامة، لأنه صواب لا خطأ فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Answering why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses if two contain its meanings: earlier scriptures each included only some meanings, while the Qur'an gathers all of them for Muhammad's community and adds many more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره جمع لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأمته بما أنزل إليه من كتابه معاني لم يجمعهن بكتاب

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: The Torah is admonition and detailed instruction, Psalms praise and glorification, and Gospel admonition and reminder, but none has a miracle proving its recipient; the Qur'an contains these meanings and more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل، والزبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير؛ لا معجزة في واحد منها

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Among the Qur'an's distinctive merits is its miraculous arrangement and composition: rhetoricians cannot compose even a sura as short as one of its chapters.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: نظمه العجيب، ورصفه الغريب، وتأليفه البديع، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.claim: Rahim guides believers to Gods special mercy, their happiness in the afterlife and meeting their Lord.
TABATABAI:1:1-5/r3.anchor: وهو الرحيم يبين لهم سبيل رحمته الخاصة بالمؤمنين وهو سعادة آخرتهم ولقاء ربهم

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.claim: Straight path, road, and way are near synonyms; the requested straight way is the route followed by those God blessed, and thus the goal of worship: that pure worship occur upon it.
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.anchor: فالصراط الذي من شأنه ذلك هو الذي سئل الهداية إليه وهو بمعنى الغاية للعبادة

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.claim: All creatures travel toward God and meet Him; the Qur'an distinguishes the straight way of worship from the opposing way of following Satan.

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.claim: The way of divine worship is near because God is near and responds to supplication, while those who disbelieve call from a distant place, making their destination far.
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.anchor: فبين تعالى أنه قريب من عباده وأن الطريق الأقرب إليه تعالى طريق عبادته ودعائه

TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.claim: The straight path is the believers' way, excluding the wrathful and the astray, but the believers themselves have ranks and divisions.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.anchor: يدل على أن نفس الطريق الأول أيضا يقع فيه انقسام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.claim: Proponents cite the verse saying the Prophet does not guide whom he loves to argue that his guidance differs from guidance belonging to God.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.anchor: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء

TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r3.claim: Citing the believing man from Pharaohs people who promises to guide his people, the author concludes guidance does not change meaning with transitivity.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r3.anchor: فالحق أنه لا يتفاوت معنى الهداية باختلاف التعدية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r1.claim: Striving on Gods path seeks its safety and removal of obstacles; striving in God seeks His face, and He guides each person according to individual readiness.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r1.anchor: فالمجاهد في الأول يريد سلامة السبيل ودفع العوائق عنه بخلاف المجاهد في الثاني فإنه إنما يريد وجه الله

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r2.claim: God guides a seeker through successive ways until He singles the servant out for Himself.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r2.anchor: وكذا يمده الله تعالى بالهداية إلى السبيل بعد السبيل حتى يختصه بنفسه جلت عظمته

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r3.claim: Since the straight path is preserved within ways of different ranks, God may guide someone from one way to a higher one; guidance is then progress, not repetition.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r3.anchor: ثم يزيد في هدايته فيهتدي من ذلك السبيل إلى ما هو فوقها درجة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r4.claim: The verse asking for the straight path is spoken by someone already guided through worship, which supports the possibility of further guidance.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r4.anchor: عمن هداه بالعبادة من هذا القبيل

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.claim: A follower of the final, fullest law may still be below Noah or Abraham in realized divine knowledge and spiritual station; asking for the latter's rank is therefore coherent.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك إلا أن حكم الشرائع والعمل بها غير حكم الولاية الحاصلة من التمكن فيها والتخلق بها

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.claim: Some commentators answer that religion and core beliefs are one across revelations, while the final law has wider legal coverage and earlier communities serve as examples because they preceded us.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.anchor: أن دين الله واحد وهو الإسلام، والمعارف الأصلية وهي التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.claim: The author rejects that answer's assumptions that spiritual realities have no degrees and prophets equal ordinary believers in real perfection, with rank arising only from legislated status.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.anchor: فأفضل الأنبياء المقربين مع أخس المؤمنين من حيث الوجود وكماله الخارجي التكويني على حد سواء

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.claim: He traces that error to materialism or to neglecting reflective Qur'anic interpretation in favor of ordinary surface understanding.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.anchor: إما القول بالاكتفاء بالحس اعتمادا على العلوم المادية وإما إلغاء التدبر في القرآن

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r1.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r1.claim: Al-Sadiq explains asking for the straight path as seeking direction to persist on the way to God's love and Paradise, protected from destructive desires and opinions.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r1.anchor: يعني أرشدنا إلى لزوم الطريق المؤدي إلى محبتك، والمبلغ إلى جنتك

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r2.claim: The two transmitted explanations answer why the already guided ask guidance differently: one invokes distinct actual ranks and the other continuity in one concept.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r2.anchor: فالرواية الأولى ناظرة إلى اختلاف مراتب الهداية مصداقا والثانية إلى اتحادها مفهوما

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r3.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r3.claim: Ali asks God to sustain the success that enabled past obedience so that obedience continues through the rest of life; the author treats this as guidance's continued realization.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r3.anchor: أدم لنا توفيقك الذي أطعناك به في ماضي أيامنا، حتى نطيعك كذلك في مستقبل أعمارنا

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r4.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r4.claim: Ali defines the straight path in this life as balanced between excess and negligence, and in the afterlife as the believers' route to Paradise.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r4.anchor: الصراط المستقيم في الدنيا ما قصر عن الغلو، وارتفع عن التقصير

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.claim: The Prophet transmits God's division of al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: each phrase receives divine acknowledgement and a tailored promise of blessing, mercy, ease of judgment, reward, help, and fulfillment of the servant's requests.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.anchor: قسمت فاتحة الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي، ولعبدي ما سأل

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the whole Fātiḥa is divine speech voiced on the worshipper’s behalf as praise and confession of servitude in prayer.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.anchor: السورة بتمامها كلام تكلم به الله سبحانه في مقام النيابة عن عبده فيما يقوله إذا وجه وجهه إلى مقام الربوبية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.claim: The Fātiḥa is uniquely divided: one half belongs to God and the other half to the servant.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.anchor: أنها مقسمة قسمين، فنصف منها لله ونصف منها للعبد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.claim: In a concise, clear form, the Fātiḥa contains the Qurʾān’s central teachings, branches, promises, warnings, stories, and guidance.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.anchor: تشتمل على جميعها في أوجز لفظ وأوضح معنى

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.claim: Al-Ṣadūq reports a similar narration from al-Riḍā; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says it supports his reading of the Fātiḥa as prayer speech for the worshipper.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.anchor: وروى قريبا منه الصدوق في العلل عن الرضا عليه السلام، والرواية كما ترى تفسر سورة الفاتحة في الصلاة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.claim: He contrasts the Fātiḥa with the Christian Lord’s Prayer, criticizing its father-language, political-sounding petitions, reciprocal forgiveness, and requests to escape testing as incoherent with earthly life as a trial.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.anchor: ولكن من الذي يستجيب هذا الدعاء الذي هو بشعارات الأحزاب السياسية أشبه؟

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.claim: He objects that asking God to exchange forgiveness for forgiveness makes overlooking right conditional, and that asking to avoid trial misunderstands life as a place of testing and growth.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.anchor: فالدار دار الامتحان والاستكمال وما معنى النجاة لولا الابتلاء والامتحان

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.claim: He questions the claim that Islam has no intellectual superiority because all divine laws teach monotheism, virtue, and good deeds, leaving only social fruits to distinguish religions.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.anchor: إن جميع شرائع الله تدعو إلى التوحيد وتصفية النفوس بالخلق الفاضل والعمل الصالح، وإنما تتفاضل الأديان في عراقة ثمراتها الاجتماعية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r8.claim: Al-Ṣādiq identifies the straight path with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r8.anchor: بحث آخر روائي في الفقيه وتفسير العياشي عن الصادق عليه السلام قال الصراط المستقيم أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r1.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r1.claim: Al-Ṣādiq calls the straight path the road to knowing God, with a worldly path and an afterlife path; in this world it is the obligatory imam, whose guidance leads across Hell’s bridge.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r1.anchor: وفي المعاني عن الصادق عليه السلام قال هي الطريق إلى معرفة الله، وهما صراطان صراط في الدنيا وصراط في الآخرة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r2.speaker: السجاد عليه السلام
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r2.claim: Al-Sajjād says the Imams are God’s gates and straight path, repositories of knowledge, interpreters of revelation, pillars of monotheism, and repositories of divine secrets.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r2.anchor: عن السجاد عليه السلام قال ليس بين الله وبين حجته حجاب، ولا لله دون حجته ستر، نحن أبواب الله ونحن الصراط المستقيم

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the prayer as asking to be guided to love Muḥammad and his family.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } ، قال قولوا معاشر العباد! أرشدنا إلى حب محمد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r4.claim: He treats these identifications as jary: applications naming instances covered by the verse, not restrictions on its meaning.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r4.anchor: وهذه الأخبار من قبيل الجري، وعد المصداق للآية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r5.claim: In a report conveyed by al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, al-Bāqir says a verse has an outward revelation and inward interpretation, some realized in the past and some later, recurring as the sun and moon do.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r5.anchor: عن الفضيل بن يسار قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن هذه الرواية، ما في القرآن آية إلا ولها ظهر وبطن

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r6.claim: The Imams apply Qurʾānic verses to valid cases beyond the original occasion because the Qurʾān guides all people in belief, ethics, and action, and its truths and laws are not time-bound.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r6.anchor: القرآن نزل هدى للعالمين يهديهم إلى واجب الاعتقاد وواجب الخلق وواجب العمل

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r7.claim: An occasion of revelation does not confine a general ruling to its initiating event: praise and blame attach to qualities that can recur in later people.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r7.anchor: لا يوجب قصر الحكم على الواقعة لينقضي الحكم بانقضائها ويموت بموتها لأن البيان عام والتعليل مطلق

TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r8.claim: The Qurʾān itself provides evidence for the principle that its guidance applies beyond an original occasion of revelation.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#13/r8.anchor: والقرآن أيضا يدل عليه، قال تعالى

TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.claim: Reports applying Qurʾānic verses to the Imams or their enemies are abundant, sometimes numbering in the hundreds, so he generally omits them unless useful to the discussion.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.anchor: ربما تبلغ المئين، ونحن بعد هذا التنبيه العام نترك إيراد أكثرها في الأبحاث الروائية لخروجها عن الغرض في الكتاب

TABRISI:1:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
TABRISI:1:6/r1.claim: Readers differ on ṣirāṭ: Hamza's recitation colors ṣād toward zāy, a route of al-Kisa'i uses sīn, Yaqub's route uses sīn, and the rest use ṣād.
TABRISI:1:6/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة باشمام الصاد الزاي إلا العجلي وبرواية خلاد وابن سعدان يشم ههنا في الموضعين فقط

TABRISI:1:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6/r2.claim: The etymological form is sīn from saraṭ; sīn preserves the root, ṣād agrees with emphatic ṭā and avoids moving from a low to high articulation, while zāy signals voicing without erasing the root.
TABRISI:1:6/r2.anchor: الأصل في الصراط السين لأنه مشتق من السرط ومسترط الطعام ممره ومنه قولهم سر طراط

TABRISI:1:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6/r3.claim: Hidaya can mean guidance and direction, or success granted by God, as the cited poetry illustrates.
TABRISI:1:6/r3.anchor: الهداية في اللغة الإرشاد والدلالة على الشيء يقال لمن يتقدم القوم

TABRISI:1:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6/r4.claim: Ṣirāṭ is a broad, clear road; mustaqīm means straight without crookedness, and a verse by Jarir illustrates this sense.
TABRISI:1:6/r4.anchor: والصراط: الطريق الواضح المتسع وسمي بذلك لأنه يسرط المارة

TABRISI:1:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6/r5.claim: In the imperative ihdinā, God is the understood agent, the attached pronoun is the first object, and ṣirāṭ is the second object.
TABRISI:1:6/r5.anchor: اهدنا مبني على الوقف وفاعله الضمير المستكن فيه لله تعالى والهمزة مكسورة

TABRISI:1:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6/r6.claim: One interpretation is keep us firm in true religion: people may already be guided yet need steadiness and increased guidance to resist errors and passing thoughts.
TABRISI:1:6/r6.anchor: أن معناه ثبتنا على الدين الحق لأن الله تعالى قد هدى الخلق كلهم إلا أن الإنسان قد يزل

TABRISI:1:6#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6#2/r1.claim: A second interpretation takes guidance as reward and asks to be guided to Paradise as recompense for faith.

TABRISI:1:6#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6#2/r2.claim: A third interpretation asks God to guide the speaker in the future as He did in the past; prayer for what will occur is still worship and dependence.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r2.anchor: وثالثها: أن المراد دلنا على الدين الحق

TABRISI:1:6#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6#2/r3.claim: Asking for already-given guidance can benefit religion, obtain benefits that depend on asking, or request continued obligation and the opportunity for reward, which is a divine favor.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون لنا في الدعاء به مصلحة في ديننا وهذا كما تعبدنا بأن نكرر التسبيح والتحميد

TABRISI:1:6#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r4.speaker: النبي وعلي وابن مسعود
TABRISI:1:6#2/r4.claim: The straight path is identified as God's Book in reports from the Prophet, Ali, and Ibn Masud.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r4.anchor: أنه كتاب الله وهو المروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن علي ع وابن مسعود

TABRISI:1:6#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r5.speaker: جابر وابن عباس
TABRISI:1:6#2/r5.claim: Jabir and Ibn Abbas identify the straight path as Islam.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r5.anchor: أنه الإسلام وهو المروي عن جابر وابن عباس

TABRISI:1:6#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
TABRISI:1:6#2/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya identifies it as God's religion, the only religion He accepts from people.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r6.anchor: أنه دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره عن محمد بن الحنفية

TABRISI:1:6#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6#2/r7.claim: A report in the author's tradition identifies the path as the Prophet and the Imams who succeed him.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r7.anchor: أنه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والأئمة القائمون مقامه وهو المروي في أخبارنا

TABRISI:1:6#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:6#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:6#2/r8.claim: The author prefers a general meaning encompassing all these views: the commanded religion of monotheism, justice, and loyalty to those whose obedience God requires.
TABRISI:1:6#2/r8.anchor: والأولى حمل الآية على العموم حتى يدخل جميع ذلك فيه لأن الصراط المستقيم هو الدين الذي أمر الله به من التوحيد والعدل

THALABI:v1p118#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v1p118#2/r1.claim: Ali and Ubayy understand the plea as asking to remain guided, like telling an eater to eat or a reader to continue reading.
THALABI:v1p118#2/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب (كرم الله وجهه) وأبي بن كعب: أرشدتنا فهذا كما يقال للرجل الذي يأكل: كل

THALABI:v1p118#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118#2/r2.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p118#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil gloss ihdinā as guide us to the path.
THALABI:v1p118#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي ومقاتل: أرشدنا، يقال: هديته للدين وهديته الى الدين

THALABI:v1p118#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118#2/r3.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p118#2/r3.claim: One Qurʾanic sense of guidance is calling and clarification, as in the Prophet guiding to a straight path and each people having a guide.
THALABI:v1p118#2/r3.anchor: الوجه الأول: هدى دعاء وبيان كقوله: وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم

THALABI:v1p118#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118#2/r4.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p118#2/r4.claim: A second sense is enabling and directing by God, as in verses saying God guides or misguides whom He wills and that the Prophet cannot guide whom he loves.
THALABI:v1p118#2/r4.anchor: الوجه الثاني: هدى توفيق وتسديد كقوله: يضل من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء

THALABI:v1p118#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p118#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p118#2/r5.claim: The straight path is a clear, level road; verses by ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl and Jarīr illustrate the term.
THALABI:v1p118#2/r5.anchor:
والصراط المستقيم الطريق الواضح المستوي، قال عامر بن الطفيل:
خشونا أرضهم بالخيل

THALABI:v1p119/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p119/r1.claim: The original form of ṣirāṭ is with sīn, reflecting the idea that the road swallows passersby; Ibn ʿAbbās read it this way, as did Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb through cited routes.
THALABI:v1p119/r1.anchor: بالسين وهو الأصل، سمي الطريق سراطا لأنه يسترط المارة. أخبرنا عبد الله بن حامد

THALABI:v1p119/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r2.speaker: أبو حمدون عن الكسائي
THALABI:v1p119/r2.claim: One transmitted reading gives ṣirāṭ an imāla-like sīn pronunciation (ishmām).
THALABI:v1p119/r2.anchor: وبإشمام السين وهي رواية أبي حمدون عن الكسائي

THALABI:v1p119/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r3.speaker: أبو حمدون عن سليم عن حمزة
THALABI:v1p119/r3.claim: A transmitted reading pronounces the sīn as zāy.
THALABI:v1p119/r3.anchor: وبالزاي وهي رواية أبي حمدون عن سليم عن حمزة

THALABI:v1p119/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r4.speaker: حمزة
THALABI:v1p119/r4.claim: Hamza in most transmissions and al-Kisāʾī in two routes use ishām of zāy.
THALABI:v1p119/r4.anchor: وبإشمام الزاي وهي قراءة حمزة في أكثر الروايات والكسائي في رواية نهشل والشيرازي

THALABI:v1p119/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p119/r5.claim: The remaining canonical readers pronounce ṣād.

THALABI:v1p119/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p119/r6.claim: All five pronunciations are sound Arabic, but ṣād is preferred because every codex writes it that way and ṣād and ṭāʾ share emphatic articulation.
THALABI:v1p119/r6.anchor: وكلها لغات فصيحة صحيحة إلا إن الاختيار الصاد لموافقة المصحف

THALABI:v1p119/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r7.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p119/r7.claim: The Prophet identified the straight path as God's Book.
THALABI:v1p119/r7.anchor: عن الحرث عن علي قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم [يقول] : «الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله عز وجل» .

THALABI:v1p119/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r8.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v1p119/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also glossed the straight path as God's Book.
THALABI:v1p119/r8.anchor: عن أبي وائل عن عبد الله قال: الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله عز وجل.

THALABI:v1p119/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r9.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v1p119/r9.claim: Jābir calls the straight path Islam, wider than the space between heaven and earth, since other religions and paths are not straight.
THALABI:v1p119/r9.anchor: عن أبي عقيل عن جابر قال: الصراط المستقيم الإسلام، وهو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

THALABI:v1p119/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p119/r10.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
THALABI:v1p119/r10.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says it is the path of the Prophet and his two companions.
THALABI:v1p119/r10.anchor: وروى عاصم الأحول عن أبي العالية الرياحي: هو طريق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه .

THALABI:v1p120/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p120/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan affirms that Abū al-ʿĀliya spoke truth and gave sound counsel.
THALABI:v1p120/r1.anchor: قال عاصم: فذكرت ذلك للحسن فقال: صدق أبو العالية ونصح

THALABI:v1p120/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r2.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
THALABI:v1p120/r2.claim: In a dream, the Prophet told Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the straight path is his Sunna and that of the rightly guided caliphs after him.
THALABI:v1p120/r2.anchor: وقال بكر بن عبد الله المزني: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام، فسألته عن الصراط المستقيم

THALABI:v1p120/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v1p120/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses the path as the way of truth.
THALABI:v1p120/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: يعني طريق [الحق

THALABI:v1p120/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r4.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p120/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says it is the religion that brings its follower to Paradise without punishment and directly from the grave to Paradise.
THALABI:v1p120/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: أرشدنا إلى دين يدخل صاحبه به الجنة ولا يعذب في النار أبدا

THALABI:v1p120/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r5.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
THALABI:v1p120/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya identifies it as God's religion, the only religion He accepts from servants.
THALABI:v1p120/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية: هو دين [الله] الذي لا يقبل من عباده غيره

THALABI:v1p120/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r6.speaker: أبو بريدة
THALABI:v1p120/r6.claim: Abū Burayda glosses it as the path of Muḥammad and his family.
THALABI:v1p120/r6.anchor: عن أبي بريدة في قول الله تعالى: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم قال: صراط محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وآله (عليهم السلام) .

THALABI:v1p120/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r7.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
THALABI:v1p120/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā says it means the path of the great majority.
THALABI:v1p120/r7.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى: يعني طريق السواد الأعظم

THALABI:v1p120/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r8.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v1p120/r8.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq defines it as a path whose directions are not bent right or left by whims.
THALABI:v1p120/r8.anchor: وقال] أبو بكر الوراق: يعني صراطا لا تزيغ به الأهواء يمينا وشمالا

THALABI:v1p120/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r9.speaker: محمد بن علي النهدي
THALABI:v1p120/r9.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Nahdī calls it the path of fear and hope.
THALABI:v1p120/r9.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي النهدي: يعني طريق الخوف والرجاء

THALABI:v1p120/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r10.speaker: أبو عثمان الداراني
THALABI:v1p120/r10.claim: Abū ʿUthmān al-Dārānī glosses it as the path of servitude to God.
THALABI:v1p120/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان الداراني: [يعني] طريق العبودية

THALABI:v1p120/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r11.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
THALABI:v1p120/r11.claim: Sahl al-Tustarī calls it the path of Sunna and community, because innovation cannot be straight.
THALABI:v1p120/r11.anchor: سمعت [سهل] بن عبد الله التستري يقول: طريق السنة والجماعة لأن البدعة لا تكون مستقيمة

THALABI:v1p120/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p120/r12.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p120/r12.claim: The Prophet drew one line for God's path and two side lines for other paths, each with a devil calling to it, then recited the command to follow God's straight path alone.
THALABI:v1p120/r12.anchor: عن أبي وائل عن عبد الله قال: خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطين، خطا عن يمينه وخطا عن شماله ثم قال: «هذه السبل،

THALABI:v1p121/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p121/r1.claim: A prophetic parable identifies the straight path as Islam; its curtains are God's limits, open doors are His prohibitions, the caller on the path is the Qurʾān, and the caller above is God's inner adviser in each Muslim.
THALABI:v1p121/r1.anchor: ضرب الله مثلا (صراطا مستقيما) وعلى جانبي الصراط ستور مرخاة فيها أبواب مفتحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says hadā-hu in religion means to guide him, while hadā-hu hidāya means to point someone to a road.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r1.anchor: قال الأصمعي: هداه في الدين يهديه هدى (¬2)، وهداه يهديه هداية، إذا دله على الطريق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r2.claim: The root meaning of guidance is indication; the leaders of horses and wild herds are called hawādī because they go in front to show the way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518/r2.anchor: وأصل الهداية في اللغة: الدلالة. وهوادي الخيل والوحش التي تتقدم للدلالة (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r1.claim: The term hādī broadened from a guide who leads by indication to any forerunner, including the leading animals, the neck, and a staff ahead of a traveler.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r1.anchor: هذا هو الأصل، ثم سمي كل متقدم هاديا وإن لم يتقدم للدلالة (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r2.claim: Poetic examples from ʿUbayd, Ṭarafa, and al-Aʿshā use guidance for leading, limbs that lead movement, and a staff that either precedes or directs its bearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r2.anchor:
وقول طرفة:
للفتى عقل يعيش به ... حيث تهدي ساقه (¬4) قدمه (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r3.claim: The verb hadā takes two objects and connects the second with ilā or lām, as illustrated in 37:23, 38:22, 7:43, and 10:35; awḥā behaves similarly in 16:68 and 99:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r3.anchor: والفعل من (الهدى) (¬4) يتعدى إلى مفعولين، ويتعدى إلى الثاني بأحد حرفي جر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r4.claim: The preposition before the second object can be omitted, as in 1:6; ihdinā al-ṣirāṭ means guide us to it and make us follow it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r4.anchor: وقد يحذف حرف الجر من المفعول الثاني في (الهدى) فيصل الفعل إليه بغير حرف جر (¬9).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r5.claim: Already guided believers still ask because a knower may encounter doubts that lead back to ignorance, so they request a subtle divine aid that preserves knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r5.anchor: قد تعرض للعارف شبه ينتقل بها إلى الجهل، فيحسن أن يسأل اللطيفة التي يتمسك معها بالمعرفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r6.claim: They also do not know their future state, so they ask for confirmation in the truth they presently follow; guidance can mean steadfastness rather than rescue from error.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r6.anchor: لما كانوا لا يعلمون ما يكون منهم في المستأنف، حسن أن يسألوا الهداية على (¬2) وجه التثبيت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa's prayer that God guide ʿUmar is a wish for success and firmness, not a taunt that he is astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p518#2/r7.anchor: وقد تستعمل الهداية لا من الضلالة كما قال الحطيئة لعمر رضي الله عنه:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r1.speaker: some of our companions
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r1.claim: Some scholars say believers ask for future guidance because guidance is an accident that does not endure, so they ask God to create its likeness anew.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r1.anchor: وقال بعض أصحابنا: يجوز أن يحمل على سؤال الهداية ابتداء فيما # يستقبل؛ لأن الهداية عرض لا يبقى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r2.speaker: some scholars
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r2.claim: Others treat the prayer as claiming the fulfillment of God's promise in 5:16 to guide those who follow His pleasure toward paths of peace.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا سؤال، واستنجاز لما وعدوا به في قوله: {يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r3.claim: Ṣirāṭ has reported recitations with sīn, ṣād, zāy, and an intermediate ṣād-zāy pronunciation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r3.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الصراط} [الفاتحة: 6] (¬3)، فيه لغات قد قرئ بها: السين، والصاد،
