WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r4.speaker: readers of sīn
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r4.claim: The sīn readers derive the word from istirāṭ, swallowing, because the road swallows travelers; they say a ṣād before ṭāʾ would hide the root.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r4.anchor: فمن قرأ بالسين فإنه يقول: هو أصل الكلمة؛ لأنه من الاستراط بمعنى: الابتلاع (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r5.speaker: readers of ṣād
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r5.claim: The ṣād readers say it is lighter and sounds better beside ṭāʾ because both are emphatic, unlike sīn, which is voiceless and farther from ṭāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r5.anchor: ويقول من يقرأ بالصاد: إنها أخف # على اللسان، لأن (الصاد) حرف مطبق ك (الطاء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r6.speaker: readers of zāy
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r6.claim: The zāy reading replaces sīn with a voiced sound, closer to ṭāʾ and light to articulate; they cite the Arab variant zaqr for ṣaqr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r6.anchor: ويقول من قرأ بالزاي: أبدلت منها حرفا مجهورا (¬2) حتى يشبه (الطاء) في الجهر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r7.speaker: readers of intermediate ṣād-zāy
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r7.claim: Those who blend ṣād and zāy seek ease without making either pure sound and thereby confusing the word's root.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r7.anchor: ويقول من قرأ بالمضارعة (¬4): رمت الخفة، ولم أجعلها (زايا) خالصة، ولا (صادا) خالصة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r8.speaker: ابن السراج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r8.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj prefers ṣād for ease, euphony, and clarity; it is also the majority recitation, while pure zāy is unrecognized and should not control recitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r8.anchor: قال ابن السراج (¬6): الاختيار (الصاد) للخفة والحسن في السمع، وهو غير ملتبس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r9.speaker: ابن السراج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r9.claim: He rejects the intermediate sound as a difficult, ad hoc articulation that is not an independent letter or a normal building block of words.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r9.anchor: وأما المضارعة (¬10) فهو تكلف حرف بين حرفين، وذلك أصعب على # اللسان؛ لأنه إنما استعمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r10.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r10.claim: The author of al-Ḥujja argues ṣād is preferable because sīn before emphatic ṭāʾ creates an unwanted rise in articulation, as speakers already replace sīn with ṣād before qāf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r10.anchor: وقال صاحب "الحجة" (¬1): الحجة لمن قرأ بالصاد: أن (¬2) السين مضارعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r11.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r11.claim: Replacing sīn with ṣād is even more apt before ṭāʾ than before qāf because ṣād is closer to ṭāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p521/r11.anchor: فلأن يبدلوا منها (الصاد) مع (الطاء) # أجدر (¬1) من حيث كانت (الصاد) إلى (الطاء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r1.claim: Istiqāma means straightness and continuation along one direction: qāma is to stand upright, aqāma to straighten, and qāwama to match in strength.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {المستقيم}: (الاستقامة) في اللغة: الاستواء، يقال: قام إذا استوى منتصبا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r2.speaker: علي وابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r2.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd from the Prophet identifies the straight path as God's Book; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r2.anchor: فروى علي وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: "الصراط المستقيم: كتاب الله عز وجل"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r3.speaker: جابر ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r3.claim: Jābir and Muqātil say the straight path is Islam.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r4.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī says it is the way of the Messenger and the two who succeeded him, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r4.anchor: وعن أبي العالية الرياحي (¬2)، قال: هو طريق رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وصاحبيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r5.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r5.claim: In a dream report, Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī asks the Prophet about the straight path and is told it is his Sunna and that of the rightly guided caliphs; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r5.anchor: وقال بكر بن عبد الله المزني (¬1): رأيت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في المنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r6.claim: The theologians of meaning say true religion is called the straight path because it reaches God's pleasure and lasting bliss, as a straight road reaches its destination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p528/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: إنما وصف الدين الحق (¬3) بأنه الصراط المستقيم؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى الغرض المطلوب

WAHIDI-QT:1:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:6/r1.claim: The prayer asks God to show the straight path, lead the petitioner along it, and keep him firm upon it.
WAHIDI-QT:1:6/r1.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم أي دلنا عليه واسلك بنا فيه وثبتنا عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r3.claim: The prayer asks God to show the straight path, lead the worshippers along it, and keep them firm upon it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r3.anchor: دلنا عليه، واسلك بنا فيه، وثبتنا عليه.

ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.claim: After the covenant, the prayer for guidance begins as the most comprehensive practical application of seeking divine aid; it answers the worshipper's need, after pausing at “we seek aid,” to know where and how to begin.
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r1.anchor: Bu talep ve dua isti‘ânenin ehem ve eşmel bir sûret-i tatbîkiyesiyle beyânıdır

ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.claim: Guidance is contained in seeking aid, which is contained in worship and praise; thus all of Fatiha unfolds as one complete الحمد لله sentence and unified discourse, so its first two pauses are complete but not obligatory.
ELMALILI:1:5#9/r2.anchor: bütün Fâtiha’nın bir اَلْحَمْدُ للّٰهِِّٰ cümle-i tâmmesinin inkişâfı olup sade başıyla değil hey’et-i mecmû‘asıyla kelâm-ı vâhid hâlinde

ELMALILI:1:6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r1.claim: The command form becomes an imperative from higher to lower, a supplication from lower to higher, and a request between equals.
ELMALILI:1:6/r1.anchor: Bu sîga ile yukarıdan aşağıya büyükten küçüğe cezmen vukū‘bulan taleb-i fiile “emir”, aşağıdan yukarıya yapılan talebe “dua”

ELMALILI:1:6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r2.claim: Guidance gently and delicately indicates how to reach a desired destination: it may show the way, take someone along it, or lead them all the way; showing is non-arriving direction (irshad), while taking there is tawfiq.
ELMALILI:1:6/r2.anchor: “Hidâyet” matlûba îsâl edecek şeye lutf u letâfetle delâlet etmektir ki yolu sadece gösterivermek veya yola götürüvermek

ELMALILI:1:6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r3.claim: Guidance concerns a good goal and gentle method; applying it to an evil destination, as in the direction to Hell, is figurative sarcasm or insinuation.
ELMALILI:1:6/r3.anchor: Hidâyet matlûb-i hayra mahsustur. Meselâ hırsıza yol göstermeye, rehberlik etmeye “hidâyet” denilmez

ELMALILI:1:6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r4.claim: The best Turkish rendering is the familiar “bize hidâyet et”: “show” omits leading, “take” omits gentleness, and replacing an established word with a strained alternative distorts the intended meaning.
ELMALILI:1:6/r4.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh ٱهْدِنَا’nın meâlinde en muvâfık tâbir lisânımızda mâruf olduğu gibi “bize hidâyet et” demektir

ELMALILI:1:6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r5.claim: Divine guidance is innumerable in both its particular forms and its kinds, but can be considered under four ordered general categories.
ELMALILI:1:6/r5.anchor: ‘add u ihsâ olmadığı gibi envâ‘ı itibariyle de öyledir

ELMALILI:1:6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r6.claim: One kind is bestowing and sustaining spiritual or bodily powers, senses, reason, will, and the natural or animal faculties that serve human needs, and aligning intentions with desires.
ELMALILI:1:6/r6.anchor: havâss-ı zâhire ve bâtınesini, kuvve-i akliye ve irâdiyesini ve hatta ef‘âl-i tabî‘iye ve hayvâniyesinin sudûruna sebep olan kuvâ-yı

ELMALILI:1:6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r7.claim: A second kind establishes proofs that distinguish truth from falsehood and right conduct from corruption; the Thamud were shown guidance but preferred blindness.
ELMALILI:1:6/r7.anchor: Hak ile bâtılı, salâh ile fesâdı fark ettiren delâil nasb u ikāme etmek

ELMALILI:1:6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r8.claim: A third kind guides through sending messengers and revealing scriptures, as with divinely guided leaders and the Qur'an's guidance to the soundest way.
ELMALILI:1:6/r8.anchor: İrsâl-i rusül ve inzâl-i kütüb ile hidâyet

ELMALILI:1:6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r9.claim: A fourth, special guidance unveils hidden realities to hearts through revelation, inspiration, or true dreams, especially for prophets and saints; others have a limited share below certainty, and guidance can also be summarized as inner or outer, creational or revealed.
ELMALILI:1:6/r9.anchor: Vahiy veya ilham veya rü’yâ-yı sâdıka gibi fevkalâde tarîklerle

ELMALILI:1:6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r10.claim: The contextual setting determines which sense of guidance a Qur'anic occurrence carries.
ELMALILI:1:6/r10.anchor: Kur’an’da “hidâyet” kelimesi kullanıldığı zaman, bunlardan hangisi murad olunabileceğini makamına göre anlamak iktizâ eder

ELMALILI:1:6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r11.claim: The verb may take its second object directly, as here, or with ilā; some grammarians explain the direct form as eliding the preposition for arrival, from an underlying “guide us to the path.”
ELMALILI:1:6/r11.anchor: Hidâyet mef‘ûl-i sânîsine kâh إل� ile, bazen de burada olduğu gibi bizzat ta‘diye eder

ELMALILI:1:6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r12.claim: Guidance and being guided are related; those already guided ask for steadfastness or a higher degree, while the previously unled ask to attain the basic guidance.
ELMALILI:1:6/r12.anchor: hidâyette bulunanların hidâyet istemesi de sebat veya ziyâde-i mertebe istemek olur

ELMALILI:1:6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r13.claim: The definite article on “the path” may mark a known covenant path belonging to God, or the generic class of road that metaphorically applies to God's path.
ELMALILI:1:6/r13.anchor: Hidâyetin ikinci mef‘ûlü, yani mef‘ûlün ileyhi olan ٱلصِّرَٰطَ lâm-ı ‘ahd ile صراطك “senin sırâtın” terkîb-i izâfîsinin mânasını ifade eder

ELMALILI:1:6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r14.claim: Most readings use ṣād as the Quraysh form, smoother and more eloquent due to emphatic sounds; Qunbul from Ibn Kathir and Ruways from Yaqub transmit sīn, while Hamza's ishmām hints at zāy in the Qays dialect (as Abu Hayyan reports).
ELMALILI:1:6/r14.anchor: İbn Kesîr’den Kunbul ve Ya‘kūb’dan Rüveys rivayetlerinde de böyle sin ile es-sirât (السراط), sirât okunur

ELMALILI:1:6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r15.claim: Although Arabic “sirat” means a great, busy highway, Turkish speakers know it as the required afterlife bridge over Hell; the text hints at that image and Amr ibn Ubayd transmitted that interpretation, but exegetes take its primary intent as a representative metaphor for truth and Islam.
ELMALILI:1:6/r15.anchor: Lâkin burada asıl murad bir isti‘âre-i temsîliye ile tarîk-i hak ve millet-i İslâm olduğunu müfessirîn-i kirâm beyan edegelmişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r16.claim: Arabic terms distinguish general road (tarīq), traveled road (sabīl), and busy, straight, great, or clear ways (including sirat and sharia); “sirat” therefore evokes sharia.

ELMALILI:1:6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6/r17.claim: Mustaqim means completely straight with no bend; because a road may still slope, the adjective adds flatness, so “straight” alone does not fully convey it, though Turkish also uses it for true or truthful.
ELMALILI:1:6/r17.anchor: “Müstakīm”, hiçbir yerinde meyil ve eğrilik bulunmayan dümdüz ve dosdoğru demektir

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r1.claim: Qur'anic rhetoric includes at least sixteen theoretically established categorical modes; suggestive, non-categorical rhetorical nuances are grasped through rhetoric's innumerable aesthetic judgments.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r1.anchor: Vücûh-i beyan kat‘iyyet nokta-i nazarıyla lâekal on altı vechi ihtivâ ettiği usûlen mâlumdur

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r2.claim: Chance is only an appearance to the ignorant; divine wisdom has no chance, and every choice by the all-wise has a weighting wisdom even though God's will is not externally compelled.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r2.anchor: Tesadüf müşâhede-i esrardan gāfil olan câhilin nazarındadır. Hikmette tesadüf yoktur ve Hakîm-i mutlakın her ihtiyârında bir hikmet-i mürecciha vardır

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r3.claim: To interpret Qur'anic wording, establish each word's sense, compare related alternatives, consider syntax and context, then distinguish intended meaning from rhetorical embellishment; separate a term's mental sense from its real referents, since this affects legal inference.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r3.anchor: evvelâ kelimelerin mefhumlarını iyice tesbit etmek, sâniyen mevki‘lerinde lafzen ve mânen alâkadar olabileceği kelimât ve me‘ânîsi ile mukayese eylemek

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r4.claim: Commentators transmit definitions including God's path, truth, a balanced way, God's Book, faith and its entailments, Islam and its law, the Prophet's and leading Companions' path, Sunna and the community, Paradise's road, and the bridge over Hell; investigators synthesize truth's path and Islam.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r4.anchor: Tefsirlere baktığımız zaman ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ’den murad ne olduğu hakkında şu rivayetleri görürüz

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r5.claim: Given the definite article's covenant or generic force, most transmitted explanations concern referents and some concern the concept; aside from Hell's bridge, they describe the same referent by attributes, so confusing sense with referent creates false disagreements.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r5.anchor: Cisr-i cehennem istisna edilirse öbürleri vâki‘de aynı medlûlün evsâfından biriyle ifadesinden başka bir şey olmadıkları hâlde

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r6.claim: The investigators' synthesis distinguishes concept from referent: “path of truth” gives the concept and Islam gives its real-world instance.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r6.anchor: Tarîk-i hak mefhum, millet-i İslâm mâsadaktır

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r7.claim: The second mention of “path” explains the first by apposition, which can be whole or partial; the intended focus remains the apposition, while the first phrase prepares and reinforces the meaning rather than being discarded.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r7.anchor: “صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ”, ٱلصِّرَٰطَ’tan bedeldir. Bedel-i kül veya ba‘z olabilir

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r8.claim: The following appositional clauses clarify the path's essence and attributes: those whom God favored, those not under anger, and those not astray.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r8.anchor: sırât-ı müstakīmin hem zâtını ve hem vasfını şerh u tavzih eden kayıtlar vardır

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r9.claim: The full appositional construction must be considered before the intended meaning and referent of the straight path can be determined.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r9.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ’den murad olan mâna ve mâsadak bunların hey’et-i mecmû‘ası mülâhaza edildikten sonra ta‘ayyün edecektir

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r10.claim: Lexically the term means a straight, level highway, but the discourse concerns seeking aid, an immaterial matter, so it must mean a spiritual road or explicitly include one figuratively.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r10.anchor: Bu ise gayr-i mahsüs bir mânadır. Binâen‘aleyh bu karîne-i kat‘iyye ile biz anlarız ki bu yol manevî yoldur

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r11.claim: The metaphor first imagines a clear, broad, busy, straight physical road, then a clear and comprehensive God-appointed intellectual and practical law safely directing human thought and action toward good goals, and finally uses “straight path” for that spiritual reality, clarified by “guide us.”
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r11.anchor: bizi doğruca ve selâmetle hayırlı muradlarımıza götürecek ilmî, amelî, vâzıh ve şümullü ve Hak teâlâ’nın vaz‘ı olan bir kānûn-ı hak tasavvur ediyoruz

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r12.claim: Whether every path that qualifies generally as a path of truth belongs to the requested straight path remains a question requiring consideration.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r12.anchor: tarîk-i hak ıtlâkına sezâ olan her tarîk, matlub olan tarîk-i müstakīme dâhil midir, değil midir?

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r13.claim: Because the preceding plea seeks aid, the first and most important request is guidance to a clear path that elicits divine aid; the passage therefore asks for God's most important assistance first.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r13.anchor: ibtidâ me‘ûnet-i ilâhiyenin ehemm u akdemini taleb etmemizi telkin ediyor

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r14.claim: Truth's broad meaning can encompass paths that lead to evil relative to created aims: each divine law leads to an objective, and some paths lead to God's pleasure while others lead to His wrath.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r14.anchor: lâkin birisi rızâsına götürür, biri de gazabına götürür

ELMALILI:1:6#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r15.claim: The requested path must therefore be defined as the path leading to God's pleasure; “the straight path” conveys a more specific and clearer meaning than the broad notion of a path of truth, and its appositional expansion identifies it fully with Islam.
ELMALILI:1:6#2/r15.anchor: İşte bütün bu ibhamları izâle için bedelin tezyîliyle mefhûmun mütenâveli tefsir veya tahsis olunmuş

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r1.claim: Because God is Lord of all worlds, His laws operate in every realm; laws may be named for their maker or their subject, but “divine laws” and “God's way” are more accurate for all of them.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r1.anchor: hepsinin vâzı‘ı Hak teâlâ olduğundan bunlara “kavânîn-i Hak” ve “sünnet-i ilâhiye” demek elbette daha doğrudur

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r2.claim: Knowing divine laws is science; laws that lead to good are religion, community, or sharia. Seeking religion outside divine ordinance is false, yet not every divine law is religion: the law that a suicide dies is real, but suicide is evil; good-conforming acts are religious, evil-conforming ones contrary to religion.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r2.anchor: Bu kanunları bilmeye “ilm u fen” denildiği gibi, onların hayra götürenlerine de “din”, “millet”, “şeri‘at” ıtlak olunur

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r3.claim: Human-made laws cannot constitute true science or religion; people should discover and reveal God's laws rather than legislate them. Archimedes, Newton, Aristotle, and Abu Hanifa discovered laws rather than inventing them.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r3.anchor: beşerin hakkı gerek ilimde ve gerek dinde kanun vaz‘etmek değil, Hakk’ın kanunlarını arayıp bulmak ve keşf u izhâr etmektir

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r4.claim: Since divinely established laws are straight, “straight path” also conveys a clear, busy main road for revealing hidden laws and avoiding crooked human inventions unrelated to divine aid.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r4.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ ise vâzıh mânasını dahi tazammun ettiğinden bunları izhâra vesile olacak vâzıh ve işlek bir tarîk-i esâsîyi ifham ediyor

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r5.claim: Guidance's orientation to good does not erase the laws that lead to evil; it frames good laws positively as commands and evil laws negatively as prohibitions, and the following verse's favored/not-angered/not-astray clauses show both aspects.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r5.anchor: hayr kanunlarını evâmir olarak müsbet ve şer kanunlarını nevâhî olarak menfî bir haysiyetle takyid etmeyi îcab edecektir

ELMALILI:1:6#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r6.claim: With the definite article marking the covenant path, verse 6 is a complete definition of the true religion and the following material explains it.
ELMALILI:1:6#3/r6.anchor: ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ lâm-ı ‘ahd ile dîn-i hakkın hadd-i tâmmıdır. Mâba‘di de bunun şerhidir

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r1.claim: In'am means giving and conveying a blessing; connecting it with “ala” conveys the Benefactor's exaltedness and the blessing's loftiness.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r1.anchor: “İn‘âm”, nimet vermek, nimeti îsâl etmektir. Aslında müte‘addîdir. Lâkin tafdil mânasını tazammun ile mün‘imin ulviyetini

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r2.claim: Ni'ma first means a pleasurable state or bliss and then anything that causes it; it relates to softness. A proverb says some have wealth but no enjoyment, like someone with bread who cannot taste it; true blessing includes the ability to enjoy.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r2.anchor: nice nimet sâhibi vardır ki tena‘‘umu yoktur. Meselâ ekmeği vardır yiyemez, yerse tadını bulamaz

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r3.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted; they may broadly be considered as worldly or afterlife blessings.

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r4.claim: Worldly blessings are bestowed or acquired: bestowed gifts include spiritual and bodily capacities, while acquired gifts include moral purification, knowledge, virtue, social standing, and wealth.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r4.anchor: Ni‘am-ı dünyeviye iki kısımdır: Vehbî, kesbî

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r5.claim: Afterlife blessings include forgiveness, attaining God's pleasure, and eternal repose in the highest station with the nearest angels; they too divide into bestowed/acquired and spiritual/physical forms.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r5.anchor: Ni‘am-ı uhreviye, dünyada vâki‘olan ifrat ve tefritlerini mağfiret ederek rızâsına erdirmek

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r6.claim: An apparent present blessing may later become a calamity, and an apparent hardship may become happiness; real happiness is what ends safely, so the request is for blessings that bring a safe outcome rather than immediate pleasure.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r6.anchor: ciddî ve hakīkī olan ni‘met ü saâdet âkıbeti her hâlde sâlim olanlardır

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r7.claim: The qualification that excludes anger and misguidance restricts the potentially all-inclusive favor to lasting good: afterlife blessings and their worldly precursors, especially life, liberty, faith, sound conscience, good character, social rectitude, beneficial knowledge, and righteous action.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r7.anchor: Bunların başı da hakk-ı hayat, hakk-ı hürriyet, iman, selâmet-i vicdan, hüsn-i ahlâk, salâh-ı ictimâ‘î, ilm-i nâfi‘, amel-i sâlihtir

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r8.claim: In Islamic usage, liberty means owning one's rights, as explained in Kashf al-Pazdawi; its opposite is enslavement through another's ownership of those rights.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r8.anchor: Lisân-ı İslâm’da “hürriyet”, hukūkuna mâlikiyet diye târif olunur (Keşf-i Pezdevî)

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r9.claim: Rights originate in divine ordinance; if human law can alter or control them without consent, a person is partly enslaved and duties depend on another's arbitrary will rather than right.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r9.anchor: herhangi bir ferdin vaz‘-ı ilâhî olan hukūku kendi rızâsı munzam olmaksızın diğer bir vaz‘-ı beşerî ile tebdil, tağyir veya tasarrufa mahkum olabiliyorsa

ELMALILI:1:6#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r10.claim: Liberty cannot coherently belong to someone who rejects God or serves another; its guarantee lies in worshipping God alone. The straight path begins in servitude to God, aims first at the great worldly blessing of liberty, rests on life and faith, and depends on divine aid and guidance.
ELMALILI:1:6#4/r10.anchor: Ve bunun için damân-ı hürriyet yalnız Allah’a ubûdiyettedir. Ve sırât-ı müstakīmin mebde’i bu ubûdiyet

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r1.claim: The right-path image derives ultimately from Jewish-Christian two-ways teaching and receives a standard formulation in the Fātiḥa, nearly matching Psalm 27:11.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r1.anchor: Das letztlich auf die jüdisch-christliche Zwei-Wege-Lehre zurückverweisende Bild des rechten Weges erhält durch die Fātiḥa seine Standardformulierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r2.claim: Ṣirāṭ is a Latin loan from strata via, paved road, evoking straight Roman military roads across broad territories; its metaphorical use was probably already conventional.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r2.anchor: Zu ṣirāṭ – ursprünglich lateinisches Lehnwort aus strata via (»geebnete Straße«)

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r3.claim: At Q 15:41 ṣirāṭ mustaqīm still means a right course in God’s dispute with Iblīs; after the Fātiḥa it apparently became reserved for God’s guidance of humanity.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:6:kommentar/r3.anchor: erst nach der Durchsetzung der Fātiḥa wird er offenbar für die göttliche Leitung der Menschen insgesamt reserviert

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r1.claim: Self-sufficiency and refusal to turn to God for knowledge and power cause error; the command to seek guidance itself shows people need it, and they should use their abilities under divine direction (96:6–8).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r1.anchor: Sapmanın ve yanılmanın baş sebebi insanın kendini yeterli sanması, bilgi ve güç almak için Allah’a yönelmeyi reddetmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r2.claim: The straight path is Islam, the general name for the religions sent through God’s prophets; it correctly orders relations between Creator and creation, reason and revelation, freedom and compulsion, justice and injustice, and good and evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r2.anchor: “Doğru yol” (sırât-ı müstakîm) İslâm’dır. Allah’ın peygamberleri ile kullarına gönderdiği dinlerin genel adı da İslâm’dır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r3.claim: A hadith’s straight-road parable maps the road to Islam, walls to God’s limits, curtained doors to forbidden acts, the caller at the entrance to scripture, and the inner caller to divine counsel; revelation, conscience, and reason work together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r3.anchor: Bu örnekteki yol İslâm’dır, duvarlar Allah’ın koyduğu sınırlardır, kapılar haramlardır, yolun başındaki çağırıcı Allah’ın kitabıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:6/r4.claim: The cited poem says the human sense of virtue arises from fear of God, rather than from learning or conscience alone.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.claim: Rabb al-alamin suits the request for guidance to the straight path because a nurturer's primary task is guidance, a frequent Qur'anic association.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p33/r2.anchor: أن قوله: {رَبِّ العالمين} مناسب لقوله فيما بعد: {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.claim: Worship suits mention of recompense, while seeking aid fits the ensuing request for guidance; each expression is placed beside what suits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r2.anchor: ومنها: أنَّ العبادة أكثرُ مناسبةً للجزاء أعني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.claim: Worship belongs to the God-praising half of the surah, whereas the servant’s request for aid belongs with the supplication beginning guide us.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p46/r5.anchor: فكان مع الشطر الذي له وهو {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} إلى آخر السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.claim: The direct address prepares for the supplication that follows in guide us.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r1.anchor: ذكر توطئةً للدعاء في قوله: اهدنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.claim: The opening praise is fittingly in the third person, while supplication from this point onward is fittingly direct address.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r3.anchor: الكلام من أول السورة إلى هنا ثناءٌ، والثناء في الغيبة أَوْلى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r5.claim: Guidance can mean directing, showing, clarifying, or inspiring; the verb appears with a direct object, with ilā, or with li.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p48/r5.anchor: معنى الهداية الإرشاد والدلالة والتبيين والإلهام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r1.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r1.claim: A preposition is used when the person is outside the path and must be led to it; a direct object works both for those on the path and those not yet on it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r1.anchor: إن الفرق بين التعدية بالحرف والتعدية من دون حرف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r2.claim: Abraham’s father and the hypocrites are outside the path, while the messengers and Muhammad are already walking it, showing direct-object guidance can describe either case.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r2.anchor: فتعديةُ الفعل بنفسه تقال لمن كان فيه أي في الصراط ولمن لم يكن فيه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r3.claim: Guidance with ilā or li is used for someone not yet on the route, as in requests to be guided to the middle path or to truth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p49/r3.anchor: أما التعدية باللام وإلى فتكون لمن لم يكن فيه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r1.claim: With a direct object, guide us includes inspire us, enable us, provide for us, or grant us; showing the two ways means explaining good and evil.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r1.anchor: وقد تُعدَّى الهداية بنفسها كما هنا: {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} فتضمن معنى ألهمنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r2.claim: Guidance with ilā means directing and showing the way, whereas guidance with li can mean granting success and making someone fit for it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r2.anchor: وذلك بمعنى الإرشاد والدلالة وكذلك قوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r3.speaker: اللسان
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r3.claim: Hijazi usage takes a direct object to mean acquainting someone with the road; other dialects use ilā, as al-Akhfash reported.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r3.anchor: هديته الطريق والبيت هداية، أي: عَرَّفته، لغة أهل الحجاز

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r4.speaker: ابن بري
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r4.claim: He distinguishes introducing someone to the road by direct object from guiding or directing them to it with a preposition.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r4.anchor: قال ابن بري: يقال: هديته الطريق بمعنى عرّفته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r5.claim: He glosses the Quranic phrase with guide them as make it clear to them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p50/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: أَوَ لم يُبَيِّنْ لهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r1.claim: Guidance has stages: one far from the way needs to be led to it, while one who has arrived needs its conditions, stages, dangers, and safe passages explained.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r1.anchor: فالبعيدُ الضالُّ عن الطريق، يحتاج إلى هادٍ يدلّه على الطريق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r2.claim: The lām can mark a purpose or endpoint; with guidance it can mean bringing a traveler to the goal that made the journey worthwhile.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r2.anchor: وقد تستعمل اللام مع الهداية لبيان الغاية من الحدث

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r3.claim: People need every kind of guidance: being returned to the route, taught its way, kept moving, and finally brought to their destination.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r3.anchor: والإنسان محتاج إلى هذه الهدايات كلها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r4.claim: The people of Paradise describe their final arrival as God guiding them to this, the culmination of guidance.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r5.claim: The Quran does not use guide with lām for a path or way because a path is a means to the goal, not the goal itself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p51/r5.anchor: ولذا لم نجد استعمال (هدى) مُعَدَّى باللام في القرآن الكريم مع السبيل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r1.claim: Faith, truth, what is most upright, light, and Paradise are desired endpoints, which explains Quranic use of lām with guidance for them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r1.anchor: فالإيمان والحق والتي هي أقوم والنورُ والجنة، كلها غاياتٌ مُرادةٌ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r2.claim: Guidance with lām to an endpoint is attributed only to God or His Book; people may guide others by direct object or with ilā.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r3.claim: Although a passage pairs direct-object guidance with guidance using ilā, that apparent interchange needs explanation rather than proving identical meanings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p52/r3.anchor: وقد تقول: لكن القرآن استعمل تعبيرين أحياناً في سياق واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r1.claim: The paired wording in the passage about paths of peace and a straight path can appear to make direct-object guidance and guidance with ilā synonymous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r1.anchor: مما يدل على أنهما بمعنى واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r2.claim: The verse about guidance to truth and for truth likewise appears to treat ilā and lām as equivalent.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r2.anchor: فعداه مرة بإلى ومرة باللام فقال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r3.claim: The author rejects the claim that these constructions mean the same thing and explains the first passage by the recipients’ different starting states.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r3.anchor: والحق أنها ليست بمعنى واحد، وأن هناك ما يقتضي هذا الاختلاف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r4.claim: Those already following God’s pleasure need the way explained, while people in darkness need to be brought out and delivered to the straight path.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p53/r4.anchor: فإن الذي اتَّبعَ رضوانَ الله ليس ضالاً ولا مبتعداً عن الصراط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r1.claim: Idols cannot even point to truth because they do not know where it is; God explains the way and brings seekers to their destination.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r1.anchor: وأما شركاؤهم فلا يدرون الحق أين هو؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r2.claim: The direct-object form in guide us covers both people already on the straight path, who need it explained, and believers who strayed, who need return.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r2.anchor: فهنا نطلب الهداية لمن كان في الطريق فيعرّفه به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r3.claim: Believers also ask to remain firm and increase in guidance, since they need God’s support at every moment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p54/r3.anchor: طلب استمرار الهداية على الطريق المستقيم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r1.claim: The prayer asks God to show the true route, restore the speaker if he strays, keep him firm, and increase his guidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r1.anchor: عرّفنا الطريقَ الحق وردّنا إليه ردّاً جميلاً إذا ما ضللنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r2.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r2.claim: Since the worshipper has already praised God and declared worship and reliance, guide us asks for guidance to continue.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r2.anchor: ومضمون هذه الجملة طلب استمرار الهداية إلى طريق مَنْ أنعم الله عليهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r3.claim: One interpretation asks to be kept firm in religion against doubts, supported by a Quranic prayer and a prophetic supplication for steadfast hearts.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r3.anchor: أحدها: أن معناه ثَبِّتنا على الدين كيلا تزلزلنا الشُّبَه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r4.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r4.claim: A second interpretation asks God to increase the guidance already received.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r5.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r5.claim: A third interpretation takes guidance here to mean reward.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r6.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r6.claim: A fourth interpretation asks God to show the truth in the future as He showed it previously.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r6.anchor: ورابعها: أن المراد دُلَّنا على الحق في مستقبل عمرنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r7.claim: Fronting us before the verb would wrongly imply that the supplicant asks for guidance only for his group and not for anyone else.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p55/r7.anchor: لا يصلح طلب التخصيص بالهداية دون سائر الناس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.claim: Guide us matches we worship and we seek aid: once the speaker includes companions in worship, he asks guidance for all, needed to reach their aim.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r1.anchor: لأنه لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله ويستعينونه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.claim: Invoking the congregation’s mercy, the worshipper praises, worships, seeks help, asks guidance, follows the righteous, and flees the rejected as a group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.anchor: سمعت رسولك يقول: (الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب) فلما أردت تحميدك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r3.claim: A prayer made broadly for others as well as oneself is more likely to be answered.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r3.anchor: أن الدعاء كلما كان أعم كان إلى الإجابة أقرب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r1.claim: Praying for everyone trains a Muslim to want others to receive what he wants and counters selfishness and exclusive desire for good.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r1.anchor: أن تحب للآخرين ما تحب لنفسك فيغسل ما في النفس من درن الأثرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r2.claim: The plural prayer spreads a communal spirit among individuals.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r3.claim: Traveling the path together strengthens and comforts believers; solitude brings fear and fatigue, while the flock separated from the group is vulnerable.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r3.anchor: أن الاجتماع على الهدى، تثبيتٌ وقوة، وأن كثرة السائرين على الطريق تورث الأُنس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r4.claim: The request connects with Rabb of all worlds because a nurturer’s first task is to guide.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r4.anchor: لأن من معاني الرب المربي، وأول مهامّ المربي هي الهداية كما ذكرنا.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r5.claim: Guiding someone is an act of mercy, so the prayer asks the Most Merciful not to abandon the supplicant to error.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p57/r5.anchor: لأن مَنْ هداه الله فقد رحمه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r1.claim: Seeking aid includes asking God for guidance and steadfastness on it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r1.anchor: ومن الاستعانة أن تطلب منه الهداية والثبات عليها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.claim: The blessed are those who have followed the straight path, while those astray are lost from it; the Quran often pairs guidance and misguidance as opposites.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.anchor: والهدى ضد الضلال، وكثيراً ما يجمع القرآن بين الهدى والضلال على أنهما متضادان،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r3.claim: The author reads ṣirāṭ as a form suggesting inclusion and breadth, unlike ṭarīq and sabīl, which he derives from a beaten or heavily trodden way.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r3.anchor: ذلك أن (صراط) على وزن (فِعال) من (صراط) وهو من الأوزان الدالة على الاشتمال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r4.claim: The author says the form of ṣirāṭ suggests it can embrace every traveler, while ṭarīq may be narrow and fail to encompass them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r4.anchor: فيشتمل على كل السالكين، ولا يضيق بهم فهو واسع رَحْبٌ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r5.claim: The singular, definite, annexed, and qualified straight path is one unique route, as there is only one straight line between two points.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r5.anchor: وقد جاء بالصراط مفرداً مُعَرَّفاً بتعريفين: بالألف واللام والإضافة، وموصوفاً بالاستقامة مما يدل على أنه صراط واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r1.claim: The straight path is Islam, the shortest and easiest route to the goal; other routes bend and fail to arrive.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r1.anchor: فالصراط المستقيم هو طريق الإسلام وهو دين الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r2.claim: Following the path aims at reaching God, meaning attaining His approval, since all people eventually return to Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r2.anchor: إن المراد من السلوك على الصراط، هو الوصول إلى الله تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r3.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r3.claim: The straight line is the shortest between two points, so it suits a weak servant seeking the nearest, shortest route.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r3.anchor: الأول: أنه أقرب الخطوط وأقصرها، وأنا عاجز فلا يليق بضعفي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r4.claim: Because there is only one straight path and crooked paths resemble one another, the straight way is less confusing and safer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r4.anchor: الثاني: أن المستقيم واحد وما عداه معوجة، وبعضها يشبه بعضاً في الاعوجاج

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r5.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r5.claim: A straight path reaches the destination, whereas a crooked one does not.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r5.anchor: الثالث: الطريق المستقيم يوصل إلى المقصود، والمعوج لا يوصل إليه.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r6.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r6.claim: The straight route remains unchanged, unlike a crooked one.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p59/r6.anchor: الرابع: المستقيم لا يتغير، والمعوج يتغير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r1.claim: The path’s two forms of definiteness identify one exclusive route to God, conveyed through His messengers and revealed books.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r1.anchor: وذكر الصراط المستقيم منفرداً مُعَرَّفاً بتعريفين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r2.claim: The rebellious routes are described in plural, while the way to God is one; all other approaches are closed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r2.anchor: فوحَّد لفظ الصراط وسبيله وجمع السبل المخالفة له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r3.claim: Quran uses ṣirāṭ only in the singular, unlike sabīl, because ṣirāṭ is the broad route into which the many paths lead.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r3.anchor: أن القرآن لم يأت بكلمة الصراط، إلا مُفْرَدَةً فلم يستعملها مجموعة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.claim: The next phrase identifies the straight path as the way of the blessed, excluding the angry and the astray and encompassing every accountable person.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.anchor: ثم زاد هذا الصراط بياناً وتوضيحاً، فقال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.claim: Living out worship and seeking aid in knowledge, action, and inward state cures corruption of the heart and intention.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.anchor: والتحقق بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} علماً ومعرفة وعملاً وحالاً يتضمنُ الشفاءَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.claim: Asking for the straight path cures ignorance; healing these spiritual diseases makes a person among the blessed, unlike those corrupt in intention or knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.anchor: ومن مرض الجهل بـ {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} عُوفيَ من أمراضه وأسقامه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.claim: After asking for guidance, it is fitting to ask distance from misguidance; this order also suits the verse endings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.anchor: وأما سؤال الهداية بعد ذلك وهو قوله:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.claim: The surah gathers the foundations of Islamic belief: God and His perfect attributes, monotheism, the Last Day, divine power, and the messengers and revelation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة جمعت أصول العقيدة الإسلامية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.claim: The straight path is known through prophets and messengers; acceptable worship comes from revelation, not from each person’s preference.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.anchor: فإن الصراط المستقيم الذي يريده الله إنما يعرف من طريق الأنبياء والرسل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.claim: The surah contains the religion’s two pillars, faith and righteous action; the faith section names belief in God, His messengers, and the Last Day.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r8.anchor: وتضمنت دين الإسلام بركنيه، الإيمان والعمل الصالح.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.claim: Rabb also fits the request for guidance because education is a core sense of lordship and guidance frequently follows the name Rabb in scripture.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p15/r2.anchor: من معاني الرب المربي وهي أشهر معانيه وأولى مهام الرب الهداية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r1.claim: The obligatory repeated request for guidance shows its importance: people cannot find the straight path unaided, and prayer requires reciting al-Fatiha; this differs from the sunnah supplication in 2:201.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r1.anchor: لا صلاة بدون فاتحة فلذا يجب الدعاء به في الصلاة الفريضة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p22/r2.claim: Guidance means inspiration and direction, and هدى may govern its object directly, with إلى, or with ل, as the cited verses demonstrate.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r1.claim: The author distinguishes constructions by stages: إلى can bring an outsider to the path; direct transitivity can describe someone on or off it; ل marks reaching the goal after traveling it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r1.anchor: إذا وصل ويحتاج من يعرفه بالطريق وأحواله نستعمل الفعل المتعدي بنفسه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p23/r2.claim: Examples contrast the stages: Abraham's father and hypocrites need direction to the path, while the prophets and the Messenger are already on it; إلى likewise marks an outsider in 38:22 and 10:35.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r1.claim: The author says ل is never used with sirat or sabil because these are means rather than destinations; it marks final guidance and is used with God or the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r1.anchor: الهداية مع اللام لم تستعمل مع السبيل أو الصراط أبدا في القرآن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r2.claim: In 10:35 God's guidance to the truth reaches its final destination, unlike the false gods' inability to bring people there.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r2.anchor: الله وحده يرشدك ويوصلك إلى خاتمة الهدايات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r3.claim: In 5:16 direct transitivity suits people who already follow God's favor, while إلى suits those in darkness who need to be brought to the path.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r3.anchor: والذي في الظلمات هو بعيد عن الصراط ويحتاج إلى من يوصله إلى الصراط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r4.claim: The direct object in اهدنا الصراط combines the stages: ask God both to bring the straying to the path and to show and steady those already on it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p24/r4.anchor: لجمع عدة معاني فالذي انحرف عن الطريق نطلب من الله تعالى أن يوصله إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.claim: Fronting إيانا would wrongly restrict guidance to us alone; unlike worship and reliance, guidance is not requested exclusively for the speaker's group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r1.anchor: ولا يجوز أن نقول إيانا اهدي بمعنى خصنا بالهداية ولا تهدي أحداً غيرنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r2.claim: The plural اهدنا matches the prior plural worship and reliance, counters selfishness, and asks for others what one asks for oneself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r2.anchor: فيه إشاعة لروح الجماعة وقتل لروح الأثرة والأنانية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r3.claim: Traveling the path together brings strength and comfort; a solitary traveler may weaken, tire, fall, or be eaten by wolves.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r3.anchor: كلما كثر السالكون كان ادعى للاطمئنان والاستئناس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r4.claim: Communal salvation is a mercy, while punishment adds isolation to fire; the plural saved in 4:13 share company in Paradise, unlike the solitary punished in 4:14.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p25/r4.anchor: في العذاب فيزيد على عذاب الكافر عذاب الوحدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r2.claim: Sirat's fa'al pattern suggests encompassing breadth, unlike tariq or sabil; it is roomy enough for all travelers, as al-Zamakhshari describes it swallowing paths through its width.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري في كتابه الكشاف: الصراط من صرط كأنه يبتلع السبل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.claim: The definite, construct, singular, straight path is one route to God's pleasure; other paths do not reach the goal, and scripture consistently uses sirat in the singular.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.anchor: مما يدل على انه صراط واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.claim: Sirat is singular while sabil can be plural because the many paths lead into the one broad path; following other paths fragments people away from it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.anchor: الصراط هو الأوسع وهو الذي تفضي إليه كل السبل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r3.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r3.claim: Al-Kubaisi likens imam to a unique main highway and says Quranic imam can mean a community's law or a clear record/book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r3.anchor: يقول الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي في كلمة الصراط وأخواتها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r4.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r4.claim: Al-Kubaisi describes sirat as a unique passage between opposites, metaphorically monotheism and absolute divine justice, while other paths are relative.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r4.anchor: صراط: هو كل ممر بين نقطتين متناقضتين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r5.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r5.claim: Al-Kubaisi describes sabil as a long, safe, easy but multiple route from one starting point to one destination; it can also mean rights, and ibn al-sabil is a legitimate stranded traveler.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r5.anchor: سبيل: الطريق الذي يأتي بعد الصراط وهو ممتد طويل آمن سهل لكنه متعدد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r6.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r6.claim: Al-Kubaisi compares tariq to repeatedly traveled city streets and to regular acts of worship such as prayer, charity, fasting, pilgrimage, and remembrance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r6.anchor: طريق يكون داخل المدينة وللطرق حقوق خاصة بها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r7.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r7.claim: Al-Kubaisi defines nahj as a special route for particular groups and their distinctive devotional practices; he illustrates it with night worship and beneficence, with spending shared across the examples.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r7.anchor: نهج: وهو عبارة عن ممرات خاصة لا يمر بها إلا مجموعة خاصة من الناس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r8.speaker: الدكتور أحمد الكبيسي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r8.claim: Al-Kubaisi distinguishes a mountain pass (fajj), a heavily worn trail or track (jada/judad), and an underground passage (nafaq).

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.claim: Al-Fatiha contains faith and good works, affirming God, the Last Day, angels, messengers, and scriptures, and joins lordship's unity to the unity of worship; it is therefore the Mother of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r5.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه السورة توحيد الربوبية

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr is reported with both sīn and ṣād; Abū ʿAmr with sīn, ṣād, and an intermediate sound, while al-Aṣmaʿī reports zāy; others use ṣād, with Ḥamza between ṣād and zāy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r1.anchor: فروي عن ابن كثير: السين والصاد. وروي عن أبي عمرو: السين، والصاد، والمضارعة بين الزاي والصاد

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r2.claim: The sīn reading is defended as preserving the word’s original consonant, since a dialect using ṣād before ṭā obscures that origin.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r2.anchor: للقارئ بالسين أن يقول: هو أصل الكلمة، ولو لزم لغة من يجعلها صادا مع الطاء لم يعلم ما أصلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r3.claim: The ṣād reading is defended as easier and more pleasing because its emphatic articulation resembles ṭā; sīn is voiceless and farther from it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r3.anchor: ويقول من يقرأ بالصاد: إنها أخف على اللسان، لأن الصاد حرف مطبق كالطاء فتتقاربان

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r4.claim: The zāy reading is explained as voicing the consonant to match ṭā, with ease supported by the variants ṣaqr, saqr, and zaqr.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r4.anchor: ويقول من قرأ بالزاي: أبدلت منها حرفا مجهورا حتى يشبه الطاء في الجهر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r5.claim: The intermediate sound aims for ease without becoming pure zāy or ṣād, thus avoiding confusion with either.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r5.anchor: ويقول من قرأ بالمضارعة التي بين الزاي والصاد : رمت الخفة، ولم أجعلها زاء خالصة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sarrī prefers ṣād for ease, sound, and prevalence; it is not confusing because the relevant dialect avoids sīn before ṭā, and most readers use it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r6.anchor: والاختيار عندي الصاد، للخفة، والحسن في السمع، وهو غير ملبس

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r7.claim: He rejects the pure zāy report as likely a mishearing of Abū ʿAmr’s intermediate pronunciation and says it should not govern recitation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r7.anchor: وأما الزاي فأحسب الأصمعي لم يضبط عن أبي عمرو

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r8.claim: He rejects the intermediate reading as difficult and nonstandard, though not impossible Arabic; ṣād is more eloquent, common, and close to ṭā, while Abū Ḥātim says pure zāy is unknown.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p49/r8.anchor: وأما القراءة بالمضارعة التي بين الزاي والصاد فعدلت عن القراءة بها، لأنه تكلف حرف بين حرفين

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the request with an indefinite ‘straight path’ rather than the common definite ‘the straight path.’
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن رضي الله عنه: "اهدنا صراطا مستقيما"5.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī interprets the indefinite reading as humble obedience: the worshippers accept whatever straight guidance God grants, whether little or much, and promise to follow it.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r3.anchor: أي: قد رضينا منك يا ربنا بما يقال له: صراط مستقيم، ولسنا نريد المبالغة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r4.claim: He also hears an ongoing plea in the indefinite form: ‘keep guiding us’; the result is a straight path, expressed through an abstract description that becomes a concrete, exemplary person in his poetic analogies.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p40/r4.anchor: وذلك أن تقديره: أدم هدايتك لنا؛ فإنك إذا فعلت ذلك بنا فقد هديتنا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.claim: The sīn form preserves the word’s original consonant; ṣād replaces sīn to harmonize its hissing quality with ṭāʾ’s emphatic articulation.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.anchor: قرله تعالى ﴿ الصراط ﴾ تقرأ بالصاد والسين واشمام الزاي فالحجة لمن قرأ بالسين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.claim: The sīn reading of الصراط is transmitted from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr through named reciters, while Ibn Kathīr also has transmissions with ṣād; Abū ʿAmr is reported with all three sibilant realizations.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.anchor: وروى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو أنه قرأ / الزراط / بالزاي خالصة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.speaker: عريان بن أبي سفيان عن أبي عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.claim: One transmission from Abū ʿAmr places the sound between ṣād and zāy; the ordinary reading preserves clear ṣād, while Ḥamza’s imāla approaches zāy and cannot be represented precisely in writing.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.anchor: وروى عريان بن أبي سفيان عن أبي عمرو أنه كان يقرأ بين الصاد والزاي مثل حمزة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.speaker: الكسائي عن حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.claim: Reports differ on whether Ḥamza shades only quiescent ṣād toward zāy or also moving ṣād; some say he gives the zāy outright only when ṣād is quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.anchor: وقال الكسائي عن حمزة إنه كان يفعل ذلك بالصاد الساكنة خاصة ولا يفعله بالمتحركة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.claim: Sīn is etymologically original, but scribes and readers use ṣād to ease articulation beside emphatic ṭāʾ: both sounds can be made with the tongue raised, unlike sīn and ṭāʾ together.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.anchor: والسين الأصل والكتاب بالصاد وإنما كتبت بالصاد ليقربوها من الطاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.claim: Shading ṣād toward voiced zāy matches the voicing of ṭāʾ while retaining a sibilant; the same voicing rationale applies to the cited ṣād+dāl words.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.anchor: وأما إمالة الصاد إلى الزاي فلأن الصاد وإن كانت من حروف الإطباق فهي مهموسة

QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#1/r1.claim: A canonical substitution of sīn for ṣād changes emphatic to non-emphatic articulation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#1/r1.anchor: Sīn for ṣād — canonical phonetic substitution; emphatic→non-emphatic, semantic identical

QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#2/r1.claim: The ishmām reading blends ṣād with zāy, a phonetic intermediate that preserves the same lexeme.
QIRAAT-ER:1:6:2#2/r1.anchor: Intermediate ṣ/z sound (ishmām) — phonetic blend between ṣād and zāy; same lexeme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r1.claim: Hidāya may mean guidance, direction, precedence, clarification, inspiration, or calling; its usual transitive construction takes lām or ilā, then may expand to a direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r1.anchor: الهداية: الإرشاد والدلالة والتقدم ومنه الهوادي أو التبيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r2.claim: The suffix -nā in ihdinā is a first-person plural pronoun, whether the speaker means self with others or a plural of majesty, and it can occupy several cases.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r2.anchor: ونا ضمير المتكلم ومعه غيره أو معظم نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r3.claim: Ṣirāṭ originally begins with sīn, from the idea of swallowing; ṣād is standard Quraysh usage, while sīn, zāy, and an intermediate sound are reported readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r3.anchor: الصراط الطريق، وأصله بالسين من السرط، وهو اللقم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r4.claim: The majority read ṣirāṭ with ṣād, the Quraysh form written in the codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r4.anchor: وإبدال سينه صادا هي الفصحى، وهي لغة قريش، وبها قرأ الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r5.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r5.claim: Ḥamza reads ṣirāṭ with a sound between zāy and ṣād, with variation in the transmitted details.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r5.anchor: وإشمامها زايا لغة قيس وبه قرأ حمزة بخلاف وتفصيل عن رواته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r6.speaker: أبو علي عن ابن مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī transmits Ibn Mujāhid's objection that a pure zāy reading may be a mistaken hearing of an intermediate consonant, while conceding it could be eloquent Arab usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r6.anchor: وحكى هذا الكلام أبو علي عن أبي بكر بن مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r7.claim: Al-Ṭūsī says ṣād is Quraysh and the good form, sīn common to Arabs generally, and zāy the dialect of several tribes; he also reports variable gender by region.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r7.anchor: الصراط بالصاد لغة قريش، وهي اللغة الجيدة، وعامة العرب يجعلونها سينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي، والضحاك، ونصر بن علي، عن الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r8.claim: These authorities read ṣirāṭan mustaqīman without the definite article, a form also attested in other Qur'anic wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p44/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي، والضحاك، ونصر بن علي، عن الحسن: اهدنا صراطا مستقيما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r1.claim: Mustaqīm derives from istaqāma used simply as qāma; it means uprightness or being straight without crookedness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r1.anchor: استقام: استفعل بمعنى الفعل المجرد من الزوائد، وهذا أحد معاني استفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r9.claim: Ihdinā is an imperative expressing request and desire; the form itself does not specify immediacy, repetition, or obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r9.anchor: اهدنا صورته صورة الأمر، ومعناه الطلب والرغبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r10.claim: Several glosses of ihdinā are attributed mostly to Ibn ʿAbbās, including guide, enable, lead, inspire, explain, or keep us firm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r10.anchor: وهل معنى اهدنا أرشدنا، أو وفقنا، أو قدمنا، أو ألهمنا، أو بين لنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r11.speaker: علي وأبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r11.claim: The final reported gloss of ihdinā, establish us firmly, is attributed to ʿAlī and Ubayy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r11.anchor: أو ثبتنا؟ أقوال أكثرها عن ابن عباس، وآخرها عن علي وأبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r12.speaker: ثابت البناني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r12.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reads the petition as baṣṣirnā al-ṣirāṭ, make us see the path.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r1.speaker: علي وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r1.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the straight path as the Qur'an; further reported identifications include faith, Islam and its laws, the balanced way, the Prophet's path, pilgrimage, Sunna, Paradise, the community, hope and fear, or the bridge over Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r1.anchor: ومعنى الصراط القرآن، قاله علي وابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r2.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r2.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḥasan identify the path as that of the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r2.anchor: أو طريق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأبي بكر وعمر، قاله أبو العالية والحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r3.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r3.claim: Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ interprets the path as the route of pilgrimage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r3.anchor: أو طريق الحج، قاله فضيل بن عياض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r4.speaker: عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r4.claim: ʿUthmān identifies the path with the Sunan.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the path is the path to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r5.anchor: أو طريق الجنة، قاله سعيد بن جبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r6.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r6.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd identifies the path as the bridge over Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r6.anchor: أو جسر جهنم، قاله عمرو بن عبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r7.speaker: الجنيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r7.claim: Al-Junayd interprets asking for guidance amid bewilderment as asking for the qualities of servanthood rather than absorption in God's eternal attributes; Abū Ḥayyān says such mystical readings exceed the wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r7.anchor: وقول الجنيد إن سؤال الهداية عند الحيرة من إشهار الصفات الأزلية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r8.speaker: الفخر الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that prior recipients of divine favor could not have followed the Qur'an or Islamic law; Abū Ḥayyān replies that this assumes, without proof, that the blessed are only predecessors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r8.anchor: وقد رد الفخر الرازي على من قال إن الصراط المستقيم هو القرآن أو الإسلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r9.claim: The plural suffix links ihdinā to We worship and We seek help: those who confess worship ask together for clear guidance, since worship requires reaching its proper path.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r9.anchor: واتصال نا باهد مناسب لنعبد ونستعين لأنه لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r10.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read ṣirāṭan mustaqīman without the definite article.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p47/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، والضحاك: صراطا مستقيما دون تعريف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads “straight path” in annexation, meaning the religion that is upright.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق: صراط مستقيم بالإضافة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: On al-Ḥasan’s and al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s reading, “the path of those” is a definite apposition to an indefinite, like “a straight path, God’s path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: فعلى قراءة الحسن والضحاك يكون صراط الذين بدل معرفة من نكرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: On al-Ṣādiq’s and the majority’s readings, “the path of those” is an apposition of one definite to another, clarifying the previously somewhat vague “straight path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة الصادق وقراءات الجمهور تكون بدل معرفة من معرفة صراط الذين بدل شيء من شيء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: This apposition restates the request for guidance, making it firmer and more emphatic by directing it to the path of those God favored.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: وجيء بها للبيان لأنه لما ذكر قبل اهدنا الصراط المستقيم كان فيه بعض إبهام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: The shift to direct address in “You alone we worship,” “You alone we seek help,” and “guide us” is iltifāt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: النوع الثامن: الالتفات، وهو في إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين، اهدنا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r4.claim: “Guide us” asks for the continuance of guidance, not its initial acquisition alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r4.anchor: النوع التاسع: طلب الشيء، وليس المراد حصوله بل دوامه، وذلك في اهدنا.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r1.claim: Guidance is gentle direction, as suggested by the word's derivation; the related verb is also used for walking gently.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r1.anchor: الهداية دلالة بلطف لدلالة إشتقاقه ومادته عليه ولذا أطلق على المشي برفق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r2.claim: The command to lead the guilty to Hell is sarcastic, like announcing painful punishment with the wording of good news.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r2.anchor: فأهدوهم إلى صراط الجحيم ) وارد على الصحيح مورد التهكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
