ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r3.claim: Arabic permits hadaa with li or ila; when used with a direct object, the verb may either describe a current state or mean bringing someone to the destination.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r3.anchor: ويقال هداه لكذا وإلى كذا فتعديه باللام وإلى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r4.claim: When the direct-object construction means bringing someone to attainment, a verse about striving for God's paths can be understood as seeking the will to attain higher ranks or actually obtaining them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r4.anchor: لنهدينهم سبلنا ) لسبلنا أو إلى سبلنا إلا بإرادة الإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r5.claim: Later linguists disagree whether guidance must convey the traveler to the goal or may merely point toward what will lead there.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r5.anchor: وأما باب التجوز فواسغ وهل يعتبر في الدلالة الإيصال أم لا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r6.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r6.claim: One camp reserves guidance for direction that actually reaches the destination; another uses it for pointing to a route that can lead there.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r6.anchor: ففريق خصها بالدلالة الموصلة وآخرون بالدلالة على ما يوصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r7.speaker: قليل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r7.claim: A third view says direct transitivity means successfully conveying and applies only to God, while constructions with li or ila mean showing a route and may describe God, the Quran, or the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r7.anchor: وقليل قال إن تعدت إلى المفعول الثاني بنفسها كانت بمعنى الإيصال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r8.claim: The claim that guidance always conveys the recipient is contradicted by Thamud, who were shown the way yet preferred blindness; explanations involving apostasy conflict with historical and exegetical reports that most never believed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r8.anchor: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فأستحبوا العمى على الهدى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r9.claim: The second view has difficulty with the statement that the Prophet cannot guide those he loves; explaining it as mere inability to show the way is strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p91/r10.claim: The third view is unsupported by linguistic usage and is refuted by Abraham and the believing Egyptian who use direct-object guidance for human instruction.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r1.claim: Ṣirāṭ means a path and derives from swallowing; its root evokes the path consuming its traveler or the traveler consuming it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r1.anchor: والصراط ( الطريق وأصله بالسين من السرط وهو اللقم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub transmit the original sīn; most readers use the Qurayshi ṣād, Hamza colors ṣād toward zāy, and pure zāy is attributed to ʿUdhr and Kalb; Alusi judges ṣād most eloquent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r2.anchor: وبالسين على الأصل قرأ إبن كثير برواية قنبل ورويس اللؤلؤي عن يعقوب وقرأ الجمهور بالصاد وهي لغة قريش وقرأ حمزة بإشمام الصاد زايا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r3.claim: Hijaz speakers treat ṣirāṭ as feminine, Tamim speakers as masculine; masculine use is more common, with plural patterns depending on gender.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r3.anchor: وأهل الحجاز يؤنثون الصراط كالطريق والسبيل والزقاق والسوق وبنو تميم يذكرون هذا كله وتذكيره هو الأكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r4.claim: Al-mustaqīm is level and without crookedness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r4.anchor: و ( المستقيم ( المستوي الذي لا إعوجاج فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r5.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the straight path as the true path.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r5.anchor: وأختلف في المراد منه فقيل الطريق الحق وقيل ملة الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r6.claim: Other reported interpretations identify it with Islam or the Qur'an.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r7.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r7.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Islam and Qur'an readings because the people blessed in 1:7 include earlier nations who had neither; Alusi objects that al-Razi elsewhere defines the path by universal moral moderation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r7.anchor: ردهما الرازي قدس سره بأن قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r8.claim: A reported view makes the path knowledge of how each thing points to the divine essence and attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد به معرفة ما في كل شيء من كيفية دلالته على الذات والصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r9.claim: Another view makes it the early peoples’ path of enduring great hardships for God's pleasure.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد منه صراط الأولين في تحمل المشاق العظيمة لأجل مرضاة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r10.claim: A further view identifies the path with worship, citing God's command to worship Him; Alusi says Qur'anic passages interpret one another but finds this argument questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r10.anchor: وقيل العبادة لقوله تعالى ( وأن أعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r11.claim: Another reported interpretation is turning away from everything besides God and devoting oneself wholly to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92/r11.anchor: وقيل هو الإعراض عن السوي والإقبال بالكلية على المولى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿArabi defines the straight path as the establishment of tawhid in both union and distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.anchor: وقال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره وهو ثبوت التوحيد في الجمع والتفرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.claim: Alusi distinguishes a general path for everyone from a special path for spiritual elect; both belong to the paths of those blessed according to their ranks.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.anchor: فالأول جسر بين العبد وبين الله سبحانه ممدود على متن جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.claim: The general path is the revealed law in knowledge, action, character, and spiritual state, imaged as a bridge over the hell of disbelief, sin, ignorance, innovation, and desire; its afterlife form reflects one's present state.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.anchor: وهو الإستقامة على ما ورد به الشرع الشريف القويم علما وعملا وخلقا وحالا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.claim: The special path is arrival at God: seeing creatures as without independent action, then life, then as sheer nonbeing; further travel in God is endless because divine beauty and majesty are inexhaustible.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.anchor: ومن شهد الخلق لا فعل لهم فقد فاز ومن شهدهم لا حياة لهم فقد جاز ومن شهدهم عين العدم فقد وصل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says a veil or cloud comes over his heart and that he seeks God's forgiveness seventy times daily; Alusi uses it to illustrate ongoing spiritual ascent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.anchor: إنه ليغان على قلبي فأستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة سبعين مرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.claim: For ordinary believers the prayer asks guidance to obey commands and avoid prohibitions; for spiritual elect it asks steadfastness in gifts already received, a reading attributed to ʿAli and Ubayy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.anchor: متى قال العامي أهدنا الصراط المستقيم أراد أرشدنا إلى الإستقامة على إمتثال أوامرك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.speaker: يعسوب المؤمنين وأبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.claim: The special interpretation—asking to be kept firm in what one has been granted—is transmitted from ʿAli and Ubayy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.anchor: وهو المروي عن يعسوب المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه وأبي رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r8.claim: A seeker must perfect and become firmly established in each station before moving to the next, so asking for continued firmness advances spiritual progress.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r8.anchor: ولا ينتقل إلى مقام أو حال إلا بعد الرسوخ فيما تحته والثبات عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r9.speaker: المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r9.claim: One answer to why the already guided ask for guidance is that they seek protection from doubts and deviation, as in the prayer of 3:8 and the hadith asking the Turner of hearts for firmness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r9.anchor: أحدها أن معناه ثبتنا على الدين كيلا تزلزلنا الشبه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r10.speaker: المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r10.claim: A second answer is that believers seek an increase in guidance, as promised in 47:17.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r10.anchor: وثانيها أعطنا زيادة الهدى كما قال تعالى : ( والذين أهتدوا زادهم هدى )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r11.speaker: المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r11.claim: A third answer interprets guidance as reward: believers ask to be led to Paradise, supported by 10:9 and 7:43.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r11.anchor: وثالثها أن الهداية الثواب كقوله تعالى ( يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r12.speaker: المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r12.claim: A fourth answer asks God to keep guiding believers to truth in the future as He guided them in the past.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r12.anchor: ورابعها أن المراد دلنا على الحق في مستقبل عمرنا كما دللتنا عليه في ماضيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r13.claim: Alusi relates the request for guidance to the preceding request for aid through four combinations of broad or specific aid and broad or specific meanings of the path; in one combination guidance singles out the greatest aim from all needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r13.anchor: بقى الكلام في ربط هذه الجملة بما قبلها وقد قيل أن عندنا إحتمالات أربعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r14.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r14.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Zayd ibn ʿAli read ṣirāṭan mustaqīman without the definite article; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm in an annexation, while the canonical reading is the wording given.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p92#2/r14.anchor: وقد قرأ الحسن والضحاك وزيد بن علي صراطا مستقيما دون تعريف وقرأ جعفر الصادق صراط المستقيم بالإضافة والمتواتر ما تلوناه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: Ihdina means guide us; Ali and Ubayy instead gloss it ‘keep us steadfast,’ as when someone tells a person already standing to remain so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: اهدنا أرشدنا وقال علي وأبي بن كعب: ثبتنا كما يقال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r2.claim: Believers already guided ask for constancy and for further guidance, since God’s gracious aids and guidance have no limit according to Sunni doctrine.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r2.anchor: وهذا الدعاء من المؤمنين مع كونهم على الهداية بمعنى التثبيت وبمعنى طلب مزيد الهداية لأن الألطاف والهدايات من الله تعالى لا تتناهى على مذهب أهل السنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: The word sirat is also read with sīn, its original form; Yaʿqub’s transmitter Uways reports that reading, while zāy and Hamza’s imāla-like sound are valid dialects.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: وسراط بالسين رواه أويس عن يعقوب وهو الأصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r4.claim: Most readers choose ṣād because it matches the written codex.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r4.anchor: والاختيار: الصاد، عند أكثر القراء لموافقة المصحف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Jabir, with Muqatil, identify the straight path as Islam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجابر رضي الله عنهما: هو الإسلام وهو قول مقاتل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r6.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the path as the Quran; a report attributed to Ali from the Prophet likewise calls it God’s book.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه: هو القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r7.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr identifies the straight path as the way to Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه: طريق الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r8.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r8.claim: Sahl b. Abd Allah says the path is the way of the Sunnah and community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r8.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله: طريق السنة والجماعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r9.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r9.claim: Bakr b. Abd Allah al-Muzani identifies it as the path of the Messenger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r9.anchor: وقال بكر بن عبد الله المزني: طريق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r10.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r10.claim: Abu al-Aliya and al-Hasan say it is the Messenger, his family, and his two Companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r10.anchor: وقال أبو العالية والحسن: رسول الله وآله وصاحباه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54/r11.claim: In ordinary Arabic, sirat means a clear road.

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r1.claim: “Guide us” specifies the requested aid or names its chief purpose; guidance is gentle direction and is normally for good, while its use for the path to Hell in 37:23 is ironic.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r1.anchor: بيان للمعونة المطلوبة فكأنه قال: كيف أعينكم فقالوا { اهدنا }

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r2.claim: Divine guidance has four ordered kinds: faculties for recognizing interests, distinguishing signs, messengers and revealed books, and disclosure of realities by revelation, inspiration, or true dreams.

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r3.claim: Scripture illustrates guidance by signs at 2:10, 41:17, 21:73, 17:9, 6:90, and 29:69; the last kind is reserved for prophets and saints.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r3.anchor: وهذا قسم يختص بنيله الأنبياء والأولياء وإياه عنى بقوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r4.claim: The request seeks an increase in guidance already granted, steadfastness in it, or the further ranks that follow it; the spiritually realized ask to travel toward God and shed bodily veils.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r4.anchor: فالمطلوب إما زيادة ما منحوه من الهدى، أو الثبات عليه، أو حصول المراتب

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r5.claim: Command and supplication share wording and meaning but differ through the speaker's elevated or lower rank, or simply through rank.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r5.anchor: والأمر والدعاء يتشاركان لفظا ومعنى ويتفاوتان بالاستعلاء والتسفل

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r6.claim: Ṣirāṭ derives from swallowing because the road seems to swallow its travelers; ṣaraṭ with ṣād assimilates the sīn to emphatic ṭāʾ, sometimes retaining a z-like sound.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r6.anchor: من سرط الطعام إذا ابتلعه فكأنه يسرط السابلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r7.claim: Qunbul's Ibn Kathīr and Ruways's Yaʿqūb read the original sīn; Ḥamza uses an imāla-like z sound, and the rest read ṣād, the Qurashī form preserved in the codex.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير برواية قنبل عنه، ورويس عن يعقوب بالأصل

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r8.claim: Ṣirāṭ is masculine or feminine like ṭarīq, and its plural is suruṭ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:6/r8.anchor: والثابت في الإمام وجمعه سرط ككتب وهو كالطريق في التذكير والتأنيث

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r1.claim: The straight path is the level path of truth, identified by some as Islam; “the path of those You favored” is an emphatic explanatory apposition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r1.anchor: المستوي والمراد به طريق الحق، وقيل: هو ملة الإسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: أبو الفضل محمد المشدالي المغربي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.claim: Al-Mashdali's method for Qur'anic coherence is to identify a surah's purpose, its prerequisites and their distance from the goal, then answer expectations raised as the discourse unfolds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا الإمام المحقق أبو الفضل محمد بن العلامة القدوة أبي عبد الله محمد ابن العلامة القدوة أبي القاسم محمد المشدالي المغربي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.claim: A surah's name summarizes its purpose, as a title signals the details within; Adam demonstrated this naming principle when he named things before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: أن اسم كل سورة مترجم عن مقصودها هلأن أسم كل شيء تظهر المناسبة بينه وبين مسماه عنوانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.claim: The Fatiha's many titles converge on مراقبة: it is the Mother of the Book, foundation, oft-repeated, treasure, healing, sufficing, complete, protecting, incantation, praise, thanks, supplication and prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: فمدار هذه الأسماء كما ترى على أمر خفي كاف لكل مراد وهو المراقبة التي سأقول إنها مقصودها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.claim: The Fatiha is a treasure, cure, sufficiency, fulfillment, protection and incantation; it gathers praise, gratitude and supplication, with prayer as their greatest assembly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: فكل شيء لا يفتتح بها لا اعتداد به ، وهي كنز لكل شيء شافية لكل داء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: The Fatiha's purpose is to establish God's exclusive right to all praise and perfection, sovereignty over both worlds, worship and aid, and to ask for the path of the successful rather than the doomed; its center is مراقبة.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.anchor: الغرض الذي سبقت له الفاتحة وه إثبات استحقاق الله تعالى لجميع المحامد وصفا الكمال ، واختصاصه بملك الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: The basmala relates to the Fatiha as the Fatiha relates to the Qur'an: each is a compact synthesis of what the larger whole details.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: وأشد منه أنه لما كانت نسبة البسملة من الفاتحة نسبة الفاتحة من القرآن صدرت بها الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.claim: Worship is possible only through God's aid, and guidance lies in His hand; the sequence moves from essence to acts to attributes and back to essence, teaching dependence after recognizing God's right.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن عبادته لا تتهيأ إلا بمعونته وإلى أن ملاك الهداية بيده

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.claim: Al-Harali says all Qur'an is God's speech, but some verses voice what creatures at different levels ought to say yet cannot express; God teaches them words that fulfill their duty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أى هذه وما بهدها مما جاء كلام الله فيه جارياعلى لسان خلقه فإن القرآن كله كلام الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: Al-Harali explains the sound report that God divided prayer between Himself and His servant: the first three verses are God's praise, which He accepts from the reciting servant as praise and glorification.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: وتلك هي صلاتهم المقسمة التى عبر عنها فيما صح عنه علية الصلاة والسلام من قوله تعالى : ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.claim: The verse teaches confession of inability, need and reliance on God's power; that dependence leads directly to asking for guidance along the necessary path.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r9.anchor: وفي الآية ندب إلى اعتقاد العجز واستشعار الافتقار والاعتصام بحوله وقوته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an's arrangement is miraculous, so the Fatiha must retain its required order in prayer; rearrangement or insertion of foreign material invalidates it. Al-Isfahani locates its clearest inimitability in order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين الإعجاز يتعلق بالنظم والترتيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.claim: The spiritual seeker passes through awe of God's attributes, recognizes many perilous paths and the lack of guidance or safety apart from God, then asks for the straight path, its blessed companions and protection from both condemned groups.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.anchor: فلما أشرف وستنار وعرف مواقع الأسرار بالأقدار كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي أي مذهب تذهب ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: مسعود التفتازاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Taftazani maps the Fatiha's blessings to two creations and two preservations: creation in Rabb al-alamin, preservation in mercy, second creation in judgment, and afterlife preservation in worship onward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فغنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء ثانيافي دار الفناء والبقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the seven repeated verses are the Qur'an's gathered essence and its contents will be disclosed at creation's completion; earlier scriptures progress from changeable scrolls and lasting books to the Qur'an, which completes religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب القفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في أخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Al-Harali contrasts the Qur'an's detailed, dispersed sequence with the Fatiha's seven complete universals, and makes the Fatiha a mirror of the servant's move from misguidance to guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: ووجه فوت أم القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع , فيه نجوم مبثوثة غير منتظمة , وحداة إثر واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent to complete noble character; the author links this completion with the Fatiha's comprehensive opening and the Qur'an's culmination.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق . أن إلى ربك المنتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's majesty through rulings spanning immediate and deferred realities, witnessed experience, and reports of the past and patterns that recur in time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: ومن مجيده وهو ما حربت أحكامه من بين عاجل ما شهد وآجل ما علم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual descent that moves understanding between states and rulings from descent from high to low, which may occur with or without intermediaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وما كان منه بتدريج وتقريب للأفهام ففاءت من حال إلى حال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: The passage names al-Baqara 2:281 as the last revealed verse and says its recitation position between the debt verse and the verse before it shows revelation and recitation order can differ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an's sevenfold gathering in Muhammad's heart relates to the Mother of Qur'an's universals as the Qur'an's gathering in his heart relates to the Mother.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: وأما الجمع ففي قلبه نسبة جوامعه السبع في أم القرآن إلى القرآن بمنزلة نسبة جمعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an reached the Prophet on his tongue over the span of the prophetic mission, after its descent to the lowest heaven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: وعلى لسانه في أمد أيام النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: Aisha reports that Muhammad's character was the Qur'an, making his conduct the visible form of its inner reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Al-Harali says the Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother: its first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, while its last three cover the creature's way to God, mercy or failure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: فالآيات الثلاث الول قال شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Recitation order can differ from revelation chronology; the verse allowing the Prophet to marry certain women was placed before a later restriction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: فقد يتطابق قرآن الأمر وتطور الخلق وقد لا يتابق والله يتولى إقامتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: In the authentic report in Muslim and the four Sunan, God says the Fatiha is divided between Himself and His servant: He answers praise, glorification and worship, and grants the servant's final requests.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : سمعت زسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-Baqara aims to prove the Book is guidance to follow; belief in the unseen, especially resurrection and the afterlife, is its greatest guidance and organizing theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال ، وأعظم ما يهدي إليه الإيمالن بالغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: The cow story makes the surah's title apt because resurrection occurs through an apparently slight human cause; it is a clearer sign of divine power than Abraham's story or earlier Israelite resurrections.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: فلذلك سميت بها السورة وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: The following comparison of hearts and stones shows the guided and astray: hearts become hard and wretched, while stones display fear and yield benefit that reaches God's servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: ولا سيما وقد اتبعت بوصف القلوب والحجارة بما عم اللمهتدين بالكتاب والضالين فوصفها بالقسوة الموجبة للشقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: The Book functions like a caliph from the resolute messengers, guiding every matter to the right exit: rejecting it fails, hesitation nearly perishes, and accepting it brings piety and excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى أن هذا الكتاب فينا كما لو كان فينا خليفة من أولي العزم من الرسل يرشدنا في كل أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-Baqara is also called the Radiant and the Hump: it illuminates guidance and sufficiency, brightens believers' faces at judgment, and exalts belief in the afterlife above every other good after monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة ، ولأيجابها إسفار الوجوه يفي يوم الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Because praise is the seventh inclusive letter, the Fatiha begins with it and gathers the seven universals diffused through the Qur'an, as the Qur'an gathers earlier scriptures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: ولما كان حرف الحمد هو سابعها الجامع افتتح الله به سبحانه وتعالى الفاتحة أم القرآن وأم الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: The fifth verse's request returns to praise, the sixth to the grace of lawful and forbidden provisions, and the seventh to the sovereign's command; together these complete all seven letters.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: وعادتت مسألة الآيةى الخاتمسة على حرف الحمد ومسألة الآية السادسة على آية النعمة من حرفي الحلال والحرام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: “Guide us” means direct us; the straight path is Islam, since any religion without monotheism is not straight.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: اهدنا} أرشدنا {الصراط المستقيم} يعني دين الإسلام لأن كل دين غير الإسلام فليس بمستقيم

DURR-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: Qatada identifies the straight path with the path of the prophets and explains those under anger as Jews and the astray as Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} أي الصراط المستقيم {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} أي طريق الأنبياء

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Ali recited “You alone we worship … guide us” with both verbs raised; another report says he used hamza, lengthening, and shadda in “iyyaka.”
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: عن أبي رزين قال: سمعت عليا قرأ هذا الحرف وكان قرشيا عربيا فصيحا {إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين اهدنا

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: The Prophet recited “ihdina al-sirat” with sad.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor:
عن أبي هريرة
أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} بالصاد

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Kathir read “sirat” with sin; Hamza read it with zay, a pronunciation al-Farra attributes to Udra, Kalb, and Banu al-Ayn.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس
أنه قرأ / اهدنا السراط / بالسين

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r5.speaker: الفراء
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r5.claim: Al-Farra says Hamza's “zirat” has a pure zay and is a dialect of Udra, Kalb, and Banu al-Ayn.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r5.anchor: عن الفراء قال: قرأ حمزة / الزراط / بالزاي قال الفراء

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “guide us to the straight path” as “inspire us with Your true religion.”
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} يقول: ألهمنا دينك الحق

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “guide us to the straight path” as “inspire us with the guided path.”
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} قال: ألهمنا الطريق الهادي

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas completes the gloss by saying the straight path is God's religion, which has no crookedness.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r8.anchor: هو دين الله الذي لا عوج له

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “sirat” simply as a road.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس قال {الصراط} الطريق

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r10.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r10.claim: Jabir identifies the straight path with Islam and describes it as wider than the distance between heaven and earth; the report is graded sound in the source.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r10.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله في قوله {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} قال: هو الإسلام وهو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the straight path is Islam.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن جريج عن ابن عباس قال {الصراط المستقيم} الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v1p37/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r12.claim: Ibn Masud and other Companions likewise interpret the straight path as Islam.
DURR-FULL:v1p37/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة {الصراط المستقيم} الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v1p39/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r1.claim: A sound prophetic parable depicts Islam as a straight path flanked by God's limits, with open doors as prohibitions, the Quran calling at its entrance, and God's inward admonition calling above.
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r1.anchor: عن النواس بن سمعان عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ضرب الله صراطا مستقيما وعلى جنبتي الصراط سوران

DURR-FULL:v1p39/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r2.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the straight path with the Book of God and urges people to follow it and hold fast to it.
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} قال: هو كتاب الله

DURR-FULL:v1p39/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r3.claim: In a report whose transmission is weakened by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says the Quran is the refuge from trials and the decisive, wise Book, God's strong rope and the straight path.
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r3.anchor: عن علي قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ستكون فتن قلت: وما المخرج منها قال: كتاب الله

DURR-FULL:v1p39/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says the straight path is the way the Prophet left the community upon, with its other end in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v1p39/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال {الصراط المستقيم} الذي تركنا عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r1.claim: A report says the Quran is the clear light, wise reminder, and straight path.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r1.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال القرآن هو النور المبين والذكر الحكيم والصراط المستقيم

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the straight path with the Prophet and his two Companions after him; al-Hasan affirms that he spoke truly and gave sound advice.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {الصراط المستقيم} قال: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas likewise says the straight path is the Prophet and his two Companions.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r3.anchor: أبي العالية عن ابن عباس في قوله {الصراط المستقيم} قال: هو رسول الله وصاحباه

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya al-Riyahi urges learning Islam and not turning away; the straight path is Islam, with no deviation to either side.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية الرياحي قال: تعلموا الإسلام فإذا علمتموه فلا ترغبوا عنه وعليكم بالصراط المستقيم

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r5.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r5.claim: Sufyan says Quranic interpretation has no real disagreement because a comprehensive expression may intend more than one of its meanings.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r5.anchor: عند سفيان قال: ليس في تفسير القرآن اختلاف انما هو كلام جامع يراد به هذا وهذا

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Darda says full understanding requires recognizing that Quranic expressions can have multiple meanings.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال: قال أبو الدرداء: إنك

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r7.claim: Ali sent Ibn Abbas to debate the Kharijites using the Sunnah rather than Quran alone, since Quranic wording admits multiple readings; Ibn Abbas prevailed by citing Sunnah.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r7.anchor: ابن عباس يحدث عن الخوارج الذين أنكروا الحكومة فاعتزلوا علي بن أبي طالب قال: فاعتزل منهم اثنا عشر ألفا

DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says he knows the Quran well because it was revealed in his family's houses, but Ali answers that its many possible meanings make Sunnah the proper argument against the Kharijites.
DURR-FULL:v1p39#2/r8.anchor:
فقال ابن عباس: يا أمير المؤمنين فأنا أعلم بكتاب الله منهم
في بيوتنا نزل فقال: صدقت

RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r6.claim: The request is for guidance in every kind of guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r6.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ بحسب كل أنواع الهدايات

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r13.claim: Asking for guidance has two routes: acquiring knowledge through proof and argument, and purifying the inner self through spiritual discipline.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r13.anchor: أما قوله جل جلاله ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ فاعلم أنه عبارة عن طلب الهداية ولتحصيل الهداية طريقان : أحدهما طلب المعرفة بالدليل والحجة والثاني : بتصفية الباطن والرياضة

RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r14.claim: Proofs of God are inexhaustible because every particle in the upper and lower worlds testifies to divinity, majesty, and self-sufficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v1p19/r14.anchor: لأنه لا ذرة من ذرات العالم الأعلى والأسفل إلا وتلك الذرة شاهدة بكمال إلهيته وبعزة عزته وبجلال صمديته

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r1.claim: The cited poem says every thing bears a sign of God's oneness; bodies share corporeality but differ in qualities, which requires a particularizing, wise agent rather than body or impersonal nature.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r1.anchor: تقريره : أن أجسام العالم متساوية في ماهية الجسمية ومختلفة في الصفات وهي الألوان والأمكنة والأحوال

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r2.speaker: ضياء الدين عمر
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r2.claim: Rāzī's father says each indivisible substance offers infinitely many proofs of power, wisdom, and mercy because it could occupy countless locations and bear countless possible attributes, each implying a wise, merciful maker.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r2.anchor: الشيخ الإمام الوالد ضياء الدين عمر رحمه الله يقول : إن لله تعالى في كل جوهر فرد أنواعا غير متناهية من الدلائل الدالة على القدرة والحكمة والرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r3.claim: Purification is an endless field, and each traveler to God has a distinct path and way; Rāzī cites the verse that each has a direction toward which they turn.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r3.anchor: وأما تحصيل الهداية بطريق الرياضة والتصفية فذلك بحر لا ساحل له ولكل واحد من السائرين إلى الله تعالى منهج خاص

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r4.claim: Human reason cannot reach the secrets of these spiritual paths, though realized knowers discern deep, subtle matters beyond most people's understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r4.anchor: ولا وقوف للعقول على تلك الأسرار ولا خبر عند الافهام من مبادئ ميادين تلك الأنوار والعارفون المحققون لحظوا فيها مباحث عميقة

TAB:1:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the plea as asking God to grant steadfastness on the straight path, an interpretation he says was also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās.
TAB:1:6/r1.anchor: ومعنى قوله : ( اهْدِنا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيم ) في هذا الموضع عندنا : وَفّقنا للثبات عليه

TAB:1:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Gabriel instructing Muhammad to ask for guidance, glossed as inspiring them toward the guiding path.
TAB:1:6/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس قال :  قال جبريل لمحمد :  «قل يا محمد اهدنا الصراط المستقيم » ،   يقول :  ألهمنا الطريق الهادي .

TAB:1:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r3.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r3.claim: The plea follows the exclusive worship and request for help in 1:5: worshippers ask God to help them worship and follow the way granted to His favored servants.
TAB:1:6/r3.anchor: فكان معنى الكلام :  اللهم إياك نعبد وحدك لا شريك لك ،   مخلصين لك العبادة دون ما سواك من الاَلهة والأوثان ،

TAB:1:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r4.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r4.claim: The request concerns God's help to remain obedient, hit the truth, and avoid what He forbids in the remainder of one's life, not completed past deeds.
TAB:1:6/r4.anchor: التوفيق للثبات على العمل بطاعته ، وإصابة الحقّ والصواب فيما أمره به ، ونهاه عنه فيما يستقبل من عمره دون ما قد مضى

TAB:1:6/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:6/r5.claim: Some gloss the request as “increase us in guidance.”
TAB:1:6/r5.anchor: وقد زعم بعضهم أن تأويل قوله : ( اهْدِنا ) زدنا هداية

TAB:1:6/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r6.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r6.claim: If “increase guidance” means more exposition, it is wrong: God clarifies duties and establishes proof before imposing them; asking for unclarified or new duties is incoherent.
TAB:1:6/r6.anchor: لا يكلف عبدا فرضا من فرائضه إلا بعد تبيينه له وإقامة الحجة عليه به

TAB:1:6/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r7.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r7.claim: If the proposed increase means added divine help, it must concern future deeds, since a servant no longer needs help for completed deeds; this matches his reading.
TAB:1:6/r7.anchor: وفي ارتفاع حاجة العبد إلى المعونة على ما قد تقضّى من عمله ما يعلم أن معنى مسألة تلك الزيادة إنما هو مسألته الزيادة لما يحدث من عمله

TAB:1:6/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r8.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r8.claim: The verse refutes the Qadariyya claim that anyone commanded has already received enough aid to have no further need of God, since the servant is taught to ask for divine help.
TAB:1:6/r8.anchor: لبطل معنى قول الله جل ثناؤه : ( إِيّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وإِيّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ اهْدِنا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ )

TAB:1:6/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r9.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r9.claim: Arabic usage makes guidance mean enabling: one cited poem asks God to enable the listener to fulfill the speaker's request.
TAB:1:6/r9.anchor: لا تَحْرِمَنّي هَدَاكَ اللّهُ مَسألتي *** ولا أكُونَنْ كمَنْ أوْدَى بِهِ السّفَرُ يعني به : وفقك الله لقضاء حاجتي

TAB:1:6/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r10.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r10.claim: A second Arabic poem uses “may the King guide you” to mean “may He enable you to reach the truth in my matter.”
TAB:1:6/r10.anchor: فمعلوم أنه إنما أراد :  وفقك الله لإصابة الحقّ في أمري .

TAB:1:6/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r11.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r11.claim: The repeated Qur'anic statement that God does not guide wrongdoers means that He does not grant them success or open their hearts to truth and faith, not that He withholds clarification of duties.
TAB:1:6/r11.anchor: ولكنه عنى جلّ وعز ، أنه لا يوفقهم ، ولا يشرح للحق والإيمان صدورهم

TAB:1:6/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r12.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:6/r12.claim: Some understand the plea as asking to be led along the road to Paradise in the afterlife, comparing it with being led into Hell and ordinary uses of leading someone or something to a destination.
TAB:1:6/r12.anchor: أن معنى قوله : ( اهْدِنا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) : أَسْلِكْنا طريق الجنة في المعاد

TAB:1:6/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r13.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:6/r13.claim: This alternative cites “lead them to the path of Hell” (37:23) and Arabic idioms for leading a woman to her husband, giving a gift, or a foot following a leg as evidence for leading to a destination.
TAB:1:6/r13.anchor: كما قال جل ثناؤه : ( فاهْدُوهُمْ إلى صِرَاطِ الجَحِيمِ ) أي أدخلوهم النار كما تُهدى المرأة إلى زوجها

TAB:1:6/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r14.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r14.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the afterlife reading: 1:5 asks for help in worship, and the Companions and Successors agree that “the path” here is not that destination; “guide us” asks for steadfastness in guidance.
TAB:1:6/r14.anchor: وذلك أن جميع المفسرين من الصحابة والتابعين مجمعون على أن معنى «الصراط » في هذا الموضع غير المعنى الذي تأوله قائل هذا القول ،

TAB:1:6/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r15.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r15.claim: In Arabic, “I guided him the road,” “to the road,” and “toward the road” all mean that one showed and directed him to it; the Qur'an uses these constructions.
TAB:1:6/r15.anchor: والعرب تقول : هديت فلانا الطريق ، وهديته للطريق ، وهديته إلى الطريق : إذا أرشدته إليه وسددته له

TAB:1:6/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r16.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r16.claim: A poem uses “I ask God's forgiveness for a sin” without the preposition that would mean “for,” paralleling Qur'anic “ask forgiveness for your sin” (47:19).
TAB:1:6/r16.anchor: أسْتَغْفِرُ اللّهَ ذَنْبا لَسْتُ مُحْصِيَهُ *** *** رَبّ العِبادِ إلَيْهِ الوَجْهُ والعَمَلُ يريد : أستغفر الله لذنب

TAB:1:6/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r17.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r17.claim: Al-Nābigha's line “فيصيدنا” means “فيصيد لنا,” illustrating the range of Arabic preposition use in speech and poetry.
TAB:1:6/r17.anchor: فَيَصِيدُنا العَيَر المُدِلّ بِحُضْرِهِ *** *** قَبْلَ الوَنى والأشْعَب النّبّاحا يريد : فيصيد لنا .

TAB:1:6/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r18.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r18.claim: Exegetes unanimously take the straight path to be a clear road without crookedness, which is also its meaning in Arabic.
TAB:1:6/r18.anchor: أجمعت الأمة من أهل التأويل جميعا على أن الصراط المستقيم هو الطريق الواضح الذي لا اعوجاج فيه

TAB:1:6/r19.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r19.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r19.claim: Jarīr's verse calls the rightly directed way a “straight path,” evidencing the ordinary sense of ṣirāṭ as a path.
TAB:1:6/r19.anchor: أمِيرُ المُؤْمِنِينَ على صِرَاطِ *** إذا اعْوَجّ المَوَارِدُ مُسْتَقِيمِ يريد على طريق الحقّ .

TAB:1:6/r20.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r20.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r20.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb's comparison “thinner than the path” is another poetic witness to ṣirāṭ as a physical track or road.
TAB:1:6/r20.anchor: صَبَحْنا أرضَهُمْ بالخَيْلِ حتّى *** تَرْكْناها أدَقّ مِنَ الصّرَاطِ

TAB:1:6/r21.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r21.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r21.claim: A rajaz line uses ṣirāṭ in the ordinary sense of a direct road or way.

TAB:1:6/r22.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r22.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r22.claim: By extension, Arabs call any statement or action described as straight or crooked a ṣirāṭ, using the road metaphor for conduct and speech.
TAB:1:6/r22.anchor: ثم تستعير العرب الصراط فتستعلمه في كل قول وعمل وصف باستقامة أو اعوجاج

TAB:1:6/r23.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r23.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r23.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers asking God to keep worshippers firm in the beliefs and deeds He approved for those He favored: Islam, affirming the messengers, holding the Book, obeying commands, avoiding prohibitions, and following the Prophet and righteous predecessors. This broad sense gathers the reported explanations.
TAB:1:6/r23.anchor: وَفّقنا للثبات على ما ارتضيته ووفقت له من أنعمت عليه من عبادك ، من قول وعمل

TAB:1:6/r24.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r24.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:6/r24.claim: A report from ʿAlī attributes to the Prophet the statement that the Qur'an is the straight path; al-Ṭabarī gives two transmission routes and no grading.
TAB:1:6/r24.anchor: عن عليّ بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه ،   عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال وذَكَرَ القُرآنَ فَقَال :  «هُوَ الصّرَاطُ الْمُسْتَقِيمُ »

TAB:1:6/r25.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r25.speaker: عليّ
TAB:1:6/r25.claim: ʿAlī identifies the straight path as the Book of God Most High.
TAB:1:6/r25.anchor: عن الحارث ،   عن عليّ ،   قال :  «الصّرَاطُ المُسْتَقِيمُ كِتابُ اللّهِ تَعالى »

TAB:1:6/r26.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r26.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB:1:6/r26.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies the straight path as God's Book.
TAB:1:6/r26.anchor: عن أبي وائل ،   قال :  قال عبد الله :  «الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله »

TAB:1:6/r27.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r27.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB:1:6/r27.claim: Jābir says the straight path is Islam and describes it as wider than the space between heaven and earth.
TAB:1:6/r27.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله . اهدنا الصراط المستقيم قال : الإسلام ، قال : هو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

TAB:1:6/r28.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r28.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:6/r28.claim: In a report through Maymūn ibn Mihrān, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the plea as asking for Islam.
TAB:1:6/r28.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : ( اهْدِنا الصرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) قال : ذلك الإسلام

TAB:1:6/r29.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r29.speaker: ابن الحنفية
TAB:1:6/r29.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya calls the straight path God's religion, the only religion He accepts from His servants.
TAB:1:6/r29.anchor: عن ابن الحنفية في قوله : ( اهْدِنا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) قال : هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره

TAB:1:6/r30.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r30.speaker: السدي
TAB:1:6/r30.claim: Al-Suddī transmits the gloss “Islam” from Abū Mālik, Abū Ṣāliḥ/Ibn ʿAbbās, Murra al-Hamdānī/Ibn Masʿūd, and a group of the Prophet's Companions.
TAB:1:6/r30.anchor: عن السدي في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك ، وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس ، وعن مرة الهمداني ، عن ابن مسعود ، وعن أناس من أصحاب النبي

TAB:1:6/r31.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r31.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:6/r31.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the straight path simply as “the way.”
TAB:1:6/r31.anchor: قال ابن عباس في قوله : ( اهْدِنا الصرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) قال : الطريق

TAB:1:6/r32.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r32.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB:1:6/r32.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the straight path with the Messenger, then Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
TAB:1:6/r32.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : ( اهْدِنَا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) قال : هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده : أبو بكر وعمر

TAB:1:6/r33.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r33.speaker: الحسن
TAB:1:6/r33.claim: Al-Ḥasan affirms Abū al-ʿĀliya's interpretation, saying he spoke truly and gave sincere advice.
TAB:1:6/r33.anchor: فذكرت ذلك للحسن ، فقال : صدق أبو العالية ونصح

TAB:1:6/r34.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r34.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
TAB:1:6/r34.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam glosses the request as asking for Islam.
TAB:1:6/r34.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن يزيد بن أسلم : ( اهْدِنا الصّرَاطَ المُسْتَقِيمَ ) قال : الإسلام

TAB:1:6/r35.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r35.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:6/r35.claim: In a report from Nawās ibn Samʿān, the Prophet says God gives the example of a straight path and identifies the path as Islam; al-Ṭabarī presents two routes and no grading.
TAB:1:6/r35.anchor: عن نواس بن سمعان الأنصاري ،   عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :  «ضَرَبَ اللّه مَثَلاً صرَاطا مُسْتَقِيما » .   وَالصّرَاطُ :  الإسْلامُ .

TAB:1:6/r36.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r36.speaker: author
TAB:1:6/r36.claim: The path is called straight because it is correct and contains no error.
TAB:1:6/r36.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله بالاستقامة ، لأنه صواب لا خطأ فيه

TAB:1:6/r37.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:6/r37.speaker: بعض أهل الغباء
TAB:1:6/r37.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the claim that the path is called straight because it leads its followers straight to Paradise, since this conflicts with the exegetes' consensus.
TAB:1:6/r37.anchor: وقد زعم بعض أهل الغباء أنه سماه مستقيما لاستقامته بأهله إلى الجنة

TAB:1:7/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r54.speaker: أهل الإلحاد الطاعنون في القرآن
TAB:1:7/r54.claim: Critics ask why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses when, they argue, the meaning of its remaining verses is already contained in “Master of Judgment Day” and “You alone we worship and ask for help.”
TAB:1:7/r54.anchor: فما الوجه إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفت في إطالة الكلام بمثل سورة أم القرآن بسبع آيات

TAB:1:7/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r55.claim: Earlier scriptures each contain some meanings found together in the Qur'an: the Torah gives admonitions and detail, the Psalms praise and glorify, and the Gospel admonishes and reminds; the Qur'an gathers these and adds more.
TAB:1:7/r55.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل ، والزّبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد ، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير

TAB:1:7/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prior books lack a miracle certifying their recipients, whereas the Qur'an's unmatched composition defeats all attempts to produce even a short surah and proves Muhammad's prophethood.
TAB:1:7/r56.anchor: نظمه العجيب ، ورصفه الغريب ، وتأليفه البديع ، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB:1:7/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r57.claim: The Qur'an's varied contents—encouragement, warning, commands, prohibitions, stories, argument, and parables—also make its extended expression purposeful.

TAB:1:7/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Fātiḥa's inimitable arrangement proves prophethood, while its praise and glorification direct people to recognize God's greatness, sovereignty, power, and dominion and to thank Him for His favors.
TAB:1:7/r58.anchor: ليذكروه بآلائه ويحمدوه على نعمائه ، فيستحقوا به منه المزيد ويستوجبوا عليه الثواب الجزيل

TAB:1:7/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r59.claim: The account of those favored through knowledge of God and His enabling teaches that every religious and worldly blessing comes from Him, directing requests to God rather than idols or rivals.
TAB:1:7/r59.anchor: تعريف عباده أن كل ما بهم من نعمة في دينهم ودنياهم فمنه ، ليصرفوا رغبتهم إليه

TAB:1:7/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r60.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r60.claim: Recounting punishments for disobedience warns people away from sin and from incurring God's anger, whose consequences lead to destruction.
TAB:1:7/r60.anchor: ترهيب عباده عن ركوب معاصيه ، والتعرض لما لا قبل لهم به من سخطه

TAB:1:7/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r61.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r61.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God answers the worshipper's recitation: He calls al-ḥamdu praise, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm commendation, Mālik Yawm al-Dīn glorification, and the rest of the surah the servant's share.
TAB:1:7/r61.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله : حمدني عبدي

TAB:1:7/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r62.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:1:7/r62.claim: A second Abū Hurayra version gives the same recitation exchange but is not attributed to the Prophet.
TAB:1:7/r62.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله ، فذكر نحوه ، ولم يرفعه

TAB:1:7/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r63.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r63.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the divine saying that the prayer is divided between God and His servant, with the servant receiving what he asks; the first three praises are God's, and what follows is for the servant.
TAB:1:7/r63.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.speaker: بعض النصارى
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.claim: He also quotes a Christian's parody of al-Fatiha as another failed counter-imitation.

ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.claim: He seeks refuge in God's grace and guidance and asks for mercy because he has failed to worship adequately.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r3.anchor: İnâyetine sığındım kapına geldim, hidâyetine sığındım lütfuna geldim. Kulluk edemedim affına geldim

ELMALILI:v1p85/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r4.claim: He asks not to be led astray and asks God to enable right speech, to reveal divine joy, and to teach truth.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r4.anchor: Kulluk edemedim affına geldim. Şaşırtma beni, doğruyu söylet

BURHAN:v1p16/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥa is the Mother of the Book because it contains all three fields: monotheism through 1:4, rulings in 1:5, and reminder from 1:6 onward.
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.anchor: ولهذا المعنى صارت فاتحة الكتاب أم الكتاب لأن فيها الأقسام الثلاثة

BURHAN:v1p359/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.claim: The author says the familiar labels for stop quality are not a complete, sound classification and have produced confusion in books on pauses.
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.anchor: فالوجه أن يقال الوقف ضربان اضطرارى واختيارى

BURHAN:v1p359/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.claim: A forced pause is caused only by running out of breath and is not restricted to particular places; examples include Ḥamza pausing within words or before a genitive complement.
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.anchor: فالاضطرارى ما يدعو إليه انقطاع النفس فقط وذلك لا يخص موضعا دون موضع

BURHAN:v1p359/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.claim: An optional pause is preferable and is classified by how the two parts of the statement depend on each other.
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.anchor: والاختيارى وهو أفضلهما هو الذى لا يكون باعتبار انفصال ما بين جزأى القول

BURHAN:v1p359/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.claim: An incomplete pause leaves the preceding part sufficient but the following part dependent; one may stop at “straight,” but cannot begin with “the path of those.”
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.anchor: الثانى الناقص وهو أن يكون ما قبله مستغنيا عما بعده ولا يكون ما بعده مستغنيا عما قبله

BURHAN:v1p6/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r1.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
BURHAN:v1p6/r1.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says that God’s threat to turn the arrogant away from His signs means depriving them of understanding the Qurʾān.
BURHAN:v1p6/r1.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة في قوله تعالى : ^ ( سأصرف عن آياتي الذين يتكبرون في الأرض بغير الحق ) ^ ، قال : أحرمهم فهم القرآن

BURHAN:v1p6/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r2.speaker: سفيان الثوري
BURHAN:v1p6/r2.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī says understanding the Qurʾān and preoccupation with worldly possessions never coexist in a believer’s heart.
BURHAN:v1p6/r2.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري : لا يجتمع فهم القرآن والاشتغال بالحطام في قلب مؤمن أبدا

BURHAN:v1p6/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى الكناني
BURHAN:v1p6/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz al-Kinānī compares Qurʾānic knowledge to a lion, whose lair only its master can enter.
BURHAN:v1p6/r3.anchor: قال عبد العزيز بن يحيى الكناني : مثل علم القرآن مثل الأسد لا يمكن من غيله سواه

BURHAN:v1p6/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r4.speaker: ذو النون المصري
BURHAN:v1p6/r4.claim: Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī says God denies idle hearts access to the Qurʾān’s hidden wisdom.
BURHAN:v1p6/r4.anchor: قال ذو النون المصري : أبى الله عز وجل [ إلا ] أن يحرم قلوب البطالين مكنون حكمة القرآن

BURHAN:v1p6/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BURHAN:v1p6/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd interprets “guide us to the straight path” as the Qurʾān, meaning “guide us to its knowledge.”
BURHAN:v1p6/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله تعالى : ^ ( اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ) ^ قال : القرآن ، يقول : أرشدنا إلى علمه

BURHAN:v1p6/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
BURHAN:v1p6/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says that Qurʾānic knowledge is a reminder known only to discerning men.
BURHAN:v1p6/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري : علم القرآن ذكر لا يعلمه إلا الذكور من الرجال

BURHAN:v1p6/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p6/r7.claim: The author says every discipline is drawn from the Qurʾān and otherwise lacks proof; Ibn Masʿūd’s instruction to “dig into” it refers to foundations of knowledge.
BURHAN:v1p6/r7.anchor: وكل علم من العلوم منتزع من القرآن

BURHAN:v1p6/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BURHAN:v1p6/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says anyone seeking knowledge should probe the Qurʾān, since it contains the knowledge of earlier and later peoples; al-Bayhaqī glosses this as the foundations of knowledge.
BURHAN:v1p6/r8.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : من أراد العلم فليثور القرآن

BURHAN:v1p6/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p6/r9.claim: The Companions had distinct specialties: ʿAlī in judging, Zayd in inheritance, Muʿādh in lawful and unlawful matters, and Ubayy in recitation.
BURHAN:v1p6/r9.anchor: كل منهم مخصوص بنوع من العلم كعلي رضي الله تعالى عنه بالقضاء

BURHAN:v1p6/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p6/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās alone was called an ocean because of his distinctive expertise in exegesis; ʿAlī praised his insight, and Ibn Masʿūd called him an excellent interpreter.
BURHAN:v1p6/r10.anchor: فلم يسم أحد منهم بحرا إلا عبد الله بن عباس لاختصاصه دونهم بالتفسير وعلم التأويل

BURHAN:v1p6/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p6/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd died in 32 AH, while Ibn ʿAbbās lived another thirty-six years, prompting the author to reflect on the knowledge he gained afterward.
BURHAN:v1p6/r11.anchor: وقد مات ابن مسعود في سنة ثنتين وثلاثين

BURHAN:v1p6/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p6/r12.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BURHAN:v1p6/r12.claim: ʿAlī had prior expertise in interpreting the Fātiḥa and said he could dictate a camel-load of commentary on it.
BURHAN:v1p6/r12.anchor: وهو القائل : لو أردت أن أملي وقر بعير على الفاتحة لفعلت

BURHAN:v1p38/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p38/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p38/r1.claim: The author favors the view that sūrah order is established by revelation and says each sūrah’s opening closely or subtly fits the ending of the preceding one.
BURHAN:v1p38/r1.anchor: قلت وهو مبنى على أن ترتيب السور توقيفى وهذا الراجح كما سيأتى

BURHAN:v1p38/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p38/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p38/r5.claim: Al-Baqara’s opening, “This is the Book, without doubt,” answers al-Fātiḥa’s request for guidance: this Book is the straight path requested, resolving al-Zamakhsharī’s question about the connection.
BURHAN:v1p38/r5.anchor: كأنهم لما سألوا الهداية إلى الصراط المستقيم قيل لهم ذلك الصراط الذى سألتم

BURHAN:v1p102/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p102/r1.claim: Faces are one shared word used for several senses; counterparts are words with a single shared sense, as the listed senses of huda illustrate.
BURHAN:v1p102/r1.anchor: فالوجوه اللفظ المشترك الذى يستعمل فى عدة معان كلفظ الأمة والنظائر كالألفاظ المتواطئة

BURHAN:v1p102/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p102/r2.claim: The alternative that faces concern meanings while counterparts concern wording is weak, since the books classify a single word's varied uses as faces.
BURHAN:v1p102/r2.anchor: وقيل النظائر فى اللفظ والوجوه فى المعانى وضعف لأنه لو أريد هذا لكان الجمع فى الألفاظ المشتركة

BURHAN:v1p102/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p102/r3.claim: Some classify the many senses a single Qur'anic word can bear as a form of inimitability unavailable in human speech.
BURHAN:v1p102/r3.anchor: وقد جعل بعضهم ذلك من أنواع معجزات القرآن حيث كانت الكلمة الواحدة تنصرف إلى عشرين وجها أو أكثر أو أقل

BURHAN:v1p102/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v1p102/r4.claim: Muqatil cites a marfuʿ report that full understanding of Qur'an requires recognizing its many possible senses; no grading is given.
BURHAN:v1p102/r4.anchor: وذكر مقاتل فى صدر كتابه حديثا مرفوعا لا يكون الرجل فقيها كل الفقه حتى يرى للقرآن وجوها كثيرة

BURHAN:v1p102/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p102/r11.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p102/r11.claim: In the Fatiha petition, huda means right guidance or rectitude.

BURHAN:v1p352/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p352/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p352/r1.claim: A good stop gives a complete sense, though what follows remains attached in wording or meaning and cannot be begun independently; the Fatiha examples illustrate it.
BURHAN:v1p352/r1.anchor: والحسن هو الذى يحسن الوقوف عليه ولا يحسن الابتداء بما بعده لتعلقه به فى اللفظ والمعنى

BURHAN:v1p352/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p352/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p352/r2.claim: A bad stop obscures the intended sense, including breaks between an adjective and its noun, a substitute and its antecedent, or a preposition and its object.
BURHAN:v1p352/r2.anchor: القبيح هو الذى لا يفهم منه المراد نحو

BURHAN:v1p352/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.claim: One classification calls a stop sufficient when the next verse has verbal attachment, good and sufficient when attachment is semantic, complete when neither holds, and bad when the sense conflicts; 1:6 continues verbally into 1:7.
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن تعلقت الآية بما قبلها تعلقا لفظيا كان الوقف كافيا

BURHAN:v2p139/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p139/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p139/r5.claim: A Muslim's prayer for an absent fellow Muslim is answered, with an attending angel saying amen and the same blessing for the supplicant; the Fatiha's plural petition also includes the community.
BURHAN:v2p139/r5.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعوة المسلم لأخيه بظهر الغيب مستجابة عند رأسه ملك وكل به

BURHAN:v2p195/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.claim: Wanting steadfastness on the straight path is itself obedience to God and His Messenger, since guidance to that path entails the obedience that places one with the blessed.
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.anchor: والرغبة إلى الله تعالى فى الثبات عليها هي نفس الطاعة لله ولرسوله

BURHAN:v2p455/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r1.claim: Abu Ali explains that a substitute can clarify its antecedent because its governing element is understood from the antecedent and connects the two in wording.
BURHAN:v2p455/r1.anchor: وقيل لأبي علي كيف يكون البدل إيضاحا للمبدل منه وهو من غير جملته فقال لما لم يظهر العامل في البدل

BURHAN:v2p455/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.claim: Part and inclusion substitutes clarify and specify an antecedent by naming it twice, first generally and then particularly; the forelock example adds its quality as the reason for seizing it.
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.anchor: وفائدة البدل أن ذلك الشيء يصير مذكورا مرتين إحداهما بالعموم والثانية بالخصوص

BURHAN:v2p455/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.claim: A definite noun may be replaced by another definite noun, as in the Fatiha's repeated mention of the straight path.
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.anchor: ويجوز بدل المعرفة من المعرفة نحو ﴿ الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين ﴾

BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.claim: When the same definite noun is repeated, the second usually refers to the first; examples include hardship in 94:5–6, the path in the Fatiha, and celestial objects in 41:37.
BURHAN:v4p93#2/r1.anchor: فالأول إن يكونا معرفتين والثاني فيه هو الأول غالبا

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r6.claim: The name Surah of Supplication reflects the request for guidance it contains.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r6.anchor: الحادي والعشرون سورة الدعاء لاشتمالها عليه

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r7.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r7.claim: Fakhr al-Din also gives it the name Surah of Asking because it contains a request.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r7.anchor: الثاني والعشرون سورة السؤال لذلك ذكره الإمام فخر الدين

ITQAN:v1p150#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r8.speaker: المرسي
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r8.claim: Al-Mursi calls it the Surah of Teaching the Request because it models supplication etiquette by beginning with praise.
ITQAN:v1p150#2/r8.anchor: الثالث والعشرون سورة تعليم المسألة قال المرسي لأن فيها آداب السؤال لأنها بدئت بالثناء قبله

ITQAN:v4p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v4p420/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Din maps the Qur’an’s four aims—God, resurrection, prophethood, and divine decree—onto the Fatiha: praise, Judgment Day, worship and reliance, and guidance through the surah’s end; this supports its name Umm al-Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين المقصود من القرآن كله تقرير أمور أربعة الإلهيات والمعاد والنبوات وإثبات القضاء والقدر لله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ITQAN:v4p420/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.claim: Al-Tibi divides the Fatiha’s religious knowledge into foundations (God and attributes, prophethood, resurrection), branches (worship), ethical perfection and seeking the path, and accounts of earlier peoples with promise and threat.
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي هي مشتملة على أربعة أنواع من العلوم التي هي مناط الدين

ITQAN:v4p421/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.speaker: الغزالي
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali lists three essential Qur’anic aims—knowing God, the straight path, and the return in the Hereafter—and three supplementary aims: the obedient, deniers’ speech, and the stations of the path, all signaled by the Fatiha.
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.anchor: وقال الغزالي مقاصد القرآن سنة ثلاثة مهمة وثلاثة متمة الأولى تعريف المدعو إليه كما أشير إليه بصدرها

ITQAN:v4p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

ITQAN:v4p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

ITQAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

ITQAN:v4p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

ITQAN:v4p490/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.claim: The closing request requires explaining guidance and the straight path and its opposites, the angered and astray and their qualities, and the approved people and their way.
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان الهداية ما هي والصراط المستقيم وأضداده وتبيين المغضوب عليهم والضالين وصفاتهم

ITQAN:v2p410/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p410/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p410/r1.claim: The author says huda has seventeen senses, beginning with steadfastness in the request to be guided on the straight path; his list in fact contains eighteen numbered senses.

ITQAN:v2p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p560/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p560/r1.claim: When a noun is repeated, four definiteness patterns are possible; when both occurrences are definite, the second usually denotes the first, as with “the straight path, the path of those You favored.”
ITQAN:v2p560/r1.anchor: فإن كانا معرفتين فالثاني هو الأول غالبا دلالة على المعهود الذي هو في الأصل في اللام أو الإضافة

ITQAN:v3p122/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p122/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p122/r3.claim: A verified metaphor has a sense realized physically or rationally; “the straight path” is the true religion, a concept realized by reason.
ITQAN:v3p122/r3.anchor: أي الدين الحق فإن كلا منهما يتحقق عقلا

ITQAN:v3p188#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r1.claim: Substitution (badal) clarifies after an ambiguous expression and reinforces it: it restates its meaning as if the governing word were repeated.
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r1.anchor: والقصد به الإيضاح بعد الإبهام وفائدته البيان والتأكيد أما الأول فواضح أنك إذا قلت

ITQAN:v3p188#4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r2.claim: “The path of those You favored” is a whole-for-whole apposition clarifying “the straight path”; the source also gives this construction in other verses, including the repeated forelock phrase.
ITQAN:v3p188#4/r2.anchor: مثال الأول ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾ ﴿ لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله ﴾ ﴿ لنسفعا بالناصية ناصية كاذبة خاطئة ﴾

ITQAN:v3p284/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.claim: The Fatiha points to all major Qur’anic disciplines: knowledge of God and attributes, prophecy, resurrection, worship, ethical conduct and the straight path, and stories teaching the outcomes of obedience and disobedience.
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.anchor: وقد وجه ذلك بأن العلوم التي احتوى عليها القرآن قامت بها الأديان أربعة علم الأصول ومداره على معرفة الله وصفاته

ITQAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

ITQAN:v3p297/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p297/r1.claim: The opening of al-Baqara, “This is the Book,” points back to the straight path requested in al-Fatiha: the requested path is the Book, linking the two suras.
ITQAN:v3p297/r1.anchor: وهذا معنى حسن يظهر فيه ارتباط سورة البقرة بالفاتحة

ITQAN:v3p297/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p297/r3.claim: Surah order may be divinely fixed; proposed grounds include alphabetic sequence, meaning links between adjacent openings and endings, verbal balance, or similarity between the suras' overall sentences.
ITQAN:v3p297/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم لترتيب وضع السور في المصحف أسباب تطلع على أنه توقيفي صادر عن حكيم

ITQAN:v3p297/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.claim: Al-Fatiha affirms lordship, seeks guidance in Islam, and protection from Judaism and Christianity; al-Baqara lays out religion's foundations, while Al Imran answers opponents' doubts, especially Christian reliance on ambiguous verses.
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.anchor: وسورة الفاتحة تضمنت الإقرار بالربوبية والالتجاء إليه في دين الإسلام والصيانة عن دين اليهودية والنصرانية

ITQAN:v3p297/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.claim: Al Imran makes pilgrimage obligatory, whereas al-Baqara establishes it and commands completion after beginning; Al Imran addresses Christians more and al-Baqara Jews more, reflecting the Torah's priority to the Gospel.
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.anchor: وأوجب الحج في آل عمران وأما في البقرة فذكر أنه مشروع وأمر بإتمامه بعد الشروع فيه

ITQAN:v3p297/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.claim: The Prophet called and fought the Jews after migrating to Medina, while his confrontation with Christians came late; Meccan suras address all people with shared prophetic religion, and Medinan suras address believers and scripturalists.
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة دعا اليهود وجاهدهم وكان جهاده للنصارى في آخر الأمر

ITQAN:v4p469/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p469/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p469/r4.claim: In the first category, interpreters describe one referent by different qualities: the straight path can mean following the Qur'an, Islam, the Sunna and community, servitude, or obedience to God and His Messenger.
