ITQAN:v4p469/r4.anchor: كتفسيرهم ( الصراط المستقيم ) بعض بالقرآن أي اتباعه وبعض بالإسلام فالقولان متفقان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p47/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p47/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p47/r1.claim: The purest metaphor draws its likeness from intellectual images: the straight path denotes religion, while proof is light because its effect on the heart resembles light's effect on sight, without shared genus or bodily form.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p47/r1.anchor: وكاستعارة الصراط للدين في قوله تعالى ( ^ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم وانك لتهدى إلى صراط مستقيم )

DAMGHANI:v1p276/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p276/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p276/r12.claim: In the Fātiḥa, the straight path means the straight religion.
DAMGHANI:v1p276/r12.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم يعني الدين المستقيم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r1.claim: In Arabic, al-sirat means a road or path.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r2.claim: Exegetes give a literal road sense, illustrated by the road on which people are threatened and the path to Hell.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r3.claim: Exegetes also use al-sirat for religion, as in the request for the straight path and God's path to be followed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p384/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أنه في القرآن على وجهين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r1.claim: The thirteenth Qur'anic sense listed for guidance is reform, illustrated by God's not guiding the treacherous plot.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r1.anchor: والثالث عشر : الإصلاح . ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r2.claim: A fourteenth sense is a messenger: the guidance sent to the Israelites and in Taha is glossed as a messenger.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r2.anchor: والرابع عشر : الرسول . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r4.claim: The fifteenth sense is discernment, illustrated by the unbelievers who were not guided in their trade.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r4.anchor: والخامس عشر : الاستبصار . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r5.claim: The sixteenth sense is a guide or indicator; in Moses's request, it can mean someone to show him the way to the fire if it is not actually fire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r5.anchor: والسادس عشر : الدليل . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r6.claim: The seventeenth sense is teaching, as in God's teaching people the practices of those before them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r6.anchor: والسابع عشر : التعليم . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r7.claim: The eighteenth sense is excellence or superiority: 'more guided' means better in way.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r7.anchor: والثامن عشر : الفضل . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r8.claim: The nineteenth sense is leading or directing, as in driving people toward the path to Hell.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r8.anchor: والتاسع عشر : التقديم . ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r9.claim: The twentieth sense is dying while adhering to Islam, expressed by the one who repents, believes, acts righteously, then is guided.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r9.anchor: منه قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r10.claim: The twenty-first sense is reward, in the statement that guidance is incumbent upon God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r10.anchor: والحادي والعشرون : الثواب . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الليل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r11.claim: The twenty-second sense is reminders: 'He found you astray and guided you' means He reminded you after forgetfulness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r11.anchor: والثاني والعشرون : الأذكار . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في الضحى )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r12.claim: The twenty-third sense is correctness, as in asking whether a person is on the right guidance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r12.anchor: والثالث والعشرون : الصواب . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r13.claim: The twenty-fourth sense is steadfastness: the prayer asks God to keep the worshippers on the straight path.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p629/r13.anchor: الثبات . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفاتحة

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r2.claim: The straight path is the clear way; an unnamed poet uses ṣirāṭ for a clear road.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r2.anchor: معناه المنهاج الواضح قال الشاعر: أمير المؤمنين على صراط. . . إذا اعوج

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r3.claim: “Guide us” means “keep us firm in guidance,” like asking a person already standing to remain so until one returns.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r3.anchor: ومعنى (اهدنا وهم مهتدون: ثبتنا على الهدى.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.claim: The object ‘You’ is fronted with worship and seeking help because these belong exclusively to God; worship is similarly exclusive in 39:66 and 2:172.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r3.anchor: على فعل العبادة وعلى فعل الاستعانة دون فعل الهداية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r5.claim: The request for guidance is not exclusive: one cannot ask God to guide only oneself and leave everyone else unguided, as with requests for provision, healing, and well-being.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4/r5.anchor: ولم يقدم مفعول الهداية على فعله فلم يقل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r4.claim: The object of guidance is not fronted because one cannot sensibly ask God to guide oneself exclusively while withholding guidance from everyone else.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p476/r4.anchor: ولم يقدم مفعول الهداية على فعله قلم يقل: إيانا اهد كما قال (إياك نعبد) وذلك لأن طلب الهداية لا يصح فيه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r1.claim: Directly transitive hadā may be said to someone already on the path or far from it; for the guided, it can ask God to keep and instruct them on it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r1.anchor: إذن المتعدي بنفسه يقولها لمن هو على الصراط أو بعيداً عن الصراط

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r2.claim: Hadā with إلى is for someone away from the path, whom God brings to it; examples include the disputants and the question about guiding to truth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r2.anchor: المتعدّي بـ (إلى) الموجودة في الآية تقال لمن كان بعيداً عن الصراط تحديداً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r3.claim: Transitivity with لام applies to reaching a goal or endpoint; the preposition can also mark purpose, as in لأجل مسمى.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p988/r3.anchor: التعدية باللام تكون لمن وصل إلى الغاية، إلى غاية الأمر، إلى المنتهى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p989/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p989/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p989/r1.claim: Guidance includes bringing the distant person to the path, showing someone already on it what it contains, and leading the traveler to its end; Qur’anic uses with ل often express reaching a destination.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p989/r1.anchor: المرحلة الأولى أن يوصله إلى الصراط والمرحلة الثانية أن يعرّفه ماذا في الطريق

NASHR:v1p227/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r4.claim: Stopping after these phrases is good because their sense is understood, but starting with attached phrases such as rabb al-ʿālamīn, ṣirāṭ alladhīna, or ghayr al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim is poor, except at verse ends per the Sunnah.
NASHR:v1p227/r4.anchor: الوقف على ذلك وما أشبهه حسن ; لأن المراد من ذلك يفهم، ولكن الابتداء ب (الرحمن الرحيم

NASHR:v2p93/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p93/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p93/r1.claim: Among readers, only al-Azraq lightens an open rāʾ after kasra or a silent yāʾ in a medial or final position; he normally does so without restriction, but tafkhīm returns in stated exceptions, including ṣirāṭ before an istiʿlāʾ letter.
NASHR:v2p93/r1.anchor: وأجمعوا على تفخيمها في هذه الأقسام كلها إلا أن تقع بعد كسرة، أو ياء ساكنة والراء مع ذلك وسط كلمة، أو آخرها فإن الأزرق له فيها مذهب خالف سائر القراء

NASHR:v2p93/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p93/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p93/r2.claim: Al-Azraq uses tafkhīm when a letter of istiʿlāʾ follows the rāʾ; the Qur'anic examples include ṣirāṭ in every case and firāq.
NASHR:v2p93/r2.anchor: متى وقع بعد الراء حرف استعلاء فإنه يفخمها كسائر القراء ووقع ذلك بعد المتوسطة في أربعة ألفاظ، وهي (صراط) كيف جاء

NASHR:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة
NASHR:v1p49/r1.claim: Abu Amr, and also Hamza, read ṣirāṭ with a pure zāy; sibilants may substitute for one another, and the reading fits the rasm as does the sīn reading.
NASHR:v1p49/r1.anchor: أبي عمرو، (الزراط) بالزاي الخالصة وجاء أيضا عن حمزة ووجه ذلك أن حروف الصفير يبدل بعضها من بعض

NASHR:v1p229/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p229/r1.claim: A pause on an incomplete fragment such as “bi-smi,” “al-ḥamdu,” or “rabbi” leaves the utterance unfinished and without an intelligible meaning.
NASHR:v1p229/r1.anchor: نحو الوقف على: بسم، وعلى: الحمد، وعلى: رب، وملك يوم، وإياك

ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.claim: The direct address in iyyāka naʿbud is a preparation for the supplication ihdinā that follows.
ABUHAYYAN:1:5/r37.anchor: ولأنه ذكر ذلك توطئة للدعاء في قوله اهدنا

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r1.claim: Hadā can mean guiding, directing, leading ahead, or making something clear; it can also mean inspiration or calling, depending on context.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r2.claim: The wording about Thamūd is an example of guidance meaning clarification.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r3.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r3.claim: The commentators explain that God inspired all animals toward what benefits them in the verse about giving each thing its creation and guidance.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r3.anchor: معناه ألهم الحيوانات كلها إلى منافعها

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r4.claim: In the phrase every people has a guide, guide means a caller or preacher.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r5.claim: The verb hadā originally takes its second object with li- or ilā; usage broadened to take it directly, as in ihdinā al-ṣirāṭ.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r5.anchor: ثم يتسع فيه فيعدى إليه بنفسه

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r6.claim: The nūn in ihdinā can represent the speaker together with others, or be the plural of majesty.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r6.anchor: ون ضمير المتكلم ومعه غيره أو معظم نفسه

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r7.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ means the road or path.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r8.claim: The original form begins with sīn and derives from saraṭ, swallowing; the road is named as though it swallows what travels it.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r9.speaker: قنبل ورويس
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r9.claim: Qunbul and Ruways read the original form with sīn.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r9.anchor: وبالسين على الأصل قرأ قبل ورويس

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r10.claim: Replacing sīn with ṣād is the standard Qurashī form; the majority read it, and it is the spelling in the codex.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r10.anchor: وإبدال سينه صاداً هي الفصحى ، وهي لغة قريش

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r11.speaker: الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r11.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports a zāy pronunciation from Abū ʿAmr.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r11.anchor: وزايا لغة رواها الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r12.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r12.claim: A sound between zāy and ṣād is a Qays dialect; Ḥamza reads it with variants and detail among his transmitters.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r12.anchor: وأشمامها زاياً لغة قيس ، وبه قرأ حمزة

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r13.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r13.claim: Abū ʿAlī reports sīn, ṣād, and an intermediate zāy-ṣād pronunciation from Abū ʿAmr; al-ʿAryān transmits it through Abū Sufyān, and al-Aṣmaʿī reports a pure zāy.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r13.anchor: أبو علي : وروي عن أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r14.speaker: بعض اللغويين
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r14.claim: Some linguists accuse al-Aṣmaʿī of mistaking an intermediate pronunciation for a pure zāy; Abū ʿAlī attributes this criticism to Ibn Mujāhid.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r15.claim: Al-Ṭūsī says ṣād is Qurashī and good Arabic, sīn is common among Arabs, and zāy belongs to ʿUdhra, Kaʿb, and Banū al-Qayn.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r15.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر الطوسي في تفسيره ، وهو إمام من أئمة الإمامية : الصراط بالصاد لغة قريش

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r16.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r16.claim: Ibn Mujāhid says the intermediate zāy-ṣād reading is an awkwardly produced sound between two letters, not one of the alphabetic phonemes.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r16.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن مجاهد ، وهذه القراءة

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān does not deny that the intermediate sound belongs to eloquent Arab speech, but judges ṣād more eloquent and widespread.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r18.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ can be masculine or feminine, with masculine usage more frequent.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r18.anchor: إلا أن الصاد أفصح وأوسع ، ويذكر ويؤنث

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r19.speaker: أبو جعفر الطوسي
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r19.claim: Al-Ṭūsī says Hijaz speakers treat ṣirāṭ like other path and place nouns as feminine, while Tamīm speakers make them masculine.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r19.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر الطوسي : أهل الحجاز يؤنثون الصراط

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r20.claim: If ṣirāṭ is masculine its common plural is suruṭ and its small plural is asriṭa; if feminine, its plural pattern is afʿul, as with dhirāʿ/adruʿ and shimāl/ashmul.

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r21.speaker: زيد بن علي، والضحاك، ونصر بن علي عن الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r21.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Naṣr ibn ʿAlī from al-Ḥasan read an indefinite ṣirāṭan mustaqīman without the definite article, as in the cited passage.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r21.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي ، والضحاك ، ونصر بن علي ، عن الحسن : اهدنا

ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r22.claim: Mustaqīm derives from istaqāma, where istifʿala has the simple verb sense of qāma: to stand upright without bending.
ABUHAYYAN:1:6/r22.anchor: والقيام هو الانتصاب والاستواء من غير اعوجاج

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.claim: The request for guidance follows naturally from the preceding declaration of worship and reliance: worship is sound only through guidance to the clear route that reaches its goal.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.anchor: لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله ويستعينونه

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.claim: The prayer asks that guidance to the path of the favored continue: those who praise God and declare worship and reliance already possess guidance, but ask for its permanence.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.anchor: ومضمون هذه الجملة طلب استمرار الهداية إلى طريق من أنعم الله عليهم

ALUSI:1:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī explains guidance as gentle indication, relating the root to walking gently (tahādī).
ALUSI:1:6/r1.anchor: الهداية دلالة بلطف لدلالة اشتقاقه ومادته عليه ولذا أطلق على المشي برفق تهاد

ALUSI:1:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r2.claim: The command to guide people to the path of Hell is, in the sound view, sarcastic, like the command to announce painful punishment.
ALUSI:1:6/r2.anchor: وارد على الصحيح مورد التهكم على حد

ALUSI:1:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r3.claim: The verb may take a path with li or ilā; without either preposition, its construction can carry either sense of guidance.
ALUSI:1:6/r3.anchor: ويقال : هداه لكذا وإلى كذا فتعديه باللام وإلى

ALUSI:1:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r4.claim: In 29:69, construing subulanā with li or ilā requires reading striving as intending guidance or attaining the lofty ranks; the plural reflects those ranks.
ALUSI:1:6/r4.anchor: لسبلنا أو إلى سبلنا إلا بإرادة الإرادة في جاهدوا

ALUSI:1:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī cites an unattributed report that acting on the knowledge one has leads God to bequeath knowledge one did not have.
ALUSI:1:6/r5.anchor: من عمل بما علم ورثه الله تعالى علم ما لم يعلم

ALUSI:1:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r6.speaker: فريق
ALUSI:1:6/r6.claim: One linguistic group restricts guidance to direction that actually reaches its destination.
ALUSI:1:6/r6.anchor: ففريق خصها بالدلالة الموصلة وآخرون بالدلالة على ما يوصل

ALUSI:1:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r7.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI:1:6/r7.claim: Another group defines guidance as indicating what leads to the destination, without requiring arrival.
ALUSI:1:6/r7.anchor: ففريق خصها بالدلالة الموصلة وآخرون بالدلالة على ما يوصل

ALUSI:1:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r8.speaker: قليل
ALUSI:1:6/r8.claim: A few say direct transitivity means conveying to the destination and belongs only to God, while li or ilā means showing the way and can be ascribed also to the Quran or Prophet.
ALUSI:1:6/r8.anchor: وقليل قال : إن تعدت إلى المفعول الثاني بنفسها

ALUSI:1:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects defining guidance as necessarily reaching the goal: Thamūd were guided but preferred blindness, and the proposed later apostasy does not fit the histories or the verse’s evident sense.
ALUSI:1:6/r9.anchor: والجواب بجواز وقوعهم في الضلال بالارتداد بعد الوصول إلى الحق لا يساعده

ALUSI:1:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r10.claim: He also finds strained attempts to reconcile route-showing with the Prophet’s inability to guide the one he loves, whether by analogy with God’s agency or by limiting whom he can guide.
ALUSI:1:6/r10.anchor: وما يقال إنه على حد قوله

ALUSI:1:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r11.claim: The claim that direct-object guidance belongs only to God conflicts with Arabic usage and with Abraham and the believing man of Pharaoh’s household saying they would guide their addressees.
ALUSI:1:6/r11.anchor: وأما الثالث فإن كلام أهل اللغة لا يساعده بل ينادي بما ينافيه

ALUSI:1:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r12.speaker: طائفة
ALUSI:1:6/r12.claim: Because these analyses have weaknesses, a group says guidance is homonymous; al-Ālūsī says the linguistic question does not turn on Muʿtazilite doctrine.
ALUSI:1:6/r12.anchor: ولهذا الخلل قال طائفة بالاشتراك والبحث لغوي لا دخل للاعتزال فيه

ALUSI:1:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r13.claim: Ṣirāṭ means road and derives, in its original form, from the root for swallowing: the traveler swallows the road or the road swallows the traveler.
ALUSI:1:6/r13.anchor: الصراط } الطريق وأصله بالسين من السرط

ALUSI:1:6/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r14.claim: Al-Azharī records that a desert may ‘eat’ a traveler by wearing him down, or be ‘eaten’ by one who crosses it easily; Abū Tammām’s line illustrates this usage.
ALUSI:1:6/r14.anchor: رعته الفيافي بعد ما كان حقبة

ALUSI:1:6/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r15.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
ALUSI:1:6/r15.claim: Ibn Kathīr in Qunbul’s transmission and Yaʿqūb in Ruways al-Luʾluʾī’s transmission read the original form with sīn.
ALUSI:1:6/r15.anchor: وبالسين على الأصل قرأ ابن كثير برواية قنبل ورويس اللؤلؤي عن يعقوب

ALUSI:1:6/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r16.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:1:6/r16.claim: The majority read ṣirāṭ with ṣād.
ALUSI:1:6/r16.anchor: وبالسين على الأصل قرأ ابن كثير برواية قنبل ورويس اللؤلؤي عن يعقوب ، وقرأ الجمهور بالصاد

ALUSI:1:6/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r17.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI:1:6/r17.claim: Ḥamza gives ṣād an imāla toward zāy; pure zāy is a dialect of ʿUdhra and Kaʿb.
ALUSI:1:6/r17.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بإشمام الصاد زاياً والزاي الخالصة لغة لعذرة وكعب

ALUSI:1:6/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r18.claim: Al-Ālūsī judges the ṣād reading the most eloquent and broadest in usage.
ALUSI:1:6/r18.anchor: والصاد عندي أفصح وأوسع وأهل الحجاز يؤنثون الصراط

ALUSI:1:6/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r19.claim: The Ḥijāzīs treat ṣirāṭ, like ṭarīq, sabīl, zuqāq, and sūq, as feminine; Tamīm treats them as masculine, which is more common.
ALUSI:1:6/r19.anchor: وأهل الحجاز يؤنثون الصراط كالطريق والسبيل والزقاق والسوق

ALUSI:1:6/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r20.claim: If masculine, ṣirāṭ has the abundant plural ṣuruṭ and the expected sparse plural aṣriṭa; if feminine, its expected plural follows the aḏruʿ pattern.
ALUSI:1:6/r20.anchor: ويجمع في الكثرة على صرط ككتاب وكتب وفي القلة قياسه أصرطة

ALUSI:1:6/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r21.claim: The straight path is level, without crookedness.
ALUSI:1:6/r21.anchor: { الصراط المستقيم } المستوى الذي لا اعوجاج فيه

ALUSI:1:6/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r22.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r22.claim: One proposed meaning is the true path.
ALUSI:1:6/r22.anchor: واختلف في المراد منه فقيل الطريق الحق . وقيل ملة الإسلام

ALUSI:1:6/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r23.claim: Another proposed meaning is the religion of Islam.
ALUSI:1:6/r23.anchor: واختلف في المراد منه فقيل الطريق الحق . وقيل ملة الإسلام

ALUSI:1:6/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r24.speaker: الرازي قدس سره
ALUSI:1:6/r24.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects both the true-path and Islam readings because the next verse describes recipients of grace, including earlier peoples who had neither the Quran nor Islam.
ALUSI:1:6/r24.anchor: وقيل القرآن وردهما الرازي قدس سره بأن قوله تعالى : { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم }

ALUSI:1:6/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r25.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that al-Rāzī’s own preferred middle-path reading, supported by 2:143, would face the same objection about earlier peoples; he finds the argument inconsistent.
ALUSI:1:6/r25.anchor: والعجب كل العجب من هذا المولى أنه ذكر في أحد الوجوه المرضية عنده

ALUSI:1:6/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r26.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r26.claim: One reading identifies the straight path as knowledge of how each thing indicates the divine essence and attributes.
ALUSI:1:6/r26.anchor: وقيل المراد به معرفة ما في كل شيء من كيفية دلالته على الذات والصفات

ALUSI:1:6/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r27.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r27.claim: Another reading is the path of earlier people in enduring great hardships for God’s pleasure.
ALUSI:1:6/r27.anchor: وقيل المراد منه صراط الأولين في تحمل المشاق العظيمة لأجل مرضاة الله تعالى

ALUSI:1:6/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r28.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r28.claim: Some identify the path with worship, citing 36:61; al-Ālūsī signals a problem with this argument even while noting that the Quran explains itself.
ALUSI:1:6/r28.anchor: وقيل العبادة لقوله تعالى : { وَأَنِ اعبدوني هذا صراط

ALUSI:1:6/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:6/r29.claim: Another inward reading is turning away from all else and turning wholly toward God.
ALUSI:1:6/r29.anchor: وقيل هو الإعراض عن السوى والإقبال بالكلية على المولى

ALUSI:1:6/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r30.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI:1:6/r30.claim: Ibn ʿArabī defines the path as the establishment of divine oneness in both unification and differentiation.
ALUSI:1:6/r30.anchor: وقال الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره : هو ثبوت التوحيد في الجمع والتفرقة

ALUSI:1:6/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r31.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r31.claim: Al-Ālūsī’s synthesis is that the straight path has a general form for people and a special form for the elect; both are paths of the graced, at different ranks.
ALUSI:1:6/r31.anchor: وعندي بعد الاطلاع على ما للعلماء وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون أن الصراط المستقيم بتنوع إلى عام للناس وخاص بخواصهم

ALUSI:1:6/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r32.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r32.claim: For everyone, the path is adherence to the revealed law in knowledge, action, character, and spiritual state; it is pictured as a bridge over the Hell of disbelief, sin, ignorance, innovation, and passions, embodied in the afterlife according to one’s present state.
ALUSI:1:6/r32.anchor: فالأول : جسر بين العبد وبين الله سبحانه ممدود على متن جهنم

ALUSI:1:6/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r33.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r33.claim: He says ṣirāṭ is used rather than sabīl or ṭarīq to remind the worshipper of the bridge over Hell, although the words otherwise share the sense of path.
ALUSI:1:6/r33.anchor: وللتذكير بذلك الصراط لم يقل السبيل ولا الطريق وإن كان الكل واحدا

ALUSI:1:6/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r34.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r34.claim: For the elect, the path is the journey to God: witnessing that creatures have no independent action, then no life, then are sheer nonexistence marks arrival and completion of the journey to God.
ALUSI:1:6/r34.anchor: الثاني : طريق الوصول إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI:1:6/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r35.claim: After arrival, the journey continues within God without end, as the manifestations of divine beauty and majesty are inexhaustible and the servant keeps ascending between them.
ALUSI:1:6/r35.anchor: ثم يتجدد له السفر فيه سبحانه وهو غير متناه لأن نعوت جماله وجلاله غير متناهية

ALUSI:1:6/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r36.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:1:6/r36.claim: Al-Ālūsī invokes the Prophet’s saying that a cloud comes over his heart and he seeks God’s forgiveness seventy times by day and night, as an indication of ongoing ascent; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:1:6/r36.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إنه ليغان على قلبي فأستغفر الله

ALUSI:1:6/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r37.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r37.claim: At this station God is the servant’s hand, hearing, and sight, so he acts, hears, and sees through God; what lies beyond is veiled from disclosure.
ALUSI:1:6/r37.anchor: وهناك يكون عز شأنه يده وسمعه وبصره فبه يبطش وبه يسمع وبه يبصر ووراء ذلك ما يحرم كشفه

ALUSI:1:6/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r38.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r38.claim: When an ordinary believer asks for guidance, he asks to be led to steadfast obedience to God’s commands and avoidance of prohibitions.
ALUSI:1:6/r38.anchor: فمتى قال العامي اهدنا الصراط المستقيم أراد أرشدنا إلى الاستقامة على امتثال أوامرك واجتناب نواهيك

ALUSI:1:6/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r39.speaker: يعسوب المؤمنين وأبيّ
ALUSI:1:6/r39.claim: For an elect person, the request means being made firm in what God has bestowed; al-Ālūsī says this reading is reported from ʿAlī and Ubayy.
ALUSI:1:6/r39.anchor: وهو المروي عن يعسوب المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه وأبي رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI:1:6/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r40.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r40.claim: The elect seek firmness because each station and state has a beginning and end; one reaches the end only by sound beginnings and moves upward only after becoming rooted in the lower station.
ALUSI:1:6/r40.anchor: ولكل منها بداية ونهاية ولا يصل إلى النهاية ما لم يصحح البداية ولا ينتقل إلى مقام أو حال إلا بعد الرسوخ

ALUSI:1:6/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r41.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r41.claim: One answer to why the already guided believer asks for guidance is: keep us firm against doubts. Al-Ālūsī cites 3:8 and the hadith supplication asking the Turner of hearts to keep hearts firm in religion.
ALUSI:1:6/r41.anchor: أحدها : أن معناه ثبتنا على الدين كيلا تزلزلنا الشبه

ALUSI:1:6/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r42.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r42.claim: A second answer is to ask for increased guidance, as in the statement that those who are guided receive more guidance.
ALUSI:1:6/r42.anchor: وثانيها : أعطنا زيادة الهدى كما قال تعالى

ALUSI:1:6/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r43.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r43.claim: A third answer takes guidance as reward: guide us to Paradise as recompense, supported by the believers’ praise for being guided there.

ALUSI:1:6/r44.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r44.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r44.claim: A fourth answer asks God to show the truth through the remainder of life as He showed it in the past.
ALUSI:1:6/r44.anchor: ورابعها : أن المراد دلنا على الحق في مستقبل عمرنا

ALUSI:1:6/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r45.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r45.claim: Al-Ālūsī tests the link to the preceding request for aid across two choices: aid may cover all important matters or worship alone, and the path may mean truth generally or Islam specifically.
ALUSI:1:6/r45.anchor: لأن طلب المعونة إما في المهمات كلها أو في أداء العبادة

ALUSI:1:6/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r46.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r46.claim: If aid and path are both general or both specific, guidance explains the requested aid and the clauses are separated because of near-complete connection.
ALUSI:1:6/r46.anchor: فعلى تقديري عموم الاستعانة والصراط وخصوصهما يكون اهدنا بيانا للمعونة المطلوبة

ALUSI:1:6/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r47.claim: If aid is general but the path is specifically Islam, the guidance request singles out the greatest aim from all matters, making the separation reflect complete connection.
ALUSI:1:6/r47.anchor: وعلى تقدير عموم الاستعانة وخصوص الصراط يكون اهدنا إفرادا للمقصود الأعظم من جميع المهمات

ALUSI:1:6/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r48.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r48.claim: If aid is restricted to worship while the path is understood generally, al-Ālūsī sees no connection between the two clauses.
ALUSI:1:6/r48.anchor: وأما على تقدير خصوص الاستعانة وعموم الصراط فلا ارتباط

ALUSI:1:6/r49.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r49.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وزيد بن علي
ALUSI:1:6/r49.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read the phrase without the definite article, ṣirāṭan mustaqīman.
ALUSI:1:6/r49.anchor: وقد قرأ الحسن والضحاك وزيد بن علي صراطا مستقيما دون تعريف

ALUSI:1:6/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r50.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI:1:6/r50.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads ṣirāṭ in a genitive construction with al-mustaqīm.
ALUSI:1:6/r50.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق صراط المستقيم بالإضافة

ALUSI:1:6/r51.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:6/r51.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:6/r51.claim: Al-Ālūsī identifies the familiar definite-form reading as the mutawātir reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r1.speaker: ابن كيسان والسيرافي وجمع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r1.claim: Ibn Kaysan, al-Sirafi, and a group construe a part-to-whole genitive as containing an implied partitive min.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r1.anchor: وقال إبن كيسان والسيرافي وجمع إضافة الجزء على معنى ( من ) التبعيضية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r2.speaker: اللمع وشرحه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r2.claim: Al-Lumaʿ and its commentary extend the implied partitive min to genitive constructions generally, whether part-to-whole or particular-to-general.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r2.anchor: بل في اللمع وشرحه إن من المقدرة في الإضافة مطلقا كذلك من غير فرق بين الجزء والجزئي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r3.claim: Some grammarians treat the particular-to-general genitive as explicative; others restrict that analysis to cases where the terms overlap, while making a universal genitive possessive.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r3.anchor: وبعضهم جعل الإضافة في الجزئي بيانية مطلقا وبعضهم خصها بالعموم والخصوص الوجهي كما في المثال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r4.claim: The proposed possessive reading for a universal genitive such as Madinat Baghdad is not supported by common usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r4.anchor: وجعلها في المطلق كمدينة بغداد لامية والشهرة لا تساعده

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r5.claim: Fatihat al-Kitab means the surah that begins the Quran in its established canonical order, not one that begins teaching, prayer recitation, or revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r5.anchor: فاتحة الكتاب لأنها مبدؤه على الترتيب المعهود لا لأنها يفتتح بها في التعليم وفي القراءة في الصلاة كما زعمه الإمام السيوطي ولا لأنها أول سورة نزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r6.claim: Those alternative explanations fail because teaching and revelation order do not match the canonical order, and book here does not mean whatever is recited in prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r6.anchor: لأن المبدئية من حيث التعليم أو النزول تستدعي مراعاة الترتيب في بقية أجزاء الكتاب من تينك الحيثيتين ولا ريب في أن الترتيب التعليمي والنزولي ليسا كالترتيب المعهود

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r7.speaker: المرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r7.claim: Al-Mursi says the surah was named because it was first written on the Preserved Tablet; Alusi says this needs a transmitted report and that writing order could differ even if the canonical order matched the Tablet.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r7.anchor: وحكى المرسي أنها سميت بذلك لأنها أول سورة كتبت في اللوح ويحتاج إلى نقل وإن صححنا أن ترتيب القرآن الذي في مصاحفنا كما في اللوح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r8.claim: Fatihat al-Quran is another name, following the same explanation of its place at the opening.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r8.anchor: فاتحة القرآن لما قدمنا حذو القذة بالقذة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r9.claim: Umm al-Kitab and Umm al-Quran are established names; the prohibition hadith telling people not to say Umm al-Kitab has no basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r9.anchor: أم الكتاب وأم القرآن وحديث لا يقولن أحدكم أم الكتاب وليقل فاتحة الكتاب لا أصل له بل قد ثبت في الصحاح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r10.claim: The surah is an umm because writing, recitation, revelation, or prayer begins with it and what follows comes after it, like a child after its mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r10.anchor: وسميت بذلك لأن الإبتداء كتابة أو تلاوة أو نزولا على قول أو صلاة بها وما بعدها تال لها فهي كالأم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r11.claim: Alternatively, umm evokes a banner leading an army or the leading position of Mecca, Umm al-Qura.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r11.anchor: ويقال أيضا للراية أم لتقدمها وإتباع الجيش لها ومنه أم القرى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r12.speaker: العلامة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r12.claim: Another explanation says al-Fatiha encompasses Quranic aims: praise of God, worship through command and prohibition, and promise and threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r12.anchor: أو لإشتمالها كما قال العلامة على مقاصد المعاني التي في القرآن من الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله ومن التعبد بالأمر والنهي ومن الوعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r13.claim: Worship need not await a prior command: tawhid is its foundation, is signaled at the surah's opening, and the Prophet had already been commanded to affirm it and convey the surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r13.anchor: ويجاب عندنا بعد تسليم العدم للأولية بأن راس العبادة التوحيد وفي الصدر ما يرشد إليه لا سيما وقد سبق تكليفه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالتوحيد وتبليغ السورة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r14.claim: The surah's promise and threat are located either in the contrast between the favored, those under wrath, and the astray, or in the Day of Judgment and its reward and punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r14.anchor: وأما الوعد والوعيد فمن قوله تعالى ( أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r15.claim: These themes match revelation's merciful guidance to worldly and afterlife welfare: knowing the giver of blessings, seeking increase through obedience, and avoiding loss through sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r15.anchor: بعثة الرسل وإنزال الكتب رحمة للعباد وإرشادا إلى ما يصلحهم معاشا ومعادا وذلك بمعرفة من يقدر على إيصال النعم إيجادا وإمدادا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r16.claim: Praise entails knowing God and His attributes; worship includes belief in revelation and angels through the commands, and promise and threat entail belief in the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p34/r16.anchor: ويدخل فيه من وجه الإيمان بالنبوات وما يتعلق بها من الكتاب والملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r1.claim: People differ in what moves them: most respond to desire and fear, the middle to hope and fear, and the few elite to intimacy and awe; these three address worldly and afterlife welfare.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r1.anchor: والناس كابل مائة لا تجد فيها راحلة والأكثرون بعثتهم الرغبة والرهبة وأوسطهم الرجاء والخوف والخواص وقليل ما هم الأنس والهيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r2.claim: The three themes may instead be reduced to two by including praise within worship; Alusi suggests separating them may allude to the Muʿtazili claim that gratitude to the benefactor is rationally obligatory, unlike al-Baydawi's framing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r2.anchor: ولك أن ترد الثلاثة إلى إثنين فتدرج الثناء في التعبد إذ لا حكم للعقل ولعله إنما جعله قسيما له تلميحا إلى أن شكر المنعم واجب عقلا مراعاة لمذهب الإعتزال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r3.claim: A second account says the surah contains Quranic theoretical and practical teachings: theory through the Day of Judgment, practice in worship and seeking the straight path, and the fortunes of the favored and the condemned.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r3.anchor: أو لإشتمالها على جملة معانيه من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الصراط المستقيم والإطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r4.claim: In this scheme, the request for guidance maps to the practical task of following the straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r4.anchor: والثاني من قوله ( إياك ) نعبد وما بعده سلوك الصراط المستقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r5.claim: The favored and those under wrath or astray give the surah its indication of human fortunes, admonitory stories, promise, and threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r5.anchor: الإطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r6.claim: A broader mapping organizes the surah into four religious disciplines: foundations, practical rulings, moral perfection, and accounts of earlier nations with promise and threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r6.anchor: أربعة أنواع من العلوم التي هي مناط الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r7.claim: The foundations are knowledge of God and His attributes, prophecy, and the afterlife, mapped respectively to Lord of the worlds and the Merciful, the favored, and Master of Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r7.anchor: معرفة الله تعالى وصفاته وإليها الإشارة بقوله ( رب العالمين الرحمن الرحيم ) ومعرفة النبوات وهي المرادة بقوله تعالى ( أنعمت عليهم )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r8.claim: Practical branches begin with worship, bodily and financial, and depend on worldly transactions, marriage, and governance, all grounded in the foundations.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r8.anchor: وهو المراد بقوله ( إياك نعبد ) وهي بدنية ومالية وهما مفتقران إلى أمور المعاش

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r9.claim: The moral discipline aims at reaching God's presence and travelling the stations of the straight path, signaled by seeking help and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r9.anchor: علم ما به يحصل الكمال وهو علم الأخلاق وأجله الوصول إلى الحضرة الصمدانية والسلوك لطريقة الإستقامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r10.claim: The final discipline recounts earlier fortunate and miserable communities and their associated promises and threats.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r10.anchor: علم القصص والأخبار عن الأمم السالفة السعداء والأشقياء وما يتصل بها من الوعد والوعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r11.claim: The two schemes that treat the surah as containing all Quranic meanings require taking Kitab as meanings or supplying that sense in the genitive; the first scheme avoids that assumption.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r11.anchor: وهذان الوجهان يستدعيان حمل الكتاب على المعاني أو تقديرها في التركيب الإضافي والوجه الأول لا يقتضيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r12.claim: The report that al-Fatiha equals two-thirds of the Quran does not defeat the summary account: the Quran's greater detail can account for the remaining third of reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p35/r12.anchor: ما ورد من أن الفاتحة تعدل ثلثي القرآن إذ يرى له إذا ثبت أن الإجمال لا يساوي التفصيل فزيادة مبانيه منزلة منزلة ثلث آخر من الثواب

BAGHAWI:1:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r2.speaker: علي وأبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI:1:6/r2.claim: ʿAli and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb interpret the request as “make us firm,” like telling someone already standing to remain standing until one's return.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r2.anchor: وقال علي ، وأبي بن كعب : " ثبتنا " كما يقال للقائم قم حتى أعود إليك ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:6/r3.claim: Believers who already have guidance ask to be made steadfast and to receive further guidance, since God's acts of grace and guidance are inexhaustible according to Sunni theology.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r3.anchor: وهذا الدعاء من المؤمنين مع كونهم على الهداية بمعنى التثبيت وبمعنى طلب مزيد الهداية ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r4.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب
BAGHAWI:1:6/r4.claim: Ruways reports the reading with sīn, ṣirāṭ, which Baghawi calls the original form.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r4.anchor: قرئ بالسين رواه رويس عن يعقوب وهو الأصل ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:6/r5.claim: The word is also read with zāy.

BAGHAWI:1:6/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r6.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI:1:6/r6.claim: Hamza reads it with a zāy-like coloring; all forms are valid dialects, but most readers choose ṣād to match the codex.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بإشمام الزاي ، وكلها لغات صحيحة ، واختيار الصاد ، عند أكثر القراء لموافقة المصحف .

BAGHAWI:1:6/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر ومقاتل
BAGHAWI:1:6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Jabir, and Muqatil identify the straight path as Islam.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجابر : هو الإسلام وهو قول مقاتل ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI:1:6/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the straight path as the Qur'an.

BAGHAWI:1:6/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r9.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI:1:6/r9.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli from the Prophet identifies the straight path as God's Book.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r9.anchor: وروي عن علي مرفوعاً " الصراط المستقيم " كتاب الله ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI:1:6/r10.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the straight path is the road to Paradise.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r10.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : طريق الجنة ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r11.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI:1:6/r11.claim: Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah says it is the way of the Sunna and the community.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r11.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله : طريق السنة والجماعة ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r12.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
BAGHAWI:1:6/r12.claim: Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani says it is the way of God's Messenger.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r12.anchor: وقال بكر بن عبد الله المزني : طريق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r13.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن
BAGHAWI:1:6/r13.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya and al-Hasan identify it as the Messenger, his family, and his two Companions.
BAGHAWI:1:6/r13.anchor: وقال أبو العالية و الحسن : رسول الله وآله وصاحباه ،

BAGHAWI:1:6/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:6/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:6/r14.claim: In ordinary language, ṣirāṭ is a clear road.

BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.claim: In a qudsi report, God divides prayer between Himself and His servant and answers each part of al-Fatiha; Baghawi grades it sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.anchor: قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ، نصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل ،

BAYDAWI:1:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r1.claim: “Guide us” explains the requested assistance—as if God asked how to help—or singles out its greatest aim.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r1.anchor: بيان للمعونة المطلوبة فكأنه قال : كيف أعينكم فقالوا

BAYDAWI:1:6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r2.claim: Hidāya is gentle direction, normally used for good; “lead them to Hell's path” is sarcastic. Related hawādī are the foreparts that lead wild animals.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r2.anchor: والهداية دلالة بلطف ولذلك تستعمل في الخير

BAYDAWI:1:6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r3.claim: Hadā normally governs li- or ilā but here is treated like ikhtāra in “Moses chose his people.”
BAYDAWI:1:6/r3.anchor: والفعل منه هدى ،   وأصله أن يعدى باللام ،   أو إلى

BAYDAWI:1:6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r4.claim: God's kinds of guidance are innumerable like His blessings, yet can be classified in an ordered scheme.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r4.anchor: وهداية الله تعالى تتنوع أنواعا لا يحصيها عد

BAYDAWI:1:6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r5.claim: The first kind grants capacities for finding one's interests, including reason, inner senses, and external perception.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r5.anchor: الأول : إفاضة القوى التي بها يتمكن المرء من الاهتداء إلى مصالحه

BAYDAWI:1:6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r6.claim: The second kind presents signs distinguishing truth from falsehood and good from corruption; verses say people were shown the two paths and Thamud chose blindness.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r6.anchor: نصب الدلائل الفارقة بين الحق والباطل والصلاح والفساد

BAYDAWI:1:6/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r7.claim: The third kind guides through messengers and revealed books, exemplified by leaders guiding by God's command and the Qur'an guiding to the upright path.

BAYDAWI:1:6/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r8.claim: The fourth kind unveils realities to hearts through revelation, inspiration, or true dreams; only prophets and saints attain it.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r8.anchor: الرابع أن يكشف على قلوبهم السرائر ويريهم الأشياء كما هي

BAYDAWI:1:6/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r9.claim: The request may seek increased guidance, perseverance in it, or higher ranks built upon it.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r9.anchor: فالمطلوب إما زيادة ما منحوه من الهدى ،   أو الثبات عليه

BAYDAWI:1:6/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r10.claim: A gnostic who has reached God seeks guidance along the journey to Him, removal of spiritual darkness and bodily veils, and vision by God's holy light.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r10.anchor: فإذا قاله العارف بالله الواصل عنى به أرشدنا طريق السير فيك

BAYDAWI:1:6/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r11.claim: Command and supplication share wording and meaning but differ by superiority or inferiority; another view says the difference is rank.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r11.anchor: والأمر والدعاء يتشاركان لفظا ومعنى ويتفاوتان بالاستعلاء والتسفل

BAYDAWI:1:6/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r12.claim: Ṣirāṭ is linked to sarata, swallowing: the road seems to swallow travelers, hence the name luqam, “gulper.”
BAYDAWI:1:6/r12.anchor: والسراط : من سرط الطعام إذا ابتلعه

BAYDAWI:1:6/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r13.claim: Ṣād replaces original sīn to match emphatic ṭāʾ; the ṣād may be colored with zāy to approach the replaced letter.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r13.anchor: و{ الصراط } من قلب السين صادا ليطابق الطاء في الإطباق

BAYDAWI:1:6/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r14.speaker: ابن كثير برواية قنبل ورويس عن يعقوب
BAYDAWI:1:6/r14.claim: Ibn Kathīr through Qunbul and Ruways from Yaʿqūb read original sīn; Ḥamza uses the mixed pronunciation and others read ṣād, the Quraysh dialect.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير برواية قنبل عنه ،   ورويس عن يعقوب بالأصل

BAYDAWI:1:6/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r15.claim: Ṣirāṭ's plural is suruṭ, like kutub; like ṭarīq, it may be masculine or feminine.
BAYDAWI:1:6/r15.anchor: والثابت في الإمام وجمعه سرط ككتب وهو كالطريق في التذكير والتأنيث

BAYDAWI:1:6/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r16.claim: Al-mustaqīm means level or straight; its intended referent is the path of truth.

BAYDAWI:1:6/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:6/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:6/r17.claim: An alternative identifies the straight path as the religion of Islam.

BIQAI:1:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r1.claim: God teaches His specially favored servants this supplication and alerts them that the way of conduct is necessary for arrival.
BIQAI:1:6/r1.anchor: تلقيناً لأهل لطفه وتنبيهاً على محل السلوك الذي لا وصول بدونه

BIQAI:1:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:6/r2.claim: Al-Harali glosses guidance as returning the strayer to what he had lost.
BIQAI:1:6/r2.anchor: والهدى قال الحرالي : مرجع الضال إلى ما ضل عنه

BIQAI:1:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:6/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes the path as a perilous road of conduct.
BIQAI:1:6/r3.anchor: مرجع الضال إلى ما ضل عنه ،   والصراط الطريق الخطر

BIQAI:1:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r4.claim: The verse is God's own speech, placed on the tongues of the most eminent of His creation.
BIQAI:1:6/r4.anchor: والآية من كلام الله تعالى على لسان العُلّية

BIQAI:1:6/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r5.claim: The definite article identifies the uniquely encompassing path, whose guided traveler does not go astray because its scope is comprehensive.

BIQAI:1:6/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r6.claim: The path encompasses the whole, while opinions and sects fragment when they incline toward one of its sides.
BIQAI:1:6/r6.anchor: وهو الذي تشتت الآراء وتفرقت الفرق بالميل إلى واحد من جانبيه

BIQAI:1:6/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r7.claim: Its likeness is the visible bridge over Hell on Judgment Day, lined with hooks; people's passage there follows how they traveled among its truths during worldly life.

BIQAI:1:6/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:6/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:6/r8.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes praiseworthy lack of orientation, arising from sound nature and calling for restraint, from blameworthy deviation after guidance, arising from a crooked disposition.
BIQAI:1:6/r8.anchor: وهذا الصراط الأكمل وهو المحيط المترتب على الضلال الذي يعبر به عن حال من لا وجهة له ،   وهو ضلال ممدوح

BIQAI:1:7/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r21.claim: Biqāʿī pictures the worshipper passing through unveiled majesty, annihilation of the transient, and visions of many perilous paths, then realizing that only God's guidance, care, and mercy bring safety.
BIQAI:1:7/r21.anchor: وعلم أن لا نجاة إلا بهدايته ولا عصمة بغير عنايته ولا سعادة إلا برحمته ولا سلامة لغير أهل نعمته

BIQAI:1:7/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r22.claim: After recognizing these realities, the worshipper answers the implied question about what to seek and where to go by asking for the straight path.
BIQAI:1:7/r22.anchor: كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي-{[283]} أي مذهب تذهب ؟

BIQAI:1:7/r39.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r39.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r39.claim: Al-Harali sees the Fātiḥa as God's disclosure from the beginning of dominion to praise, and the servants' progress from disavowing error to the straight path; the Qur'an gathers their relation.
BIQAI:1:7/r39.anchor: من بدء الملك إلى ختم الحمد

BIQAI:1:7/r49.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r49.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r49.claim: Al-Harali says the first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, the final three the creatures' approach to God or estrangement from mercy, and the middle verse the bond between them.
BIQAI:1:7/r49.anchor: الآيات الثلاث الأول شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI:1:7/r50.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r50.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI:1:7/r50.claim: In the qudsī report from the Prophet, narrated by Abū Hurayra and recorded by Muslim and the four Sunan collections, God says the guidance request belongs to the servant and the servant receives what he asks; no grading is stated.
BIQAI:1:7/r50.anchor: الحديث القدسي الذي رواه مسلم في صحيحه وأصحاب السنن الأربعة عن أبي هريرة

DURR:1:1/r117.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r117.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r117.claim: The report glosses ihdina as guide us and the straight path as Islam, since other religions lack tawhid.
DURR:1:1/r117.anchor: بقية السورة { اهدنا } أرشدنا { الصراط المستقيم } يعني دين الإسلام

DURR:1:3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:1:3/r3.claim: In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of anger are Jews, and the astray are Christians.
DURR:1:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله { الحمد لله رب العالمين } قال : ما وصف من خلقه . وفي قوله { الرحمن الرحيم } قال : مدح نفسه { ملك يوم الدين }

DURR:1:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r1.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:6/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet read al-sirat with ṣad; al-Hakim authenticated the report, and al-Dhahabi commented against him.
DURR:1:6/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة .   أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } بالصاد

DURR:1:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas read the word with sin.
DURR:1:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس .   أنه قرأ { اهدنا السراط } بالسين

DURR:1:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
DURR:1:6/r3.claim: Abd Allah ibn Kathir read the word with sin.
DURR:1:6/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كثير .   أنه كان يقرأ { السراط } بالسين

DURR:1:6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r4.speaker: الفراء
DURR:1:6/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ reports Hamza's zay reading, pronounced with a pure zay.
DURR:1:6/r4.anchor: عن الفراء قال : قرأ حمزة { الزراط } بالزاي قال الفراء : و { الزراط } بإخلاص الزاي

DURR:1:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r5.speaker: الفراء
DURR:1:6/r5.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the pure-zay form is a dialect of ʿUdhra, Kalb, and Banu al-ʿAyn.
DURR:1:6/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : و { الزراط } بإخلاص الزاي . لغة لعذرة ، وكلب ، وبني العين

DURR:1:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ihdina as asking God to inspire us with His true religion.
DURR:1:6/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } يقول : ألهمنا دينك الحق

DURR:1:6/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the prayer as asking for the rightly guiding road, God's religion without deviation.
DURR:1:6/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } قال :ألهمنا الطريق الهادي

DURR:1:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-sirat means a road or path.
DURR:1:6/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال { الصراط } الطريق

DURR:1:6/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR:1:6/r9.claim: Jabir identifies the straight path as Islam, broader than the distance between heaven and earth; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:1:6/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله في قوله { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } قال : هو الإسلام ، وهو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

DURR:1:6/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the straight path as Islam.
DURR:1:6/r10.anchor: ابن جريج عن ابن عباس قال { الصراط المستقيم } الإسلام

DURR:1:6/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:1:6/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿud and a group of Companions identify the straight path as Islam.
DURR:1:6/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة { الصراط المستقيم } الإسلام

DURR:1:6/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r12.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:6/r12.claim: The Prophet's parable makes the path Islam, its two walls God's limits, its open curtained doors His prohibitions, the caller at its head God's Book, and the caller above the divine admonition in each Muslim heart.
DURR:1:6/r12.anchor: عن النواس بن سمعان عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال " ضرب الله صراطا مستقيما ، وعلى جنبتي الصراط سوران فيهما أبواب مفتحة

DURR:1:6/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:1:6/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the straight path as God's Book and warns that devils attend the path, urging believers to follow it and hold to the Book.
DURR:1:6/r13.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } قال : هو كتاب الله

DURR:1:6/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r14.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:6/r14.claim: In response to a question about deliverance from future trials, the Prophet points to God's Book, describing it as the accounts of the past, news of the future, judgment between people, a firm rope, wise reminder, and straight path; al-Tirmidhi graded the report weak.
DURR:1:6/r14.anchor: عن علي قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول " ستكون فتن قلت : وما المخرج منها ؟ قال : كتاب الله

DURR:1:6/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:1:6/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the straight path is the way the Messenger left them upon.
DURR:1:6/r15.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال { الصراط المستقيم } الذي تركنا عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:1:6/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:1:6/r16.claim: Ibn Masʿud pictures the Messenger leaving people at one end of the straight path, whose other end is in Paradise.
DURR:1:6/r16.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال { الصراط المستقيم } تركنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على طرفه ، والطرف الآخر في الجنة

DURR:1:6/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r17.speaker: رسول الله
DURR:1:6/r17.claim: An unnamed man reports the Prophet calling the Quran the clear light, wise reminder, and straight path.
DURR:1:6/r17.anchor: من طريق قيس بن سعد عن رجل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال " القران هو النور المبين ، والذكر الحكيم ، والصراط المستقيم

DURR:1:6/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r18.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR:1:6/r18.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya identifies the straight path with the Messenger and his two companions; when this was reported to al-Hasan, he affirmed Abu al-ʿAliya was right and sincere.
DURR:1:6/r18.anchor: من طريق عاصم الأحول عن أبي العالية في قوله { الصراط المستقيم } قال : هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه

DURR:1:6/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r19.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the straight path as the Messenger and his two companions; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:1:6/r19.anchor: من طريق أبي العالية عن ابن عباس في قوله { الصراط المستقيم } قال : هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه

DURR:1:6/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r20.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
DURR:1:6/r20.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya al-Riyahi urges learning Islam, not turning away after learning it, and staying on the straight path without veering right or left.
DURR:1:6/r20.anchor: عن أبي العالية الرياحي قال : تعلموا الإسلام ، فإذا علمتموه فلا ترغبوا عنه ، وعليكم بالصراط المستقيم

DURR:1:6/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r21.speaker: سفيان
DURR:1:6/r21.claim: Sufyan says Quranic exegesis has no real disagreement: its comprehensive wording can intend one meaning and another.
DURR:1:6/r21.anchor: عند سفيان قال : ليس في تفسير القرآن اختلاف إنما هو كلام جامع يراد به هذا وهذا

DURR:1:6/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r22.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR:1:6/r22.claim: Abu al-Darda says full understanding of the Quran requires recognizing its multiple interpretive aspects.
DURR:1:6/r22.anchor: عن أبي قلابة قال : قال أبو الدرداء : إنك لا تفقه كل الفقه حتى ترى للقرآن وجوها

DURR:1:6/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:6/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Ali sent him to twelve thousand Kharijites who rejected arbitration, instructing him to summon them to Book and Sunna but to argue from Sunna because the Quran has multiple interpretations.
DURR:1:6/r23.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : سمعت ابن عباس يحدث عن الخوارج الذين أنكروا الحكومة فاعتزلوا علي بن أبي طالب قال : فاعتزل منهم اثنا عشر ألفا

DURR:1:6/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:6/r24.speaker: علي
DURR:1:6/r24.claim: Imran ibn Manah recounts Ibn Abbas's exchange with Ali: Ali agrees Ibn Abbas knows the Book, but says its many-sided meanings require arguing from prophetic traditions, against which the Kharijites have no escape; Ibn Abbas returns and defeats their argument.
DURR:1:6/r24.anchor: عن عمران بن مناح قال : فقال ابن عباس : يا أمير المؤمنين فأنا أعلم بكتاب الله منهم

ABUDAWUD:821/r2.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.claim: In a hadith qudsi transmitted by Abu Hurayra, God divides al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise and glorification receive divine responses, worship is mutual, and the guidance petition belongs to the servant.
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.anchor: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: الله عز وجل
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: In Abū Hurayra's report, God says the prayer is divided between Him and His servant: the opening praise is His, the middle is shared, and the servant receives what he asks in the remainder.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قال الله عز وجل قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.speaker: ربكم
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.claim: The continuation of Ubayy b. Kaʿb's report assigns the first three Fātiḥa verses to God, the middle verse to both, and the final three to the servant; worship is the servant's and aid comes from God.
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.anchor: ثلاث لي وثلاث لك وواحدة بيني وبينك

IBNASHUR:1:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r4.claim: Asking for guidance expresses a desire for sound judgment and admits one's need for knowledge.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r4.anchor: الثالث الرغبة في التحَلي بالرشد والاهتداء بما تضمنه { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم }

IBNASHUR:1:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r1.claim: After praise, the worshipers' confession of exclusive worship and help bridges praise to petition; trusting God's welcome and hoping for His favor, they ask for guidance.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r1.anchor: فكان ذلك واسطة بين الثناء وبين الطلب

IBNASHUR:1:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r2.claim: The petition is the purpose of the preface, like the subject of a speech or the transition in a poem, fitting the Fātiḥa as a preamble to a book sent as guidance and mercy.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r2.anchor: فهذا هو التوجيه المناسب لكون الفاتحة بمنزلة الديباجة للكتاب الذي أنزل هدى للناس ورحمة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR:1:6/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the petition as an answer to an unstated question; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers to read it as the natural aim of the preceding praise and confession.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r3.anchor: على ما ذهب إليه صاحب « الكشاف »

IBNASHUR:1:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r4.claim: The petition is separated from the preceding clauses because those clauses are declarative while this one is imperative.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r4.anchor: ولاختلاف الجمل المتقدمة معها بالخبرية والإنشائية فصلت هذه عنهن

IBNASHUR:1:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r5.claim: Guidance is gentle direction, especially direction toward what benefits its recipient; its gentleness suits someone for whom good is intended.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r5.anchor: والهداية الدلالة بتلطف ولذلك خصت بالدلالة لما فيه خير المدلول

IBNASHUR:1:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r6.claim: Hadā takes one direct object because its sense resembles irshād, and takes the person guided as a second object through ilā or lām.

IBNASHUR:1:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r7.claim: The prepositional constructions mean bringing someone to knowledge or guiding them for a purpose; Qur'anic examples use both ilā and li-.

IBNASHUR:1:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r8.claim: An explanation says direct-object use for the second object is a Hijazi idiom, while other dialects require a preposition; another analysis calls it ellipsis and connection.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r8.anchor: قيل هي لغة أهل الحجاز وأما غيرهم فلا يعديه بنفسه وقد جعلوا تعديته بنفسه من التوسع المعبر عنه بالحذف والإيصال

IBNASHUR:1:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r9.claim: An unnamed view distinguishes direct-object use for someone already on the path from prepositional use for someone not yet travelling it.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r9.anchor: وقيل الفرق بين المتعدي وغيره أن المتعدي يستعمل في الهداية لمن كان في الطريق ونحوه ليزداد هدى

IBNASHUR:1:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r10.claim: He rejects that distinction as, at most, a prevalent usage rather than proof that the verb changes meaning with its construction; both huda and hidaya are verbal nouns, while the source noun is hady.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r10.anchor: والحق أن هذا إن تم فهو أغلبي على أنه تخصيص من الاستعمال فلا يقتضي كون الفعل مختلف المعنى

IBNASHUR:1:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r11.claim: Hadā necessarily takes one object; for a second, it is direct when it means showing or clarifying, and prepositional when it means general guidance or pointing, so construction signals the embedded sense.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r11.anchor: فالحق أنه إن اعتبر فيه معنى الإراءة والإبانة تعدى بنفسه وإن اعتبر فيه مطلق الإرشاد والإشارة فهو متعد بالحرف

IBNASHUR:1:6/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r12.claim: The basic sense is showing someone the route to a destination; guidance meanings developed as widely used metaphors from this literal sense.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r12.anchor: حقيقة الهداية الدلالة على الطريق للوصول إلى المكان المقصود فالهادي هو العارف بالطرق

IBNASHUR:1:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r13.claim: The migration report says Abū Bakr hired a skilled route guide from Banū al-Dayl, illustrating the literal Arabic sense of hādī.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r13.anchor: إن أبا بكر استأجر رجلاً من بني الديل

IBNASHUR:1:6/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r14.claim: In religious usage when ascribed to God, guidance is direction toward deeds pleasing to Him; its opposite, misguidance, is leading someone astray.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r14.anchor: والهداية في اصطلاح الشرع حين تسند إلى الله تعالى هي الدلالة على ما يرضي الله من فعل الخير ويقابلها الضلالة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r15.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:1:6/r15.claim: The majority, including the Ashʿarites, define guidance as showing the way to an end whether or not arrival occurs; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this correct.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r15.anchor: فالجمهور على عدم اعتباره وأنها الدلالة على طريق الوصول

IBNASHUR:1:6/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r16.speaker: جماعة منهم الزمخشري
IBNASHUR:1:6/r16.claim: A group including al-Zamakhsharī requires successful delivery in the definition, lest guidance fail to differ from misguidance; their dispute reflects different accounts of divine command and will versus creation.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r16.anchor: وذهب جماعة منهم الزمخشري إلى أن الهداية هي الدلالة مع الإيصال وإلا لما امتازت عن الضلالة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r17.claim: There is no dispute that guidance culminating in arrival is what religiously should be sought from both guide and guided, though a guide may err or the recipient may reject it.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r17.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن الهداية مع الوصول هي المطلوبة شرعاً من الهادي والمهدي

IBNASHUR:1:6/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r18.speaker: عبد الحكيم
IBNASHUR:1:6/r18.claim: ʿAbd al-Ḥakīm chooses a shared sense covering both outcomes because the Qur'an uses guidance for each; absent contrary evidence, neither homonymy nor metaphor is assumed.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r18.anchor: وهذا معنى ما اختار عبد الحكيم أنها موضوعة في الشرع لقدر المشترك لورودها في القرآن في كل منهما

IBNASHUR:1:6/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r19.claim: Guidance comprises four ordered kinds: innate powers for human existence, rational proofs distinguishing truth, revealed messengers and books for harder matters, and disclosure of higher truths.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r19.anchor: والهداية أنواع تندرج كثرتها تحت أربعة أجناس مترتبة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r20.claim: The first kind gives sensory and motor powers, from an infant's instinctive feeding and responses to danger through practical needs and the rational power that derives unknowns from knowns.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r20.anchor: الأول إعطاء القوى المحركة والمدركة التي بها يكون الاهتداء إلى انتظام وجود ذات الإنسان

IBNASHUR:1:6/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r21.claim: The second kind is theoretical knowledge supplied by proofs that distinguish truth from falsehood and correctness from error.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r21.anchor: نصب الأدلة الفارقة بين الحق والباطل والصواب والخطأ

IBNASHUR:1:6/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r22.claim: The third kind comes through messengers, revealed books, and measures of justice for matters beyond proof or too burdensome to settle by proof, as in God's description of the messengers.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r22.anchor: الثالث الهداية إلى ما قد تقصر عنه الأدلة أو يفضي إعمالها في مثله إلى مشقة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r23.claim: The highest kind unveils higher realities and meanings beyond the reach of rational minds through revelation, sound inspiration, or divine manifestations.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r23.anchor: الرابع أقصى أجناس الهداية وهي كشف الحقائق العليا وإظهار أسرار المعاني التي حارت فيها ألباب العقلاء

IBNASHUR:1:6/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r24.claim: What a particular supplicant seeks depends on that person's or group's condition; as a prayer taught to all Quran-addressed believers, it requests kinds of guidance distributed according to each person's capacity.

IBNASHUR:1:6/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r25.claim: Some guidance is sought for acquisition by those who lack it, while guidance already possessed, including much of the innate first kind, is sought for its continuance.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r25.anchor: فبعض أنواع الهداية مطلوب حصوله لمن لم يبلغ إليه

IBNASHUR:1:6/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r26.claim: A request form ordinarily asks that an act or abstention occur; asking only for continuance is figurative, as in the address to believers in 4:136.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r26.anchor: وصيغة الطلب موضوعة لطلب حصول الماهية المطلوبة من فعل أو كف فإذا استعملت في طلب الدوام كان استعمالها مجازاً

IBNASHUR:1:6/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r27.claim: Asking for more guidance remains literal when some levels are attained and others lack; seeking increase also entails asking that existing guidance endure, making the request a kināya for continuance as well.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r27.anchor: وأما إذا استعملت في طلب الدوام للزيادة مما حصل بعضه ولم يحصل بعضه فهي مستعملة في معناها

IBNASHUR:1:6/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r28.claim: For the Prophet, who had reached guidance's highest degree, the wording is figurative and an appropriation of the verse; the verse itself asks for complete guidance through further attainment and continuance.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r28.anchor: ويكون دعاؤه ذلك اقتباساً من الآية وليس عين المراد من الآية

IBNASHUR:1:6/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r29.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r29.claim: Ṣirāṭ means a road; Arabic dialects pronounce it with ṣād or sīn, while the Hijaz dialect uses ṣād, an emphatic substitution easing the transition into emphatic ṭā.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r29.anchor: والصراط الطريق وهو بالصاد وبالسين وقد قرىء بهما في المشهورة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r30.speaker: الجعبري
IBNASHUR:1:6/r30.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī says Arabs change sīn to ṣād before several consonants; here ṣād matches ṭā in emphasis and elevation, avoiding a difficult movement from low articulation to high.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r30.anchor: عن الجعبري إنهم يفعلون ذلك في كل سين بعدها غين أو خاء أو قاف أو طاء

IBNASHUR:1:6/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r31.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR:1:6/r31.claim: Qays pronounces an intermediate sound between sīn and ṣād, called ishām, which Ḥamza reads in the transmission of Khalaf; al-Qurṭubī reports a pure zāy dialect among ʿUdhra, Kalb, and Banū al-Qayn, but says it is weak and unread.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r31.anchor: وقيس قلبوا السين بين الصاد والزاي وهو إشمام وقرأ به حمزة في رواية خلف عنه

IBNASHUR:1:6/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r32.speaker: ابن كثير في رواية قنبل
IBNASHUR:1:6/r32.claim: Most canonical readers use the eloquent ṣād form, while Ibn Kathīr in Qunbul's transmission reads sīn; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers ṣād for its conformity to the muṣḥaf spelling and the eloquent dialect.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r32.anchor: جمهور القراء وقرأ بالسين ابن كثير في رواية قنبل

IBNASHUR:1:6/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r33.claim: The Companions wrote ṣād to mark the more eloquent form in Quraysh usage; readers of sīn understood the written form as allowing known dialectal alternation, so the difference concerns pronunciation, not the word's lexical substance.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r33.anchor: فالذين قرأوا بالسين تأولوا أن الصحابة لم يتركوا لغة السين للعلم بها

IBNASHUR:1:6/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r34.claim: The spelling of al-muṣayṭir with ṣād likewise preserves a form whose origin is sīn, illustrating how the written ṣād need not rule out sīn pronunciation.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r34.anchor: كما كتبوا المصيطر بالصاد مع العلم بأن أصله السين

IBNASHUR:1:6/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r35.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ is an Arabic word, although al-Naqqāsh and Ibn al-Jawzī report it as the Roman word for road; Abū Ḥātim is also cited, and al-Suyūṭī consequently listed it among loanwords.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r35.anchor: عن النقاش وابن الجوزي أنه الطريق بلغة الروم

IBNASHUR:1:6/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r36.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r36.claim: The road is a metaphor for truth, through which a person reaches the success of God's approval that Islam seeks.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r36.anchor: والصراط في هذه الآية مستعار لمعنى الحق الذي يبلغ به مدركه إلى الفوز برضاء الله

IBNASHUR:1:6/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r37.claim: Mustaqīm is the active participle of istiqāma, the result of making something straight; it means having no bend or detour.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r37.anchor: والمستقيم اسم فاعل استقام مطاوع قومته فاستقام

IBNASHUR:1:6/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r38.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r38.claim: A straight road is best because it reaches the destination most directly, without leading its traveller astray, causing hesitation, or producing confusion.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r38.anchor: وأحسن الطرق الذي يكون مستقيماً وهو الجادة لأنه باستقامته يكون أقرب إلى المكان المقصود

IBNASHUR:1:6/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r39.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r39.claim: By metaphor, the straight path is clear truth unmixed with false suspicion, like a road without branching side tracks.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r39.anchor: والمستقيم هنا مستعار للحق البين الذي لا تخلطه شبهة باطل فهو كالطريق الذي لا تتخلله بنيات

IBNASHUR:1:6/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r40.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:1:6/r40.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the straight path as the true religion and is also reported to call it the religion of Islam; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the two glosses explain one another.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r40.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الصراط المستقيم دين الحق

IBNASHUR:1:6/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r41.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r41.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's gloss does not mean asking for an obsolete religion: all divinely revealed religions were straight paths for their own communities, as Satan's words about God's path also show.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r41.anchor: ولا يريد أنهم لقنوا الدعاء بطلب الهداية إلى دين مضى وإن كانت الأديان الإلهية كلها صرطاً مستقيمة بحسب أحوال أممها

IBNASHUR:1:6/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r42.claim: The definite article evokes a mentally understood kind, requested through its unique instance: straightness is singular, while misguidance has many forms.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r42.anchor: لأنهم سألوا الهداية لهذا الجنس في ضمن فرد وهو الفرد المنحصر فيه الاستقامة

IBNASHUR:1:6/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r43.speaker: author
