IBNASHUR:1:6/r43.claim: One possible reading takes the path as Islam: God taught this prayer to display His favor, having guided them through earlier Qur'an and continuing to guide through later Qur'an and Prophetic instruction.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r43.anchor: وقد يوجه هذا التفسير بحصول الهداية إلى الإسلام فعلمهم الله هذا الدعاء لإظهار منته

IBNASHUR:1:6/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r44.claim: The Qur'an explicitly identifies a straight path as the upright religion to which God guided the Prophet.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r44.anchor: قل إنني هداني ربي إلى صراط مستقيم ديناً قيماً

IBNASHUR:1:6/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r45.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r45.claim: He prefers that the path mean all sound knowledge, beliefs, and deeds: enabling people to recognize truth and distinguish it from error according to their capacities, without deviation or religious doubts.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r45.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن المراد بالصراط المستقيم المعارف الصالحات كلها من اعتقاد وعمل بأن يوفقهم إلى الحق

IBNASHUR:1:6/r46.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r46.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r46.claim: This reading is preferable because people need guidance in every affair, including preserving existing goodness from deficiency or deviation; guidance to Islam continues through its revealed and inferred laws, not only initial acceptance.
IBNASHUR:1:6/r46.anchor: وهذا أولى ليكون الدعاء طلب تحصيل ما ليس بحاصل وقت الطلب وإن المرء بحاجة إلى هذه الهداية في جميع شؤونه كلها

IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.claim: The comprehensive reading makes the transition to the following request, for the path excluding those under anger or astray, apt to the context.

IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.claim: Under each account of the favored, the request for guidance has the same possible force explained for the preceding verse: attainment, increase, or continuance.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.anchor: والقول في المطلوب من { اهدنا } على هذه التقادير كلها كالقول فيما تقدم من كون { اهدنا } لطلب الحصول أو الزيادة أو الدوام

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r1.claim: Ihdinā is a request from the subject to the Lord; an imperative from a subordinate is supplication, while one from a superior is a command.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { اهدنا } رغبة لأنها من المربوب إلى الرب ،   وهكذا صيغة الأمر كلها

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r2.claim: The basic lexical meaning of guidance is direction, and its interpretive senses return on reflection to direction.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r2.anchor: والهداية في اللغة الإرشاد( {[74]} ) ،   لكنها تتصرف على وجوه يعبرعنها المفسرون بغير لفظ الإرشاد

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r3.claim: Guidance may mean creating faith in the heart, as illustrated by 2:5, 10:25, 28:56, and 6:125.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r3.anchor: فالهدى يجيء بمعنى خلق الإيمان في القلب ،   ومنه قوله تعالى : { أولئك على هدى من ربهم }

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r4.speaker: أبو المعالي
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r4.claim: Abū al-Maʿālī says guidance in 6:125 must mean creating faith in the heart, and calls this pure direction.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r4.anchor: قال أبو المعالي : فهذه آية لا يتجه حملها إلا على خلق الإيمان في القلب ،   وهو محض الإرشاد

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r5.claim: Guidance can mean calling people: 13:7 calls a guide a caller, and 42:52 says the Prophet guides to a straight path; this is initial direction whether or not people respond.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r5.anchor: وقد جاء الهدى بمعنى الدعاء ،   من ذلك قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r6.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r6.claim: The exegetes understand 20:50 as God inspiring all creatures with knowledge of their benefits; this too entails direction.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون : معناه «ألهم الحيوانات كلها إلى منافعها »

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r7.claim: The exegetes gloss “We guided Thamūd” in 41:17 as “We made clear to them.”

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r8.speaker: أبو المعالي
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r8.claim: Abū al-Maʿālī instead interprets the guidance of Thamūd in 41:17 as calling them.

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r9.claim: The statement “upon Us is guidance” in 92:12 means that God undertakes to make the way clear.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r9.anchor: ومن ذلك قوله تعالى : { إن علينا للهدى }

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r10.speaker: أبو المعالي
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r10.claim: Guidance may mean leading believers along routes to Paradise, as in 47:4–5, or leading people along the path to Hell in 37:23.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r10.anchor: قال أبو المعالي : وقد ترد الهداية والمراد بها إرشاد المؤمنين إلى مسالك الجنان والطرق المفضية إليها

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies the requested guidance with direction along a worldly path, the opposite of going astray; the wording “path” makes this the sound interpretation.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r11.anchor: وهذه الهداية بعينها هي التي تقال في طرق الدنيا ،   وهي ضد الضلال

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r12.speaker: اللحياني
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r12.claim: Al-Liḥyānī treats hudā, “guidance,” as masculine, though the author calls the word feminine.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r12.anchor: والهدى لفظ مؤنث ،   وقال اللحياني : «هو مذكر »

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r13.speaker: ابن سيده
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r13.claim: Ibn Sīda says hudā is also a name for daylight; Ibn Muqbil's verse uses that sense.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r13.anchor: قال ابن سيده( {[86]} ) : «والهدى اسم من أسماء النهار »( {[87]} ) قال ابن مقبل

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r14.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ means a clear road, as shown by Jarīr's description of the straight path.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r14.anchor: في اللغة الطريق الواضح فمن ذلك قول جرير

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r15.claim: An unnamed poet also uses the expression “the clear path” as a road image.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r15.anchor: ومنه قول الآخر : فصد عن نهج الصراط الواضح

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r16.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r16.claim: Al-Naqqāsh claims that ṣirāṭ means “road” in the Roman language; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this very weak.

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r17.speaker: ابن كثير وجماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r17.claim: Ibn Kathīr and a group read al-sirāṭ with sīn, which the author identifies as the original form of the word.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r17.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وجماعة من العلماء : «السراط » بالسين ،   وهذا هو أصل اللفظة

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r18.speaker: الفارسي
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r18.claim: Al-Fārisī says a ṣād pronunciation is also transmitted from Ibn Kathīr.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r18.anchor: قال الفارسي : «ورويت عن ابن كثير بالصاد »

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r19.speaker: السبعة غير حمزة
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r19.claim: The seven readers other than Ḥamza use a pure ṣād, replacing sīn to harmonize with the emphatic ṭāʾ; Sibawayh calls it a dialect.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r19.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة غير حمزة بصاد خالصة وهذا بدل السين بالصاد لتناسبها مع الطاء في الإطباق

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r20.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported with both sīn and ṣād, and with an intermediate sound between ṣād and zāy.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r20.anchor: روي عن أبي عمرو السين والصاد

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r21.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r21.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports that Abū ʿAmr used a pure zāy.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r21.anchor: وروى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو أنه قرأها بزاي خالصة

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r22.speaker: بعض اللغويين
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r22.claim: Some linguists reject al-Aṣmaʿī's report as a mishearing of Abū ʿAmr's intermediate pronunciation; Ibn Mujāhid is cited for this criticism.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r22.anchor: قال بعض اللغويين : «ما حكاه الأصمعي من هذه القراءة خطأ منه

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r23.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r23.claim: Ḥamza reads with an intermediate sound between ṣād and zāy; one transmission says he uses it only in the definite form.

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r24.speaker: ابن مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r24.claim: Ibn Mujāhid calls the intermediate sound difficult and not a letter used to build words, yet accepts it as Arab speech and prefers the clearer, broader ṣād.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r24.anchor: قال ابن مجاهد : «وهذه القراءة تكلف حرف بين حرفين ،   وذلك أصعب على اللسان

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r25.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r25.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r25.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the phrase with an indefinite noun: “guide us to a straight path.”

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r26.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r26.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r26.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq reads ṣirāṭ in a genitive construction with al-mustaqīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r26.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد الصادق : «اهدنا صراطَ المستقيم » بالإضافة

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r27.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r27.speaker: ثابت البناني
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r27.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī reads “show us the path” in place of “guide us.”

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r28.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r28.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r28.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib identifies the straight path as the Qurʾān.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r28.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : «{ الصراط المستقيم } هنا القرآن »

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r29.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r29.speaker: جابر
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r29.claim: Jābir identifies the straight path as Islam, or the upright religion, and says its breadth spans heaven and earth.

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r30.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r30.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r30.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya says the straight path is God's religion, the only religion He accepts from servants.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r30.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية : «هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره »

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r31.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r31.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r31.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the path with the Prophet and his two Companions, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; al-Ḥasan affirms that he spoke truly and advised well.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r31.anchor: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه أبو بكر وعمر

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r32.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r32.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r32.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reconciles the interpretations: the prayer asks to follow the favored—prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous—in belief and observance, encompassing Qurʾān, Islam, and the Prophet's way with his Companions.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r32.anchor: ويجتمع من هذه الأقوال كلها أن الدعوة إنما هي في أن يكون الداعي

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r33.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r33.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r33.claim: Since believers already hold beliefs and perform some acts, “guide us” asks for firmness and continuance in what they have, and direction toward what ignorance or lax observance leaves undone.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r33.anchor: فمعنى قولهم { اهدنا } فيما هو حاصل عندهم طلب التثبيت والدوام ،   وفيما ليس بحاصل

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r34.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r34.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r34.claim: Every petitioner seeks the complete path in speech, action, and belief, so one who possesses only part can rightly ask for the whole.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r34.anchor: إن كل داع فإنما يريد { الصراط } بكماله في أقواله وأفعاله ومعتقداته

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r35.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r35.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r35.claim: Because guidance here is qualified by “to a path,” it cannot mean creating faith in the heart or simply calling people; the other senses of guidance can fit.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r35.anchor: ولا يتجه أن يراد ب { اهدنا } في هذه الآية اخلق الإيمان في قلوبنا ،   لأنها هداية مقيدة إلى صراط

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r36.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r36.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r36.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ is the second object of the verb “guide.”
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r36.anchor: و { الصراط } نصب على المفعول الثاني

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r37.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r37.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r37.claim: Al-mustaqīm is without crookedness or deviation, established upon truth and leading to success and entry into Paradise.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r37.anchor: الذي لا عوج فيه ولا انحراف ،   والمراد أنه استقام

IBNATIYYA:1:6/r38.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r38.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r38.claim: Mustaqīm derives from mustaqwim: the wāw's vowel shifted to qāf, and wāw became yāʾ after kasra.
IBNATIYYA:1:6/r38.anchor: إعلال { مستقيم } أن أصله مستقوم نقلت الحركة إلى القاف

KASHSHAF:1:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r1.claim: Hada normally takes li or ila, as in 17:9 and 42:52, but here takes a direct object by analogy with ikhtara in 7:155.
KASHSHAF:1:6/r1.anchor: هدى أصله أن يتعدى باللام أو بإلى

KASHSHAF:1:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r2.claim: Already guided worshippers ask for increased guidance through divine grace, as in 47:17 and 29:69.

KASHSHAF:1:6/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r3.speaker: علي وأبي
KASHSHAF:1:6/r3.claim: Ali and Ubayy explain ihdina as thabbitna, keep us firm.
KASHSHAF:1:6/r3.anchor: وعن علي وأبي رضي الله عنهما : اهدنا ثبتنا

KASHSHAF:1:6/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r4.claim: Imperative and supplicatory forms are alike because both request; they differ only in rank.
KASHSHAF:1:6/r4.anchor: وصيغة الأمر والدعاء واحدة ، لأن كل واحد منهما طلب

KASHSHAF:1:6/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r5.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF:1:6/r5.claim: Abdullah reads arshidna, guide us rightly.

KASHSHAF:1:6/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r6.claim: Sirat means the main road, named from swallowing because it swallows travelers, like luqman, the gulper.

KASHSHAF:1:6/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r7.claim: Sīn becomes ṣād before ṭā; ṣād can sound like zāy, but pure ṣād is the eloquent Qurayshi codex form.

KASHSHAF:1:6/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r8.claim: Sirat has plural surut, like kitab and kutub, and can be masculine or feminine like tariq and sabil.
KASHSHAF:1:6/r8.anchor: ويجمع سرطا ، نحو كتاب وكتب ، ويذكر ويؤنث كالطريق والسبيل

KASHSHAF:1:6/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:6/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:6/r9.claim: The straight path is the path of truth, the religion of Islam.
KASHSHAF:1:6/r9.anchor: والمراد طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

MAWARDI:1:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r1.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r1.claim: One interpretation of ihdina is guide us and show us the way.

MAWARDI:1:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:1:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets ihdina as grant us success.
MAWARDI:1:6/r2.anchor: معناه وفقنا ،   وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI:1:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r3.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r3.claim: Sirat can mean the straight path, illustrated by Jarir’s verse about the commander being on a straight course when routes bend.
MAWARDI:1:6/r3.anchor:
أنه السبيل المستقيم ،   ومنه قول جرير :
أَميرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى صِراطٍ	 ***  	إذَا اعْوَجَّ الْمَوَارِدُ مُسْتَقِيم

MAWARDI:1:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r4.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r4.claim: Sirat can also mean a clear road, as in 7:86 and the cited verse about turning from the clear path.
MAWARDI:1:6/r4.anchor:
أنه الطريق الواضح ،   ومنه قوله تعالى :
{ وَلاَ تَقْعُدُوا بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ تُوعِدُون }{[19]} وقال الشاعر

MAWARDI:1:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:6/r5.claim: Sirat derives from the passage of food as it moves through the throat.
MAWARDI:1:6/r5.anchor: وهو مشتق من مُسْتَرَطِ الطعام ،   وهو ممره في الحلق

MAWARDI:1:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r6.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r6.claim: The already guided ask for guidance to continue and remain constant.
MAWARDI:1:6/r6.anchor: أنهم دعوا باستدامة الهداية ،   وإن كانوا قد هُدُوا

MAWARDI:1:6/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r7.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r7.claim: Alternatively, the prayer asks God to increase their guidance.

MAWARDI:1:6/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r8.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:6/r8.claim: A third view sees the request as sincere desire for guidance and hope for the reward of prayer.
MAWARDI:1:6/r8.anchor: دعوا بها إخلاصاً للرغبة ،   ورجاءً لثواب الدعاء

MAWARDI:1:6/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r9.speaker: علي وعبد الله
MAWARDI:1:6/r9.claim: Ali and Abdullah identify the straight path as God’s Book; a similar interpretation is attributed to the Prophet.
MAWARDI:1:6/r9.anchor: أنه كتاب الله تعالى ،   وهو قول علي وعبد الله ،   ويُرْوَى نحوه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:1:6/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r10.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI:1:6/r10.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet likewise identifies the straight path as God’s Book; no grading is given.
MAWARDI:1:6/r10.anchor: ويروى نحوه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:1:6/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله ومحمد بن الحنفية
MAWARDI:1:6/r11.claim: Jabir ibn Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya identify the straight path as Islam.
MAWARDI:1:6/r11.anchor: أنه الإسلام ،   وهو قول جابر بن عبد الله ،   ومحمد بن الحنفية

MAWARDI:1:6/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:1:6/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies it as the way guiding to God’s religion, without any crookedness.
MAWARDI:1:6/r12.anchor: أنه الطريق الهادي إلى دين الله تعالى ،   الذي لا عوج فيه ،   وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI:1:6/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:6/r13.speaker: الحسن البصري وأبو العالية الرياحي
MAWARDI:1:6/r13.claim: Hasan al-Basri and Abu al-Aliya al-Riyahi identify the path as the Messenger and the best of his family and Companions.
MAWARDI:1:6/r13.anchor: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأخيار أهل بيته وأصحابه ،   وهو قول الحسن البصري وأبي العالية الرياحي

NASAFI:1:1/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:1/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
NASAFI:1:1/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s dialogue dividing the Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise, glorification, and exaltation belong to God; the worshipper’s request for guidance and the response to it belong to the servant, while worship and aid are shared.
NASAFI:1:1/r12.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

NASAFI:1:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:6/r1.claim: The request can mean ‘keep us firm on the clear way,’ like telling someone already standing to keep standing until one returns, or ‘guide us in the future as You have guided us now.’
NASAFI:1:6/r1.anchor: أي ثبتنا على المنهاج الواضح كقولك للقائم : قم حتى أعود إليك أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه

NASAFI:1:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:6/r2.claim: Hada is normally transitive to one object but can take another directly, as here, or with li or ila, as in the cited verses.
NASAFI:1:6/r2.anchor: وهدى يتعدى بنفسه إلى مفعول واحد ، فأما تعديه إلى مفعول آخر فقد جاء متعديا إليه بنفسه كهذه الآية

NASAFI:1:6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:6/r3.claim: Sirat means the broad road, from the verb ‘to swallow’: the road seems to swallow travelers who take it.
NASAFI:1:6/r3.anchor: والسراط : الجادة من سرط الشيء إذا ابتلعه كأنه يسرط السابلة إذا سلكوه

NASAFI:1:6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r4.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI:1:6/r4.claim: Hamza reads the ṣād with a trace of zāy, since zāy is closer to ṭā’ because both are voiced.
NASAFI:1:6/r4.anchor: وقد تشم الصاد صوت الزاي لأن الزاي إلى الطاء أقرب

NASAFI:1:6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
NASAFI:1:6/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir reads sirat with sīn throughout the Qur’an, preserving the word’s original form.
NASAFI:1:6/r5.anchor: والسين قراءة ابن كثير في كل القرآن وهي الأصل في الكلمة

NASAFI:1:6/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r6.speaker: الباقون
NASAFI:1:6/r6.claim: The remaining readers use a plain ṣād, the Quraysh dialect and the form preserved in the authoritative codex.
NASAFI:1:6/r6.anchor: والباقون بالصاد الخالصة وهي لغة قريش وهي الثابتة في المصحف الإمام

NASAFI:1:6/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:6/r7.claim: Sirat can be masculine or feminine, like tariq and sabil.

NASAFI:1:6/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:6/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:6/r8.claim: The straight path refers to the way of truth, the religion of Islam.
NASAFI:1:6/r8.anchor: والمراد به طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

QURTUBI:1:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r1.claim: The servant asks God to direct and show him the straight way of guidance leading to intimacy with and nearness to God.
QURTUBI:1:6/r1.anchor: اهدنا دعاء ورغبة من المربوب إلى الرب

QURTUBI:1:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI:1:6/r2.claim: The sura's prayer joins praise and requests; this prayer is excellent because the supplicant uses God's own words.
QURTUBI:1:6/r2.anchor: قال بعض العلماء : فجعل الله جل وعز عظم الدعاء وجملته موضوعا في هذه السورة

QURTUBI:1:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:6/r3.claim: A hadith says nothing is more precious to God than supplication; no grading is supplied.
QURTUBI:1:6/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( ليس شيء أكرم على الله من الدعاء )

QURTUBI:1:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:1:6/r4.claim: Another explanation is: guide us by enabling us to use the prophetic practices in fulfilling Your obligations.
QURTUBI:1:6/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى : أرشدنا باستعمال السنن في أداء فرائضك

QURTUBI:1:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r5.claim: The root idea of guidance is inclination: 7:156 says “we have turned toward You”; related usages describe swaying, a gift passing between owners, and sacrificial livestock driven to the sanctuary, hence a prayer that hearts incline to truth.
QURTUBI:1:6/r5.anchor: وقيل : الأصل فيه الإمالة ومنه قوله تعالى

QURTUBI:1:6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r6.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI:1:6/r6.claim: Al-Fudayl identifies the straight path as pilgrimage; al-Qurtubi calls this particular and prefers the general meaning.
QURTUBI:1:6/r6.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض : " الصراط المستقيم " طريق الحج

QURTUBI:1:6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r7.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
QURTUBI:1:6/r7.claim: Ibn al-Hanafiyya identifies the straight path as God's religion, the only religion He accepts from worshippers.
QURTUBI:1:6/r7.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية في قوله عز وجل  " اهدنا الصراط المستقيم "  : هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العبادة غيره

QURTUBI:1:6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI:1:6/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the path is the Prophet and his two Companions; Asim al-Ahwal transmits this view.
QURTUBI:1:6/r8.anchor: قال عاصم الأحول عن أبي العالية : " الصراط المستقيم " رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده

QURTUBI:1:6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:1:6/r9.claim: Al-Hasan affirms that Abu al-Aliya spoke truly and sincerely in identifying the path as the Prophet and his two Companions.
QURTUBI:1:6/r9.anchor: قال عاصم فقلت للحسن : إن أبا العالية يقول : " الصراط المستقيم " رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه قال : صدق ونصح

QURTUBI:1:6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r10.speaker: عامر بن الطفيل
QURTUBI:1:6/r10.claim: Sirat means road in Arabic; Amir ibn al-Tufayl's verse uses it in this sense.
QURTUBI:1:6/r10.anchor: أصل الصراط في كلام العرب الطريق ، قال عامر بن الطفيل

QURTUBI:1:6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r11.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI:1:6/r11.claim: Jarir also uses sirat to mean a road, supporting its ordinary Arabic sense.
QURTUBI:1:6/r11.anchor: وقال جرير : أمير المؤمنين على صراط

QURTUBI:1:6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r12.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI:1:6/r12.claim: Al-Naqqash says sirat is the Roman-language word for road.
QURTUBI:1:6/r12.anchor: حكى النقاش : الصراط الطريق بلغة الروم

QURTUBI:1:6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI:1:6/r13.claim: Ibn Atiyya judges al-Naqqash's claim that sirat is Roman to be very weak.
QURTUBI:1:6/r13.anchor: فقال ابن عطية : وهذا ضعيف جدا

QURTUBI:1:6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r14.claim: A reading with sin, sirat, relates to istirat, swallowing: the road is imagined to swallow its traveler.
QURTUBI:1:6/r14.anchor: وقرئ : السراط ( بالسين ) من الاستراط بمعنى الابتلاع

QURTUBI:1:6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r15.claim: Other pronunciations put the consonant between zay and sad or use pure zay; sin is original.
QURTUBI:1:6/r15.anchor: وقرئ بين الزاي والصاد . وقرئ بزاي خالصة والسين الأصل

QURTUBI:1:6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r16.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:1:6/r16.claim: Al-Farra reports pure zay as a dialect of Udra, Kalb, and Banu al-Qayn, who also pronounce asdaq as azdaq; al-Azd/al-Asd and lasiq/lasiq vary similarly.
QURTUBI:1:6/r16.anchor: حكى سلمة عن الفراء قال : الزراط بإخلاص الزاي لغة لعذرة وكلب وبني القين

QURTUBI:1:6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r17.claim: Sirat is the second object of guidance: the verb can take it with a preposition, as in 37:23, or without one here.
QURTUBI:1:6/r17.anchor: نصب على المفعول الثاني ؛ لأن الفعل من الهداية يتعدى إلى المفعول الثاني

QURTUBI:1:6/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r18.claim: Mustaqim describes a path without crookedness or deviation, as also stated in 6:153.
QURTUBI:1:6/r18.anchor: وهو الذي لا اعوجاج فيه ولا انحراف

QURTUBI:1:6/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:6/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:6/r19.claim: The underlying form is mustaqwim; its vowel moves to qaf and waw becomes ya because the preceding consonant has kasra.
QURTUBI:1:6/r19.anchor: وأصله مستقوم ، نقلت الحركة إلى القاف وانقلبت الواو ياء

RAZI:1:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r1.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
RAZI:1:1/r1.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI:1:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r1.claim: The verse asks for guidance, which can be attained by seeking knowledge through proof and argument or by purifying the inner self through spiritual discipline.
RAZI:1:6/r1.anchor: أنه عبارة عن طلب الهداية ،   ولتحصيل الهداية طريقان : أحدهما طلب المعرفة بالدليل والحجة

RAZI:1:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r2.claim: Rational proofs are limitless because every atom in the upper and lower worlds testifies to God’s divinity, might and majestic self-sufficiency; the cited verse says each thing has a sign of His oneness.
RAZI:1:6/r2.anchor: لا ذرة من ذرات العالم الأعلى والأسفل إلا وتلك الذرة شاهدة بكمال إلهيته

RAZI:1:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r3.claim: His proof starts from bodies equal in corporeal essence but different in color, place and condition; corporeality cannot explain this differentiation, so a specifying governor is required.
RAZI:1:6/r3.anchor: أن أجسام العالم متساوية في ماهية الجسمية ،   ومختلفة في الصفات ،   وهي الألوان والأمكنة والأحوال

RAZI:1:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r4.claim: If the specifying governor is a body, the same argument recurs; if not, the argument reaches its goal. If it acts by nature rather than knowledge and power, differentiation remains unexplained; a living, knowing, powerful agent is required.
RAZI:1:6/r4.anchor: ذلك المخصص إن كان جسما عاد الكلام فيه ،   وإن لم يكن جسما فهو المطلوب

RAZI:1:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r5.speaker: ضياء الدين عمر
RAZI:1:6/r5.claim: Razi’s father says every individual atom contains infinitely many proofs of divine power, wisdom and mercy: it could occupy infinitely many positions and bear alternate attributes, each possible state showing dependence on its wise, merciful Creator.
RAZI:1:6/r5.anchor: الشيخ الإمام الوالد ضياء الدين عمر رحمه الله يقول : أن لله تعالى في كل جوهر فرد أنواعا غير متناهية

RAZI:1:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r6.claim: Thus the rational route to guidance has no end; the alternative route is purification and spiritual discipline, an immense field with a distinct path for each traveler to God.
RAZI:1:6/r6.anchor: أما تحصيل الهداية بطريق الرياضة والتصفية فذلك بحر لا ساحل له

RAZI:1:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r7.claim: Razi says each traveler to God has a distinctive method and path, citing the Qur’anic statement that each has a direction toward which they turn.
RAZI:1:6/r7.anchor: كما قال : { ولكل وجهة هو موليها }

RAZI:1:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:1:6/r8.claim: The intellect cannot master these spiritual secrets or their beginnings; accomplished knowers perceive profound discussions and subtle mysteries that most people’s understanding cannot reach.
RAZI:1:6/r8.anchor: ولا وقوف للعقول على تلك الأسرار ،   ولا خبر عند الأفهام من مبادئ ميادين تلك الأنوار
